# SPECULATIVE PHILOSOPHY:

### Description of the Oil of the Sun.

After the gold has been reduced into a juice by means of vinegar, as was stated above, let it boil for fifteen days in the following digestion; afterward, let the volatile part be separated in a "Bain-marie" <note>original: "balneo Mariæ"; a water bath used for gentle, indirect heating</note>, and the pure, fixed oil of gold <note>original: "olei solis"; in alchemy, Sol (the Sun) represents Gold</note> will remain at the bottom.

### This is the body of the digestion.

Take one pound of the juice of celandine <term>chelidoniæ: Greater Celandine, a plant with yellow sap traditionally associated with the sun and used in alchemical preparations to "open" gold</term>, and an equal part (or a little more) of circulated water of life <term>aqua vitæ: "water of life," refers to distilled alcohol or spirit used as a powerful solvent</term>. Let them be resolved into a spirit, with which you should mix three ounces of gold; thereafter, proceed as was stated above.

### Conclusion of the philosophical key.

*Since the Key was previously delivered, I shall now feel no burden in handing over its use and its "chests" <note>original: "arcas"; refers to the secret vessels or hidden repositories of knowledge</note>—concerning the dissolution of these substances and the philosophical separation from their contents—to any diligent seekers of nature’s hidden cabinets. By this work, besides my other labors of whatever kind, and by a certain now supernatural craftsmanship that illuminates the said Key, I wish to prove that I have lived more for others than for myself until now. Indeed, the matter itself teaches this, and all who have seen me will testify to it. It would be just, therefore, for me to rest for a while, until at last another of our profession might come along to lighten the burden. Not that I am yielding, but rather I am breathing to regain my strength against those who attempt (though in vain) to defeat the truth of nature which Paracelsus <note>Philippus Aureolus Theophrastus Bombastus von Hohenheim (1493–1541), the Swiss physician and alchemist who pioneered the use of minerals in medicine</note> professes. Nor do I see much leisure for myself; for that "Great Duke" of his enemies is near. Therefore, we must rise up on both sides, for the weapons are clashing. Yet, with the pebble and the sling <note>a reference to the biblical David and Goliath</note> already prepared, I do not dread this giant, even if I seem a pygmy to him. For Truth arms her own against men who are liars, ambitious, and proud (those who hide under a cloak of eloquence because they would never dare to come forward naked with simple speech, lest the vice concealed in their "decorated tomb" should appear). In the power of Truth, therefore, I go to meet the Spirit. Farewell as best as you are able.*

# ON SUPERNATURAL CRAFTSMANSHIP.

It is fitting that we prove from the very beginning that our supernatural craftsmanship <note>original: "artificium supernaturale"</note> is a legitimate offspring, and that any other Chemical arts are adulterated. Modern Physicists and Metaphysicians stubbornly deny our "fifth essence" <term>quinta essentia: the "quintessence," a fifth element beyond earth, air, fire, and water, believed by alchemists to be the pure, incorruptible substance of the heavens</term>. This is the best argument for us against such people: that their own methods of teaching their opinions are worthless. What will those men judge the heavens to be? Will they dare to deny to us that the heaven is a "fifth thing," separated by God from the four elements as the pure is from the impure, or will they by this very act confess their ignorance? There is no doubt that they do not understand this secret <note>original: "arcanum"; a hidden or specialized mystery of nature</note>. If they were to admit to us that the heaven is indeed separated from the four primary essences, then it must be a fifth essence. Unless, perhaps, they were to say that the heaven is also composed of the four elements plus four pure essences, which would mean there are eight essences in total. 

By this very reasoning, they would be denying that a pure heaven exists, and they would say it is just like the lower elements. For in this context, "purity" is spoken of more in terms of a unified whole than of "sincerity" <note>original: "sinceritate"; in an alchemical context, this refers to being unmixed or in a state of natural simplicity</note>. If the four elements were in the heaven mixed together just as they are here below, they would appear mixed there just as they do here—which is not the case at all. Instead, the heaven appears as a single element, adorned with many celestial bodies—as many as are in the lower world—and these correspond to one another as effects correspond to their cause. 

This is the true separation of the elements, which it befits true Alchemists to imitate: namely, the separation of a purer substance from the impure elements, just as the superior is separated from the inferior. That common <note>original: "vulgaris"; referring to "vulgar" or everyday chemistry practiced by those without philosophical insight</note> separation, which is done by separating oils from waters, and these from their "earths," belongs to the qualities of a substance, not to its fundamental elements. For instance, if oil (which some call "air") is separated from its earth and water, nothing else will have been achieved except that the more viscous, fatty, or hot elements have been separated from their own qualities. For in any of these separated parts, every element is still present, no matter how it is separated. It is more sensible, therefore, to name them thus: namely, the "hot element," for the part in which [it is] more...

# ON SUPERNATURAL
# CRAFTSMANSHIP.

*It is fitting for us to prove from the start that our supernatural craftsmanship <term>artificium supernaturale: a term for alchemy that claims to work above the ordinary course of nature by using celestial influences</term> is a legitimate offspring, and that any other chemical arts are adulterated. Modern natural philosophers and metaphysicians <note>original: "Physici, Metaphysiciq;"; in the 16th/17th century, these were scholars of nature and the fundamental nature of reality, often tied to University Aristotelianism</note> stubbornly deny our "fifth essence" <term>quinta essentia: the quintessence, a pure, incorruptible substance that makes up the heavens, distinct from the four earthly elements of earth, water, air, and fire</term>. This is our best argument against such people: to show that the opinions they teach are worthless. What will those men judge the heavens to be? Will they dare to deny to us that there is a "fifth something," separated by God from the four elements as the pure is from the impure? Or will they, by this very fact, confess their ignorance? There is no doubt that they understand this secret <note>The author is likely being sarcastic here, implying that if they don't understand it, they are not true scholars</note>. If they admit to us that the heaven is also separated from the four primary essences, then it must follow that it is a fifth essence. Unless, perhaps, they were to say that the heaven is also made of the four elements and four pure essences, so that there would be eight essences in total.*

*By this very logic, they will deny that a pure heaven exists, and they will say it is just like the lower elements. For in this context, "purity" is spoken of in terms of union <note>original: "unione"; referring to a unified, simple, and indivisible state of matter</note> rather than merely by its clarity. If the four elements were in the heaven mixed just as they are here below, they would appear mixed there just as they do here—which is not the case at all. Instead, it appears to be a single, unique element, adorned with many celestial bodies—as many as there are in the lower world—and these correspond to one another, as effects correspond to their cause. This is the true separation of the elements, which it is fitting for true Alchemists to imitate: namely, the separation of a purer substance from the impure elements, like the higher from the lower.*

*That common separation, which is done with oils from waters and these from their earths, is a separation of qualities <note>physical traits like heat, moisture, or density</note>, not of the fundamental elements themselves. For example, if an oil (which some call "air") is separated from its earth and water, nothing else has been achieved except that the elements have been made more viscous, fatty, or hotter by the separation of their qualities. For every element is present within any of these parts, no matter how they are separated. It is therefore more sound to name them as follows: namely, the "hot element" for the part to which* <meta>catchword: magis (more)</meta>

->### PREFACE.<-

*...the heat of fire more closely adheres to it; moisture is more suited to water; cold to air; and dryness most of all to the dryness of earth. We shall also use these names below. But to return to the subject of heaven: the ancient Sages called that part the incorruptible part of the world and the "other, superior world." They affirmed it was separated by God from the other inferior part of the whole—namely, the inferior, corruptible world. They also most aptly called this universal essence the "fifth essence" <term>quinta essentia: the quintessence, a pure celestial substance distinct from the four earthly elements</term> and the "natural form." The inferior world, however, they called the matter of nature, which is also universal and capable of receiving all its various forms. Before these two parts were separated from their "whole" (which is called Chaos <note>original: "Chaos"; in alchemy, this refers to the primordial, unformed state of matter before the Creator or the Alchemist organizes it</note>), each contained the other in a confused state. They were joined such that even after separation, each part retained a bond of that first union and a sense of love within itself, each part desiring to be connected to the other daily. This affection and desire is the cause of all generation, and it is truly called "nature."*

*These are the principles of our Physics <note>original: "Physicæ"; meaning Natural Philosophy or the study of the physical world</note>, which I have treated more extensively in my preceding books. Now, however, let us see what the principles of our supernatural craftsmanship <term>artificium supernaturale: the alchemical process that works above the ordinary speed or power of nature</term> are, lest those who so sharply and wrongly attack it say that it lacks its own foundations. For this Art is properly nothing other than a craft consisting of natural principles that surpasses nature through skill. In this work, by some divine secret, it is necessary to use the same principles that nature herself uses, because we are unable to manufacture any other kind. But where nature has finished her Physics, we begin our Metaphysics <note>The author argues that alchemy begins where natural growth ends, taking "perfected" natural materials and elevating them further</note>: receiving those things which she has left for us and prepared as naturally finished and perfected, and then more than perfecting them by a certain supernatural craftsmanship.*

*And because we cannot handle the entirety of nature's great heaven with our hands, nor enclose all the elements within our instruments <note>original: "organis"; refers to laboratory tools like alembics and furnaces</note>, we are compelled—following the likeness and imitation of nature—to hunt for our own "heaven" from natural things. We do this through our mastery of separation, drawing it out from our own impure elements so that we may manufacture our own "Chaos." From this Chaos, we must begin this admirable work, which ought to surpass the mastery of nature herself. Now, unless I am mistaken, in-*

## CHAPTER I.
### On metaphysical separation performed by itself.

We have said previously in the Preface that heaven is the fifth element—not because there are five elements, but only four. The purer substance of these elements is supernaturally distinct from God and was brought back into a state of union in heaven; meanwhile, the impurer part remained below, arranged into four parts which constitute the lower and elemental world, while the other part constitutes the ethereal world. In no different a way, our metaphysical quintessence <term>essentia quinta: the "fifth essence," a refined, celestial substance thought to be hidden within all physical matter</term> is drawn by supernatural mastery from the impurer elements of things through separation. This separation is not of the kind imagined by many who deviate from the truth, who falsely believe that the four elements can be separated so that one is entirely free from the others. For if this were to happen, the machine of the world <note>original: "machina mundi" — a common Renaissance term for the structured universe as a complex, God-designed engine</note> would easily fall apart. To prevent this, the most high Creator of all things provided that these four parts be preserved under such a union that, although one can be distinguished from the others by its qualities, it nevertheless retains their essences within itself. He revealed this union to us more clearly in the heavens, in which no distinction of parts is visible; rather, He enclosed unity under the bond of a superior and inferior nature, which are one and the same nature.

Therefore, separation is twofold: one is of the elements, as the purer from the impurer; the other is of elemental qualities. This latter kind is the common <note>original: "vulgaris"</note> method, but the former is the metaphysical way. Nature, however, operates solely through commingling <note>original: "commixtionem"</note>, and this contains two operations: namely, Alteration and animation. We shall deal with each of these more extensively in what follows. For now, let us speak of the separation of the pure from the impure. In certain bodies, this occurs by itself, as in wine; in others, it occurs through a vehicle <term>vehiculum: a medium or carrier substance used to facilitate a chemical or spiritual process</term>, as in grains and seeds.

Although the quintessence lies hidden in all bodies produced by nature, it is found in none so abundantly as in wine, and it can be separated from no other thing so easily. For this reason, philosophers have preferred wine because of the ease of its separation, not because the quintessence is inherently better or more excellent in its own right than that drawn from any other body. For that celestial virtue is universal and equal in all things, and it is only different because of the diversity of the subject <note>in this context, "subject" means the physical matter or "host" containing the essence</note>, and only for as long as it remains within it; once it is free, it returns to its own unity. This is indeed one of the more hidden secrets of nature, through which philosophers have arrived at higher things. You shall therefore separate its spirit with its soul from any body, as follows.

-># THE ARTIFICE<-

I have judged it better to set this aside rather than repeat the same point for various different cases. But now, because certain bodies cannot easily be processed without a vehicle <note>original: "vehiculo" — a medium or carrier, like a solvent, used to transport or extract medicinal properties</note>, we shall also demonstrate this path through examples, from which you may be able to learn better than through rules alone, especially since we have made mention of **philosophic wine**.

Take grains of wheat, barley, or rye <note>original: "tritici, hordei, vel siliginis"</note>; after they have first been soaked in pure water so that they swell, let them be removed and piled into a heap on the ground so that, after several nights and days, they grow warm and germinate. Once this is observed, let them be spread out so they can be dried. Or, if necessity presses, let them be spread out in a wide basket woven of wicker, placed over a furnace that resembles an inverted chimney—that is, narrow at the bottom and wide at the top—and let them be dried by the smoke stirred up from below, until they appear toasted but not burnt, having a somewhat reddish color. Meanwhile, care must be taken that the basket does not catch fire, but is raised high enough away from the flame. This grain should be ground by a mill that is not too sharp, or broken in a coarse manner—not into flour, but into small fragments. 

Afterward, let it be placed in a wooden vessel, and let very hot water that has boiled for a long time be poured over it, and let the vessel be covered very well. After it has cooled and settled, the liquor should be drawn out through a hair-sieve or a sack, so that the fragments do not mix with it. Once you have separated this first water, pour on other boiling water as before and strain it. You should repeat this several times until you see that all the substance has passed from the grain into the waters; you will easily perceive this by the taste of both the liquor and the grain. 

Finally, take all the liquors and boil them in a pot <note>original: "cacabo" — a cooking pot or cauldron</note> for as long as it takes to reduce them to the thickness of yellow, skimmed honey. Then, you shall soon distill what has been placed in a vessel, and from that honey and **philosophic wine** you shall separate the soul with its spirit <term>anima cum spiritu: in alchemy, the "soul" is the fixed essence and the "spirit" is the volatile, active power</term>, and you shall sublimate it as many times as necessary until they are freed from all phlegm <term>phlegmate: the watery, tasteless, and inactive part of a substance left after distillation</term>. 

Whatever residue of the body remains settled at the bottom of the distilling vessel, you shall remove and dry in the shade or by the evaporation of its moisture. Finally, by a most violent fire, reduce it to very dry ashes, over which you shall pour boiling water, and let it boil for a very long time so that you may have from it a very sharp lye <note>original: "capitellum" — a caustic or alkaline solution extracted from ashes, used to produce salts</note>. This clear, floating liquid you shall separate from the ashes by tilting the vessel; pour water similar to the first over the ashes, boil it, and repeat what I have already said until no sharpness remains in the final lye, which you may then discard. 

Pass this and all the preceding liquids through a filter sleeve <note>original: "manicam filtream" — a conical cloth filter, often called a "Hippocrates' sleeve"</note> to obtain a most clear liquor, and let this evaporate in glass vessels so that you may have our **tartar** and the **natural salt** of all things. This can be resolved upon a marble stone in a cold, damp place into **tartaric water**, and so forth.

### *On the second separation.*
#### CHAPTER III.

After you have obtained the quintessence <note>original: "essentiam quintam" — the "fifth essence," the purest and most medicinal part of a substance, beyond the four elements</note> from the philosophic wine—or from common wine of any color, provided it is pure and very strong—and have rectified it perfectly as I have taught in my chemical books, you should reduce this juice to the highest state of simplicity through continuous motions of rotation <note>original: "rotationis motibus" — refers to "circulation," a process of continuous distillation and condensation in a sealed vessel</note>, as is described there. Once the circle of the wheel is completed, you will again see the pure separated from the impure, and the pure will float on top with the clearest color of the sky. Separate this from the impure by inclination <note>original: "inclinationem" — the process of carefully tilting a vessel to pour off the top liquid while leaving the sediment behind</note>, and preserve it. Thus far, you have seen a "naked heaven," which you may then adorn with "lower stars," just as the upper heaven is adorned with higher ones. Will the natural philosophers <note>original: "Physici"</note> who imitate the Greeks wonder now that we touch the heaven and the stars with our hands, or will they deny this as they do everything else? It matters little indeed what they do.

### *On the ornament of the metaphysical heaven.*
#### CHAPTER IV.

The "lower stars" are, for us, any individual things produced by nature in this lower world through the conjunction of the stars and heaven above with the lower elements. Even now, I hear the voices of those growling against us, saying: "Bah! Away with such men, who presume to be able to join heaven to earth." Let them shout until they are hoarse; they will be forced to hear even greater things. Heaven is celestial matter and universal form, containing within itself all distinct forms, which nonetheless proceed from a single universal form. Therefore, whoever understands how individual things can be reduced through the metaphysical art into the most general genus, and how afterward specific or multiple virtues can be fixed into it, will easily discover the universal medicine <note>original: "medicinam universalem" — the legendary Panacea or Philosopher's Stone, capable of curing all illness and perfecting matter</note>. This medicine will be able to remove all corruptions and diseases, whether specifically or universally. Since there is only one beginning for all corruption, there is likewise only one source of renewing or animating virtues. Who then, unless he is a philosopher deprived of his mind, could doubt this? Truly, because this has been described very clearly by many philosophers, I will not press the point of how it is done any further; I shall instead pass on to those things which were more obscurely set down by them, so that I may clarify them and advance this study. It benefits the reader nothing to treat the works of others with the same approach they used. Read, therefore, what they themselves have written on this matter, and compare it with these words, so that you may hold fast to what is useful.

Having previously discussed the "metaphysical heaven" as a purified essence, the author now defines "Chaos"—the raw, undifferentiated state of matter—and the role of the artisan in extracting the "Mercury" and "Form" necessary to create the perfect medicine or Philosopher’s Stone.</meta>

# THE CRAFT

...two of all the means. <note>original: "duo mediorum omnium" — this fragment likely concludes a sentence from the previous page concerning the relationship between extremes and the intermediate steps of the work.</note> **Chaos** is here properly called the confusion <note>In an alchemical context, "confusion" refers to a state where elements, forms, and matters are mixed together in an unrefined, "chaotic" state before separation.</note> of particular forms and their matters with the universal form and its own matter. This is considered in four ways: First, as the confusion of the human intellect among those who do not understand this art. Second, as the confusion of the parts that constitute this first extreme <note>The "first extreme" is the starting point of the alchemical process.</note>. Third, as the confusion in which the various intermediate stages <note>original: "media"</note> relate to their extremes and to each other—namely, one in potential to another, and indeed to all things, in any state or place, existing within them. Fourth, just as nature is the medium between the elements, the artisan in this craft is held to be the medium between Chaos, the operations, and the perfect and most perfect medicine. From these four, it can easily be understood that these medicines are brought from potentiality into reality by means of matter, form, heaven, and intermediate operations. For once motion is excited by the artisan, Chaos passes to the second extreme, which is the <term>perfect medicine</term> <note>Usually refers to the "White Stone" or silver-making tincture.</note>, and from that to the <term>most perfect medicine</term> <note>The "Red Stone" or gold-making tincture, the highest goal of the work.</note>, according to the order and disposition of the physicians. So that you may perceive the matter more sharply: our Chaos is a universal thing, enclosing within itself everything we work upon; from its "belly," the ingenious artisan must draw out the matter, its form, the heaven, and the elements, so that from these he may fashion the medicines mentioned above.

**Metaphysical matter** is called the first and universal matter, or the <term>Mercury</term> <note>original: "Mercurius" — in alchemy, this is the "Philosophical Mercury," the fluid, life-giving principle inherent in all matter, not common quicksilver.</note> moving toward growth <note>original: "vegetationem" — literally "vegetation," referring to the alchemical idea that metals "grow" in the earth or the flask.</note> and extracting the first matter of the form from the form itself. It is considered in three ways here: First, as a passive subject that undergoes motion under the artisan’s excitation through the required means; from the operations of all these, "heaven" arises from its own matter. Second, it is considered as any diseased body that receives the form of medicines, just as elementary things receive a vegetable form. Third, it is considered as the form or the matter of the form—the primary matter subject to the actions of "heaven"—for in another sense it holds the power of form, as will be explained more broadly later. For by this reasoning, the **heaven** <note>original: "caelum" — refers to the purified quintessence or the volatile, spiritualized part of the substance.</note>—which is the subject of the actions of these forms by which it is turned into a white or red <term>tincture</term> <note>The "tincture" is the concentrated essence that has the power to "stain" or transform other substances into gold or silver.</note>—can be said to have the nature of both matter and form, since by its action it moves the said form (or form-matter) toward the perfect or most perfect medicine, as will be clearer below. From this, you can gain the best knowledge of our Chaos: that one and the same substance, though by different reasonings, may behave passively toward one thing and actively toward the same thing, and vice versa. Hitherto, very few have possessed knowledge of this metaphysical matter, from which the metaphysical heaven arises. For one must account for the relationship between the simple and the compound—the latter being reduced to simplicity through alteration, mixing, etc.

The **Form** of things is the generative virtue by which any thing can produce its likeness; just as the form of a human lies hidden within a human, and not in another:

### ON THE SUPERNATURAL

...another: <note>original: "alio"</note> like a tree within a tree, or even a metal within a metal. Raw matter <note>original: "cruda"</note> must not enter the work, but must be cleared away through **sublimation** to the sides of the subliming vessel, so that it may be free from its own empty and superfluous earth. 

In this work, **Form** is considered in two ways. First, as the directing cause of the intermediate stages of this art through the intellect: under this governance, the **perfect and most perfect medicines** come to light. They are brought to motion by intellectual means, which are like sensory instruments through which the craft is led to perfection. The artisan of this work is said to have a similar form. From this, it is clear that these causative means have the greatest harmony with natural things. 

Alternatively, we consider **Form** as the agent acting upon the matter for the formation of perfection—either toward the **White** or toward the **Red**. <note>The "White" (Albedo) and "Red" (Rubedo) are the two highest stages of the Alchemical work, representing silver-making and gold-making power, respectively.</note> By its power, these medicines transmute any other external forms of lesser ability into something like themselves. However, neither of the two "forms" we have described can fulfill the Mastery <note>original: "magisterium" — the completion of the Philosopher's Stone</note> on their own; instead, they are like the **male**, from whom the seed is cast into the womb of our heaven.

**Heaven** is our **Mercury**, possessing a celestial color, which signifies that it is of a heavenly nature. For this reason, it is called "intellectual" because of its incorruptibility. In the same way that we say heaven itself "understands," so too does a man, who is both sensory and intellectual. Indeed, it possesses within itself the property of an incorruptible spirit, which is like a soul containing the conditions of a body: for it generates and produces seed from itself like a **female**. In this way, it differs from other things that enter into this Mastery. 

Because it is perceived by the senses, this Mercury is called "sensory." As a moving cause, it leads the potential within the form (or the form previously existing) into the **Red or White act**. It carries these forms in its womb no differently than a wife carries an infant conceived by her husband. From this, it can be gathered that our "heaven" acts upon the form, and the "heaven" hidden within these things leads them out from potentiality into manifest act. 

For within it lies the power of both generating and nourishing, just as in the <term>menstruum</term> <note>In alchemy, the "menstruum" or "menstrual blood" refers to a corrosive solvent or a nourishing fluid that dissolves the "seed" of the metal to allow it to grow.</note> of the male and female. For this reason, it is called "the menstruum" in this art, and is called "heaven" by reason of its motion. For no differently than the high heaven moves the universal form, the <term>prime matter</term>, the elements, and the species toward compound things and individuals, so too does **our heaven** move our forms toward the four elements, and from there to the **perfect and more-than-perfect medicine**. 

Sometimes it is called **blood**, because it is nutritive and causes the aforementioned forms to vegetate and grow until they reach their perfection—just as menstrual blood grows an embryo from a tiny seed into a great size. This is done while preserving the distinction of the parts through nourishment and the alteration of one medium into another, and of any quantity or form into another. These mediums and qualities exist in every alteration into forms from...

### THE ARTIFICE

...the male <note>original: "mas"</note> from the first diverse things, until some being arises, in a continuous quantity fused from various and discrete parts into a body living with soul and spirit. It happens no differently with the **metaphysical stone**, which is generated from a "heaven" possessing a vegetable <note>In alchemy, "vegetable" or "vegetative" refers to the power of growth and life-giving multiplication, rather than actual plants.</note> property. It pours the likeness of this property into the **perfect medicine and more**, just as a vegetative matrix <note>A "matrix" is a womb or source-structure.</note> pours into the son whom she conceives and bears; the fetus retains that property just like the parent. Likewise, the "perfect medicine and more" retains the property of its parents—namely, of heaven and of the elements—through which it pours the likeness of its own perfection (such as incorruptibility and temperance) into external substances and transmutes them into its own species. For this reason, it is called **Vegetable Mercury**, born from two substances, just as a woman conceiving the seed of a male possesses another form and a different virtue than she had before the beginning of conception.

In this art, the **elements** are considered to be the four appearing colors, and they are regarded in four other ways: First, just as they are drawn from "heaven" out of matter. Second, as the simple elements of heaven are separated from the thicker elements by the "circle of rotation" <note>This likely refers to the circular distillation or circulation of vapors in a vessel.</note>. In the third way, they exist naturally within the "forms" and are joined with heaven. Fourthly, indeed, they are considered as they are separated from the form and from heaven by the means of **alteration**, **mixture**, **dissolution**, and **generation**, through the mastery of separating their qualities; from these parts, only the airy portion is taken and made to overflow through the artifice of rotation, and thus it is mixed with the forms into heaven. It should also be noted that the elements can be drawn out from the forms through heaven before the conjunction, so that their **prime matter** <note>The "materia prima" is the original, formless substance from which all things are created.</note> or heaven may be held to approach more closely to the most general genus, and so forth.

**Dissolution** is the name given to the "knowledge," or the metaphysical intercourse of the male with the female, and of the female conceiving from the male that very thing which she ought to conceive. Let this be the beginning of the "particular generation": the effect of our metaphysical marriage which is perceived by the senses, and the union of the double nature into the embryo of the female.

**Alteration** is the conversion of one thing into another through likeness. This is considered in two ways, according to the double operation, insofar as it happens through itself. In the first way, it is considered as the forms are altered into heaven and heaven into the forms. In the latter way, let it be understood that the forms and heaven are so simply converted that they can be converted again into a third state—namely, into the **perfect medicine and more**.

These conversions or alterations are called "simple." Others are those which happen "by accident," such as when perfect medicines are made from imperfect things through **projection** <note>The final act of alchemy: casting a small amount of the Stone onto base metal to transmute it.</note>, alteration, or transmutation. **Mixture** occurs from two colors, namely pale and sky-blue, so that from them it may be known that the forms and heaven are mixed in the **Great Work** <note>original: "opere majore"</note> without anything else.

# ->SUPERNATURALE.<-

...otherwise, just as from the beginning of human generation nothing else is mixed with the man and woman or their seeds; and in this place, a **marriage** <note>original: "conjugium"</note> occurs between the **forms** and **heaven**. There also occurs another mixing, in which the air and fire of any of these, as well as the forms of heaven—through alteration, mixing, dissolution, generation, and the matter of heaven—are mixed with the forms, etc.

**Digestion** <note>In alchemy, digestion refers to the application of gentle, continuous heat to a substance, mimicking the warmth of a stomach or a womb to bring it to maturity.</note> is defined as the nourishing or warming <note>original: "fomentum"</note> of the conceived seed by the female, through which means the **perfect medicine** arises—and even something more than perfect. For it is necessary that the forms be digested in "heaven" for as long as it takes to reach that "prior medicine" which we mentioned above. Afterwards, when it seems right to the craftsman, he can proceed all the way to the second perfection. From this, best reader, you may gather that there is a twofold digestion: one by which a transition is made from the forms and heaven to the **perfect medicine**; the other by which one must pass from this medicine and heaven to the final **perfection**. For this reason, other necessary means are required, not unlike the previous ones—namely mixing, alteration, dissolution, generation, and operation—except that something more imperfect arises from the former than from the latter. And as soon as a **saffron color** <note>original: "croceus color"</note> appears through digestion, it denotes the **forms**; while **azure** <note>original: "azurinus"</note> denotes our **heaven**. Those colors that are intermediate between these represent the medium of conjunction between heaven and form, connecting that to the perfect medicine, or this to the most perfect.

**Generation** <note>The final stage where the "Stone" or "Medicine" is born and takes on its active properties.</note> in this context is considered in various ways (indeed, to provide its definition: it is the manifestation of hidden forms). First, as it is the stage generating the **perfect medicine** from heaven and forms. Second, as it generates the **most perfect medicine** from the perfect one and heaven. In another way, when it begins to pass from dissolution through alteration and digestion to the perfect medicine, it makes its limit there and reaches the end of the "lesser perfection"; or where, passing from here, it acquires the final stage of the "greater perfection." By this latter reasoning, the **mastery** <note>original: "magisterium"; the successful completion of the alchemical process.</note> of the greater perfection can easily be perceived, promoted more by nature than by artifice—nevertheless, it is excited by artifice in the lesser perfection, where art was more beneficial than nature. Indeed, in the later mastery, generation occurs in no other way than a fetus in the womb <note>original: "matrice"</note> or a bird in an egg. For this reason, it is also called the **Philosophers' Egg** <note>The "ovum philosophorum" was the sealed glass vessel where the alchemist watched the transformation of the matter, symbolizing a womb or the container of the universe.</note> in its own way. This artifice can be understood no less than that which results from the mixing of matter with forms to produce **precious stones**, such as rubies, sapphires, and **pearls** <note>original: "uniones" - large, singular pearls of great value.</note>, which are made in the womb of our "philosophical heaven" by means of generation, possessing the same virtues that natural stones have obtained from nature. It follows from this that this "heaven" is able to attract all the virtues existing in stones, by the virtue of unity, or its own simplicity, or (to speak better) by a **magnetic virtue**. In this way, the excellent craftsman can elicit celestial virtues from natural bodies...

For the **seed** <note>original: "sperma"</note> is diffused through the whole substance of our philosophical heaven. For after the appearance of that color, it is certain that our infant is completed in body and **vegetable power** <note>The "power of growth" or life-force.</note>. From which time the craftsman ought to know the number of days within which our stone was first led from the beginning of conception to the limit of the appearance of the red color; he must then apply double that time without intermission, but with a slightly more vigorous heat. When this is completed, that which was sought is acquired: namely, a **hard stone** enveloped in many superfluities, appearing just like a child appears after a woman gives birth. The means between the saffron and red colors are digestion, generation, and mixing, as perceived by the water, matter, form, and heaven. By the mixing of these, near their end, the intermediate stages of water, matter, and form appear, though without the form and heaven themselves. For if form and heaven were still present in that same way, some parts would not wish to be bound with others, nor be joined in the third number.

**Separation of virtues** is the extraction which occurs by the movement of fire in this particular mastery. # ### THE SUPERNATURAL.

By separating themselves from others through the medium, other things enter; and through that very operation of separation, the formal and also the material power is attracted from the forms and from **heaven** <note>original: "cælo"; in alchemy, the "heaven" refers to the most refined, volatile part of the substance or the upper part of the distilling vessel where vapors collect.</note> toward a lesser perfection, and from this toward a greater one. In this way, the form and the heaven—or that which is less perfect—change their simple forms into a greater or lesser perfection. While the less perfect thing exists in one form, the forms and the heaven through themselves exist in a greater and more perfect state under another form than they were when less perfect. These perfections retain their own specific powers existing under a "third form" within the transforming poison. If such an origin did not occur through the aforementioned separation, neither alteration, nor generation, nor progression would take place, and the work of nature in the **Philosopher’s Stone** <note>original: "lapide philosophico"</note> would be destroyed.

This medium is the evidence of the simple elements actually existing in our heaven, along with the natural elements existing in the forms; it shows that fire, air, water, and earth arise and are also separated from heaven into a mixture with the other things that have been mentioned. All of these stages are designated by **colors**.

**Potential** <note>original: "Potentia"</note> here is the same as alteration; by this degree, it is understood that all other degrees and any intermediates are present potentially in our **First Chaos** <note>original: "Chao primo"; the raw, undifferentiated starting material of the alchemical work.</note>; and secondly, in the elements potentially existing in our matter. Therefore, this "potential" is nothing other than the act of our heaven, which we treat more extensively in the **work of stone-making** <note>original: "opere lapidifico"</note>. Many know how to fashion stones, but they do not know how to apply natural virtues to them, because they are ignorant of our heaven—in which, from which, through which, and with which the fulfillment of the stones and the increase of their perfection consists.

**Operation** in this work refers to the excitation of the **four colors**, by which various modes of operations are designated. The **first color** denotes that heaven has its action and operation upon the forms, or upon the less perfect thing and the form. The **second color** indicates that external fire has an action upon the heaven, the forms, and the other elements, as well as the natural and actual intermediates, through movement toward a lesser and greater perfection. The **third color** shows that the forms (or the less perfect thing) possess their own action upon the heaven, informing it so that it may arrive at a lesser and greater perfection. The **fourth color** signifies the actions of the operations which the **Artist** <note>The alchemist/operator.</note> performs upon all those things mentioned above—specifically the administration of fire as a cause in the separation of heaven and the operation of the forms, etc. It also signifies the actions of the perfected things, both the lesser and the greater, upon external substances through **projection** <note>original: "projectionem"; the act of casting the finished Stone or elixir onto a base metal to transform it.</note>, according to their capabilities toward the **red** or the **white** <note>original: "rubeum vel ad album"; referring to the "Rubedo" (final perfection) and "Albedo" (purification) stages.</note> by which they have been informed. This medium denotes that the rite and method of fabrication is accomplished by fire, and by the mixing of matter with the forms and the **philosophical heaven**, along with the instruments suitable to the Art.

The **white stone** <note>original: "lapis albus"</note> is called "less perfect," being defined by only three colors, as is clear to the eye; for it is composed of them. These colors, brought into one, denote the perfection of the completed work—namely, of heaven, the elements, alteration, mixture, dissolution, generation, color, digestion, separation, operation, and fire. **Fermentation** <note>original: "Fermentatio"</note> is properly called in this context the multiplication of the lesser perfection and its advancement to the greater, through the media of mixing, dissolution, alteration, generation, colors, and digestion: by combining heaven and form, and leading the less perfect into mixture, and administering the regimen of fire for so long until it passes through all the aforementioned stages, reaching generation and colors of a greater perfection—far more powerful in quantity, quality, and virtue—attaining the red and the white, and the recovery of health for the human body. From these things, it is easily gathered that the less perfect passes into the greater by the aforementioned means and the actions of the operations of forms, heaven, the elements, fermentation, separation, operation, and fire through proper administration. Furthermore, the craftsman (whenever he wishes) ought to compose the less perfect only once, because it can be multiplied infinitely and led to a greater state, and thereafter from that into another infinitely, just as the human race continues its species; one always generating another until the end of the age. Something similar can be said of bread dough: for this produces another through successive fermentations. In this place, however, it must be noted that the less perfect can progress into the greater and the infinite by means of the **form** <note>The "form" refers to the essential nature or soul of the substance being transformed.</note> and **heaven** acting as ferments—a fact known to very few, even among the most excellent craftsmen.

The **greater perfection** <note>original: "Majus perfectum"</note> is the final perfection of the greater stone, which consists of and is composed of four colors: two of which expressly show (as seen in the colors green and red) that the four elements are within it with every perfection of virtue, and the conclusion of numbers into unity.

The other colors, truly, signify that heaven and form exist there with all perfection and the simplicity of unity, through the mastery of the four elements and the aforementioned media, etc.

From this final stage, it can be perceived that the greater perfection has the power of multiplying its species in a twofold way, and of generating its own kind and things similar to itself—namely, in virtue through the aforementioned operations, and...

<page-num>293</page-num>

->### SUPERNATURAL<-
<note>original: "SUPERNATURALE"</note>

...and in the transmutation of external substances. The Greater is far more perfect in its powers and operations, both in the transformation of metals and in the cure of infirmities considered desperate <note>Meaning "incurable" or "hopeless" by standard medical means.</note> by all; therefore, it is not undeservedly called the **Greater Perfect**.

Of all the grades and media <note>The "media" are the intermediate substances or stages in the alchemical process.</note>, some are **intellectual** <note>original: "intellectualia"; refers to concepts understood by the mind or reason rather than the physical senses.</note>, such as **Chaos**, power, operation, generation, and digestion. Others are **sensory** <note>original: "sensualia"; things perceived by the physical senses.</note>, such as wine and **prime matter**, body, form, elements, the less and greater perfect, colors, fermentation, and separation, because they are perceived by the senses, such as the eyes. Still others are partly sensory and partly intellectual, such as **heaven** and all the media and grades of the Lesser Work. Furthermore, each of the aforementioned grades or media retains its own property, differing according to its own reason: of these properties, some belong to nature, and others to the perfection of the art. Those retaining a property of nature are wine and any media of the Lesser Work, which have, as it were, a universal form and prime matter, by reason of the property mentioned before. From these two, all media and grades arise through the mediation of the **craftsman** <note>original: "artifice"; the alchemist.</note>, no differently than the elements and compounds arise from universal form and prime matter through the mediation of nature.

After discussing the grades and the Greater Media, it will be worth the effort to bring something to light concerning the lesser ones, and to produce their definitions from the **Lesser Work** <note>original: "opere minore"; the secondary or preliminary alchemical process.</note>; lest anything seem lacking for the practical understanding of those reading. Therefore, in this place, **form** is the same thing that we said it was in the Greater Work. But its use here is different, because it is prepared in formation: not toward the less or greater perfect, and it differs from the form of the **Stone**, because it receives its condition from form, heaven, elements, alteration, mixture, dissolution, generation, colors, digestion, fermentation, separation, and operation.

**Matter** in this work is considered in various ways: First, it is taken universally; second, for the **philosophical key** <note>original: "clave philosophorum"; the secret agent or solvent used to "unlock" the metals.</note>; third, for oil; fourth, for **sulfur**, by informing the sulfur through the informing oil—specifically in **inceration** <note>original: "inceratione"; the process of adding liquid to a dry substance until it reaches a wax-like consistency.</note>, by reason of which this Stone arises.

**Body** <note>original: "Corpus"</note> is taken here for the bodies of imperfect metals, from which the **sulfur of nature** arises, while this philosophical key is operating; and through the form of the oil of those informing it, the operation is arranged by the middle steps, such as solution and inceration, until the Stone which is sought is made.

The **philosophical key** in this place is considered no differently than **heaven** itself in the Greater Work; and through this must be performed **calcination** <note>The reduction of a metal to a powder by heat.</note>, dissolution, evacuation, multiplication, spirit, **overflowing quicksilver** <note>original: "argentum vivum exuberatum"; highly refined or "living" mercury.</note>, sulfur of nature, tincture, oil, and inceration, by means of sublimation and fire, until the said sulfur is brought to the effect of the Stone.

**Calcination** is considered in various ways. First, when it occurs through the **common Mercury** <note>original: "Mercurium vulgi"; standard quicksilver, as opposed to the "Philosophical Mercury."</note>, under which the **Sun** (Gold) and the **Moon** (Silver) <note>In alchemy, Sol and Luna always represent Gold and Silver.</note> are acted upon. Second, when a **very strong vinegar** is made, by which a **saffron** <note>original: "crocus"; here referring to a reddish-orange metallic powder or oxide, specifically of iron.</note> is drawn from **Mars** (Iron). Third, when **burnt copper** is made from **Venus** (Copper) by means of **sulfur** and **orpiment** <note>original: "auripigmentoque"; a yellow arsenic sulfide mineral used in alchemical reactions.</note>. Fourth indeed, when it is done by the **Key of the Philosophers**, and in this way all the bodies of the metals are prepared to enter into solution, evacuation, and the other operations mentioned previously.

**Dissolution** is the concealment of the previous manifest form of the aforementioned bodies; it does not happen through itself, but by the mediation of the said **Key**, which is very well suited to the bodies. We see this just as water is corrupted by fire through the medium of air, so that it is raised up into vapors. It differs from the **Greater Dissolution** in that in this [Lesser] process, only the forms and less perfect things are resolved, whereas in that one, any bodies of the metals are.

**Evacuation** is nothing other than the extraction of the hidden spirits from their bodies, so that they may be formed into another of the forms of the **informing oils**, and by this path, after fermentation and **waxing** <note>original: "incerationem"; the process of adding liquid to a dry substance to give it a wax-like consistency.</note>, they may pass into the **Stone**. That which is drawn from the aforementioned bodies by this operation is the matter from which our Stone must be led from potentiality into act by the means and operations that have been described.

**Multiplication** here is nothing other than the repetition and continuation of the evacuations. Through this operation, the **six bodies** <note>The "six bodies" usually refer to the metals other than Gold: Silver, Copper, Iron, Tin, Lead, and Mercury.</note> are provoked to nausea, and to vomiting the Stone from their very guts.

**Spirit** is the **quicksilver** <note>original: "argentum vivum"</note> drawn from the six bodies and existing in the waters of the evacuations.

**Exuberant quicksilver** is the spirit of the bodies already separated through a completed evacuation.

**Sulfur of nature** is the spirit of the bodies, exalted through **sublimation** into a most excellent **salt** of four colors: namely pale, green, black, and red. This last one [red] denotes fire, and through it the transition to the **Sulfur of Nature**, which arises from exuberant quicksilver; this indicates that it derives its origin from the spirit, and the spirit from the multiplication which proceeds from evacuation, and that from dissolution, and this from calcination, which indeed comes from all the bodies. This sulfur is the **son born from the imperfect** [metals], and is prepared to put on white or purple garments. The **son who is generated from the perfect** [metals] differs from this, through the oil in which the forms of the imperfect sons are contained: and because their sulfur becomes the Sulfur of Nature, as well as that of others whose sulfurs are dry and capable of receiving moisture.

**Tinctures** are the colors appearing in the work in different ways. First, green and saffron-yellow. Second, red and saffron-yellow, green and black.

The first colors denote the **tincture** itself, by which the sulfur of nature...

**Oil** <term>Oleum; a name for the fluid, concentrated essence or "soul" of a substance</term> is a form having a twofold color, namely green and saffron <note>original: "croceum"; a yellow-orange hue</note>, by which it is indicated that it is produced from perfect bodies through suitable means.

**Inceration** <term>Inceratio; the process of softening a substance to a wax-like consistency</term>, **fermentation**, or rather **information** <note>original: "informatio"; the act of giving "form" or character to a substance</term> is truly called the formation of the offspring of imperfect things so that they may receive the condition of the Stone.

**Sublimation** is called refinement <note>original: "subtiliatio"</note>, which occurs in two ways: namely into a very fine powder, and into a liquid. By this latter path, the spirits of the bodies, through an intermediate multiplication, are converted into **exuberated mercury** <term>argentum vivum exuberatum; quicksilver that has been "ennobled" or increased in potency through alchemical processing</term>; by the former path, however, they are turned into the **sulfur of nature**. By another reasoning, sublimation is also considered as the matter becomes closer to perfection—just as exuberated mercury is more perfect than a spirit, and as that sulfur of nature exists closer to the Stone.

The **Stone** is the end and the perfection of all imperfect bodies and operations, in which they rest as if in fire and like **salamanders** <note>The salamander was a mythical creature believed to live in and endure fire without being consumed; it represents the Stone's stability in high heat.</note>. This is a "third something" consisting of matter and form, above nature and yet by the mediation of nature, then forged by the industry of the artist.

The **Elements** are considered in two ways in this place: first as the fire acting from the outside; second as the agent from within, like that which is drawn from perfect bodies into the **oil**, and so forth.

# *On other differences of terms previously defined, and divisions necessary to know.*

## CHAPTER VI.

**Nature**, when corrupting any individual thing, first **putrefies** it, then separates the composite elements which are more immediate within it, afterward brings each of these to the highest simplicity, and finally to its own **prime matter** <term>materia prima; the original, formless substance from which all things are created</term>. Once this is finished, the **wheel of corruption** <note>original: "corruptionis rota"; the natural cycle of decay and breakdown</note> is complete, and from the prime matter the **wheel of generation** <note>original: "generationis rota"; the natural cycle of birth and new growth</note> takes its beginning, passing into the simple elements. Lastly, through the mixing of these, composite elements arise, from which an "elemented" subject is made, according to its own species and form, under which the elements are drawn into the composition of the individual. And the **metaphysical artist** <note>original: "artifex metaphysicus"; the alchemist who works with the hidden, spiritual, and structural forces of nature</note> must observe this process, so that where nature has ended, he himself, through the rotation of corruption...

# THE CRAFT

...refinement should begin with a backward step, namely from the end, tending through the middle toward the beginning of the **wheel of corruption** <note>The "wheel of corruption" refers to the first half of the alchemical cycle where the initial material is broken down and destroyed.</note>, applying those means which are **calcination** <term>Calcinatio; the process of reducing a solid to a fine powder through high heat</term>, **dissolution**, **putrefaction** <term>Putrefactio; a stage of decay where the matter turns black and "dies" before rebirth</term>, **division**, **purification**, and so on. Next, one must come to the **wheel of generation**, the means of which are **mixing**, **inceration** <term>Inceratio; the process of adding liquid to a dry substance until it reaches a wax-like consistency</term>, **decoction** <term>Decoctio; a concentrated "cooking" or boiling of the substance</term>, and so on; these are the most excellently arranged instruments of the **Stone**. When all these have been rightly performed, the artist <note>original: "artifex"; the alchemist performing the work</note> will possess what he desired.

The **Form** of this work is considered in a triple state. First, as it is the first cause. Second, as the artist. Third, as any other of the means.

**Matter** is also considered in just as many ways. First, as the subject from which our **Mercury** is drawn. Second, for the **elements**. Third, for the **sulfur of nature** <note>This refers to the internal "fire" or active principle within the matter, rather than common brimstone.</note>.

**Heaven** <note>original: "Cœlum"; in alchemy, this often refers to the volatile, spiritualized essence that rises to the top of the vessel.</note> also has a triple consideration here. First, as the greater heaven. Second, as **vegetable Mercury**. Third, as the **soul of metals**.

The **elements** are considered in two ways in this place. First, simply. Second, compositely.

**Power** or **alteration** differs in as many ways as there are different means.

**Mixing** has a fourfold meaning. First, of heaven with form. Second, of air with water. Third, of water with fire. Fourth, of air with water and heaven.

**Dissolution** has only one consideration, which is between heaven and forms.

**Generation** has a twofold meaning. First, by which the elements are generated. Second, insofar as the **Stone** is generated from those elements and heaven.

**Colors** also have a twofold [meaning]: the former in the evacuation of bodies and the rectification of elements; the latter in the generation of the Stone.

The **Less perfect** has only one [meaning], as is evident from the senses.

**Fermentation** is triple: the first from virtue <note>original: "virtute"; here meaning power or innate quality</note>, the second from quantity, the third from both together.

**Separation** also has a triple operation: the first is between the qualities of the elements; the second is the purification and fixation of them; and the third is of the **vegetable Mercury** and the dregs <note>original: "fæcum"; the solid waste or sediment left after distillation.</note>.

**Operation** has as many meanings as there exist means of this art.

The **Greater perfect** has a single [meaning] like the less, and it is obvious to the senses.

The principles and means of **philosophy** are in all the principles and means of this art, just like the **motion of the sphere** <note>original: "motus orbis"; referring to the cyclical rotation of the heavens or the circulation of vapors within the alchemical flask.</note>, which is to be considered as the form containing all natural instincts and appetites.

### SUPERNATURAL

The most subtle and powerful means in the work is the **repetition** of the **wheel of corruption** <term>Rota corruptionis; the stage of the alchemical process where the metal is broken down into its base components</term> of metals, which is performed as follows:

Once the **forms** have been placed in **heaven** <note>original: "cælum"; in alchemy, the "heaven" of the vessel is the upper part where vapors condense</note>, unburied, dissolved, and emptied through the practice of the "brief art" until one reaches the **Sulfur of Nature** <note>The internal, active "fire" or spiritual essence within the metal, not common brimstone</note> in the metals, then the wheel of corruption is finished.

The **repetition** <note>original: "reiteratio"; the process of repeating cycles of distillation or sublimation to increase potency</note> occurs when the **sublimated earth** is placed in heaven and is dissolved there by **putrefaction** and **division**. After the **air**, **fire**, and **water** have been evacuated, let the artist again reduce the earth to its purest **sublimation**. When this is finished, the **wheel of generation** should follow with its own principles and means, until it is led to the end. This operation is more subtle than others; although it is longer, it is nonetheless more perfect. By this path, that which is less perfect—the **unfermented stone**—is converted into that which is more perfect, the **fermented stone**, through the **separation** and **composition** of the elements, which exist as follows. Nature in no way permits the elements to be separated by themselves; for in that case, each would remain alone, having only a single quality, and would have no appetite for generation, which is against nature.

Indeed, the **separation of the elements** is the predominance and victory of one over and upon another, in a mixed rather than a divided way. For the color of **fire** is **red**; and because one must pass through the **sphere of air** before reaching the sphere of fire, a **citrine** <note>A lemon-yellow or pale orange color</note> color appears before the redness—clear and transparent. This results from the mixing of fire with air. Even before one reaches the sphere of air, it is necessary to make a passage through the **sphere of water**; for this reason, the color **white** appears, shining like water. But because the **earth** is the center and the beginning from which the ascent must be made, while the stone is still in its sphere, the color **black**—which is proper to the earth—appears in it.

Note, therefore, the separation and conjunction of these into one: namely, **fire**. Likewise, believe this: if the colors **red** or **white** (or any other color than those mentioned above) appear before the **black** color, the operation of the stone has been destroyed, because the sequence of the conjunctions has been ruined.

There is also a noted difference said to exist between the **elixir** and the **stone**, regarding the **raw** and the **cooked**. For the **elixir** is a medicine composed of air, water, and earth alone, directed toward the **white** <note>The "White Work" or Albedo, which creates silver</note>. If a body is dissolved in water and is **red**, it reflects the color of the most excellent **carbuncle** <note>A deep red gemstone, like a garnet or ruby</note> when it has been converted into a composite of the **soul of fire** and air, and into a composite of earth and fire. But if it is white, it will bring forth a **green** color mixed with blackness.

Various **errors of the artists** are also to be noted. The first and most powerful consists in this: they do not know how to **imitate nature**. The second is that they think the **end** of the stone is its **beginning**, and they believe themselves to have finished when they have scarcely begun—as in the false opinion of the **red triangle**. For the composition of the **Greater Stone** lasts **two years** for those who have never composed it before; but for the experienced, through the year...

...not continuously for three months. Now I see that we must come to the minor distinctions.

**Form** is twofold: namely, **simple** and **composite**. **Simple** is an absolute unity, the singularity of its thing consisting in itself and not with another. **Composite** is the union of its four primordial chambers <note>The four "chambers" refer to the four elements: earth, air, fire, and water</note>.

**Matter** is the four elements: either simply, as signified by the first form, or compositely, as denoted by the latter. The **vegetable menstruum** <term>Menstruum: A solvent used in alchemy to dissolve or extract the essence of a substance, usually derived from organic materials like wine or vinegar</term>, which is called **heaven** or the **philosophical key**, is one part resolving and the other part resolvable. The resolving part is a certain celestial thing, while the other is not, but is rather corporeal. The **celestial** is the **fifth essence** <note>original: "essentia quinta"; the most refined and spiritualized extract of a substance</note> of wine or of tartar, from whose nature its resolvable part is brought into action. In another way, it is defined thus: **Menstruum** is a perfectly rectified **burning water** <note>original: "ardens aqua"; high-proof distilled alcohol</note>, by whose virtue any bodies are dissolved, putrefied, and purified; their elements are separated, and they are exalted into a **miraculous salt** and earth by the virtue it possesses, which is highly attractive. Whoever thinks it is any other water is ignorant and foolish. The **resolvable menstruum** is a potential vapor existing in any metallic body, joining **sulfur** and **quicksilver**, without which it is by no means brought into action. Finally, it is defined thus: **Menstruum** is the medium joining imperfect and perfect metals into the **stone**. This resolving menstruum is hot up to the second point of the fourth degree; therefore, its virtue must be increased with hot vegetables up to the final point of that degree. These include: **wild celery**, **wolfsbane**, **oleander**, **marking nut**, **black pepper**, **pellitory**, **spurge**, etc., without which it does not dissolve except over a long period of time.

By the aforementioned operations in the dung, you will also be able to convert fire into the **soul of fire**, and form another triangle from heaven, dung, and fire. The wheel of corruption is not finished before this, the instruments of which are heaven, dung, the secret furnace, and the heat of the ashes, etc. Now it is proper to approach the **wheel of generation** as follows. # THE ARTIFICE

...of the **air**, you shall put this into digestion for fifteen days, then distill it through dung <note>original: "fimum"; horse dung was frequently used by alchemists as a natural, steady source of low-level heat for fermentation</note>. You shall repeat this digestion and distillation so many times until there remains at the bottom of the vessel a certain substance like a brilliant oil, a single compound made of air and fire, which is called **Slime** <note>original: "Limus"; in alchemy, this refers to the primordial "slime" or "mud" from which life or the philosopher's stone originates, a dense, vitalized matter</note>. By this same process you shall convert fire and earth into their own compound so that a double **quadrangle** <note>A square symbol or four-part arrangement representing the four elements or qualities</note> is formed: the first from fire, air, dung, and ashes, in the middle of which the compound of fire and air shall rejoice. The second from fire, dung, and also ashes, in the middle of which shall stand the compound of earth and fire. Now take a part of the compound of fire and air, to which you shall mix a sixth part of **heaven** <note>original: "caeli"; here referring to the purified solvent or "fifth essence"</note>, and place it into digestion for thirty days; thus you will have formed a **triangle** from heaven, the compound of fire and air, and dung, in the center of which is found this **greater perfection**, transforming into the **red** <note>original: "rubeum"; referring to Rubedo, the final, "red" stage of the alchemical Great Work signifying completion</note>, drawing its birth and origin from heaven, and from the compound of fire, air, and dung. When you have done this same thing with the compound of earth and fire, by joining to it one and a half parts of heaven, you will have a second triangle from heaven, the compound of earth and fire, and dung, in the center of which will stand the **lesser perfection**, transmuting into the **white** <note>original: "album"; referring to Albedo, the stage of purification and whitening that precedes the final red stage</note>, etc.

If, however, you do not wish to mix in heaven—to avoid such great labor—you shall **wax** <term>Ceration: The process of softening a hard substance until it has the consistency of wax, often by adding liquid drop by drop</term> the elements previously given until they flow like wax. Place this waxed material into digestion for ten days, and wax the extract again just as many times, injected drop by drop, until you perceive a settled liquification in it. Put this matter, very well sealed, into a philosophical vessel in a **secret furnace** for one hundred and fifty or more days, until you see the work completed from the signs described below. 

This process is the best in the "Greater Practice" <note>the full Alchemical work</note>, by the method of the "Lesser Work." Notice that the ceration with fire and air can be done separately before the ceration of those not yet reduced into one. Thus the **wheel of generation** is finished, through which the good artist, by the Lord's favor, acquires the desired result. From these two "slimes" various things can be done in the metaphysical work, according to its breadth, as first in the royal practice, and in the artifice of ceration of its own **foliated earth** <note>original: "terrae foliatae"; 'leaved earth' is a term for a purified, crystalline mineral state ready for the final stages of transmutation</note> or elements, by waxing first with air and fire, or with the said slimes made from air and fire: in which artifice the wheel of generation has its limit and end, the sign of which is a **red triangle** for us. 

The beginning of the work, therefore, is **corruption**, and **generation** is the end: by which operations one quality is corrupted, and another is introduced through generation—just as by corrupting water and generating earth, then hiding this and making air and fire manifest, until the lesser and greater perfections arise through their own means. These means are the heats of the dung, the ashes, and the secret furnace, by which water is converted into earth, and this into air and fire. Earth is therefore the medium between water, fire, and air; and the dung, ashes, and secret furnace exist as the medium through which...

# SUPERNATURALE

Fire and air are converted into the soul of fire and air. For this reason, fire and air are the medium between the earth itself, the soul of fire, and the soul of air. Then dung <note>original: "fimus"; horse dung was often used as a source of gentle, steady heat for fermentation or digestion</note>, ashes, the secret furnace, and heaven are the medium through which the soul of fire and the soul of air are converted into the compound of fire and air, and into the compound of earth and fire. By this reasoning, heaven is the medium between the soul of fire, the soul of air, the compound of air and fire, and the compound of fire and earth. Likewise, dung, ashes, and the secret furnace are the medium through which the compound of fire and air, as well as the compound of earth and fire, are joined to the elements. Similarly, the compound of fire and air and the compound of fire and earth are the medium between the soul of fire, the soul of air, the more and less perfect, and so forth.

## *On the specific practice of the stone from the minor work.*
### CHAPTER VIII.

Cast the metallic body into the philosophical key <note>original: "clavem philosophicam"; a secret solvent, often referred to as a "key" because it unlocks the "doors" of the metal to release its internal qualities</note> contained in its own vessel, and allow it to digest in the heat of the first degree or in dung for one week. But before it is cast into the key, it must be reduced to a calx <note>original: "calcem"; a powder produced by heating a metal to remove its moisture and reduce it to a brittle state</note>, so that the body may be better dissolved and evacuated by means of the key and the heat of the first degree from the triangle according to the natural order. Once the dissolution of the body is achieved, let the vessel be placed into distillation, already prompted by the said heat; it will lose the key and be reduced to earth. Allow this earth, having been very finely ground upon a marble stone, to resolve into water by itself. However, if the earth is too dry, let it be sprinkled with a small amount of the key, and after three days it will begin to resolve into a compound water containing the four elements.

Distill this water through a filter and repeat the solution of whatever remains of the earth in the filter, until a sufficient quantity of water seems to be present to you. By this operation, the triangle of evacuation shall have been completed, in the center of which is the earth, which must "drink" its own water, as follows: Place the filtered water into the heat of the first degree for digestion; it will cast out the key entirely and be converted into small stones, which, however, are not yet the elixir. By the aforesaid evacuation, another triangle is completed from the water, the heat of the first degree, and the key, in the center of which the said stones exist. Grind these very finely and place their powder into putrefaction <note>The stage of "blackening" (Nigredo) where the matter is broken down through decay to be reborn</note>; thus it will be converted into a metallic water or oil in which the elements are found. Divide their qualities as you have heard before.

Once these are divided, purify the earth, or return the most subtle part to it through the required sublimations. Finally, imbue it with its elements: first with the celestial water, then with the aerial, and lastly with the fiery, as is the requirement of the art. Let them be decocted into the perfection of which you have heard. According to this process, the extreme principles and the mediums of this art are applied to whatever metaphysical work <note>original: "opus metaphysicum"; here implying the spiritual or transformative alchemy that transcends mere chemistry</note> you desire.

### *Concerning the specific practice of the stone from the minor work.*

#### CHAPTER VIII.

Cast the metallic body into the <term>philosophical key</term><note>original: "clavem philosophicam"; a chemical solvent, often an acid or "mercury," capable of opening the "locks" of solid metal</note> contained in its own vessel, and allow it to digest in the heat of the first degree <note>the gentlest heat, roughly equivalent to the warmth of a human body or a sunny day</note> or in dung for one week. But before it is cast into the key, it must be reduced to a <term>calx</term><note>original: "calcem"; a fine powder produced by roasting a metal until it loses its cohesion</note>, so that the body may be better dissolved and evacuated by means of the key and the heat of the first degree from the triangle according to the natural order. 

Once the dissolution of the body is achieved, let the vessel be placed for distillation, excited by the heat already mentioned; it will lose the key and be reduced to earth. Allow this earth—once very well ground upon a marble stone—to be resolved into water by itself. However, if the earth should be too dry, let it be sprinkled with a little of the key; after three days, it will begin to be resolved into a composite water containing the four elements. Distill this water through a filter and repeat the solution of that earth which remained in the filter until a good quantity of water seems present to you. By this operation, the "triangle of evacuation" shall be completed, in the center of which is the earth, which must drink up its own water as follows:

Place the filtered water into the heat of the first degree to digest, and it will cast out the key entirely and be converted into little stones. These, however, are not yet the <term>elixir</term><note>the perfected medicine or substance capable of transmutation</note>. Through the aforementioned evacuation, another triangle is completed from the water, the heat of the first degree, and the key, in the center of which the said stones exist. Grind these very finely and put their powder into <term>putrefaction</term><note>original: "putrefactionem"; the stage of the work where the matter "dies," turns black, and decomposes before being reborn</note>; thus it will be converted into a metallic water or oil in which the elements are present. Divide their qualities as you have heard. 

Once these are divided, purify the earth—or return the finest part by the due <term>sublimations</term><note>original: "sublimationibus"; the process of heating a substance until it becomes a vapor and then collects as a solid higher up in the vessel</note>—and finally soak it with its own elements: first the celestial, then the aerial water, and finally the fiery, according to the rules of the art. Let them be cooked down <note>original: "decoquantur"</note> into the perfection which you have heard. According to this process, the extreme and middle principles of this art are applied to whatever metaphysical work you desire.
