### *On the coherence of the metaphysical operations of both practices.*

## CHAPTER IX.

The instruments of these works—namely the intellectual means and the sensory ones—hold together in a wonderful manner. The "form" <note>original: "forma"; in a philosophical sense, this refers to the essential nature or "blueprint" of a thing</note> that represents the person of the craftsman acts as an existing instrument, through which nature generates our particular egg <note>original: "ovum"; a common alchemical term for the vessel or the sealed matter undergoing transformation</note> from the intellect. Although this must be distinguished from our form which we otherwise call "heaven," <note>original: "caelum"; here referring not to the sky, but to the refined, volatile spirit or the internal "atmosphere" of the alchemical vessel</note> nevertheless, the one cannot persist without the other in our craft, nor vice versa. For our form, "heaven," is the principle and the sensory medium that generates, nourishes, and causes growth or vegetation; it moves the elements toward a specific generation just as the greater heaven moves the lower things in the world. From this forming power—which it acquires through the vegetable form <note>the life-force within minerals and plants</note> and holds bound to itself by an indissoluble knot—it causes the sought-after particularity to multiply within external substances. This is true of many other hidden things in the process of the art, which are possible for the craftsman to know and achieve.

Truly, the form which is the intellect of man is the beginning, the middle, and the end in these preparations. It is denoted by a **saffron color**, <note>original: "croceo colore"; a deep yellow or orange-gold often associated with the sun, the soul, or the final stages of the work</note> which indicates that man is the greater and principal form in this metaphysical work, more powerful than the form of "heaven." Other forms are lesser than these, existing in states of greater or lesser perfection. The equalized mixing of **saffron** with **green** <note>green often represents "raw" nature or the "Green Lion" of early transmutation</note> signifies that among all these forms, there must be a necessary harmony; there is a hierarchy of "greater" and "lesser" without any conflict, leading toward the equality of the ultimate goal. For one of these three forms cannot be absent without everything failing at once. If "heaven" were lacking, the generation of the elements would fail, and a deprivation of both greater and lesser perfection would follow. Therefore, the intellective form must be joined with the vegetable form and the form of motion through the intellect, so that each one is conditioned by the other; and so on through the remaining steps and means until the highest perfection is reached.

The form called "motive" <note>original: "motiva"; the force that drives change or chemical reaction</note> is a certain universal principle in the steps of this art, moving each stage to the next, all the way to the end. Thus, the form of motion can be said to excite all the steps in order until perfection is attained. Form and matter are substantial principles, far greater than "accidental" ones; for accidents are merely the changes seen during the work, such as colors, alteration, digestion, and so on. The truth of this matter is demonstrated by the degree of perfection and the immensity of their transmuting power, rather than by these accidental steps. Nevertheless, the principles, the means, and the end are said to be equal because of the similarity of that same goal, toward which all things tend through a **wonderful chain**. <note>original: "catenam admirabilem"; likely a reference to the "Golden Chain of Homer," representing the interconnectedness of all levels of reality from God down to matter</note>

->THE ARTIFICE<-

With two ounces of the said form, or two and a half, according to the aforementioned condition, and with only one drachma of the <term>minor perfect<note>original: "perfecti minoris"; likely referring to the White Elixir or a less concentrated form of the stone.</note></term>, you will soak it. By the same operations as before, within the space of thirty days, you will be able to convert it into the <term>greater perfect<note>original: "majus perfectum"; the Red Elixir or the completed Philosopher's Stone.</note></term> using a tempered fire and a <term>regimen of colors<note>original: "regimine colorum"; the sequence of color changes—such as black, white, yellow, and red—that alchemists used to track the progress of their chemical reactions.</note></term> according to more or less intensity, etc., until you see a round and red body—if the work was for the red. But if it was for the white, it will appear with a metallic whiteness. It must be noted, therefore, that the colors of these "infants" are various: for the male and the greater perfect, it is red; for the female and the minor perfect, it is white. The colors appear: first, green mixed with redness; second, saffron also mixed with a brilliant redness, which denotes the conjunction of the parts with their whole; third, a white and brilliant color, which is the sign of the completion of the infant’s body; and fourth, a snowy white mixed with a metallic color, and this denotes the entry of the soul into its body. Tinged with this color, the infant is born from the mother's womb, a single weight of which, projected upon three thousand parts of matter, can multiply its own kind; and upon the third repetition, it can be multiplied over three hundred thousand. Of this, as with the prior greater perfect, multiplication can also be performed. It must be noted that in this <term>chemico-metaphysical<note>original: "metaphysice chemico"; the author views alchemy as both a physical science and a philosophical or "metaphysical" pursuit.</note></term> work, a certain or determined space of time cannot be assigned. For sometimes our "infant" is born more quickly—namely, when the heat happens to be stronger than required—and sometimes more slowly due to the lessening of the same, just as is seen in a human fetus.

The colors are the best indicators of this artifice, by which it must be guided. Thus, when the metaphysical infant is in dissolution and entirely liquefied, a black color begins to arise; by this, you shall judge it to be in the state of mixture and to have passed through alteration. And after the saffron color appears, you shall consider the body to be formed and complete in its limbs. But when the final color appears—namely, red—know that the body is joined with the soul. Once this is perceived, the fire must be continued, as was said above, right until the birth. Just as has been said here regarding the colors of the "red infant," it should be understood no differently for the colors of the "white infant," according to its own qualities. By these signs, the craftsman may approach the metaphysical work without fear and complete it happily—provided, however, that God grants His favor, and not otherwise.

Once this is perceived, place it over ashes to be **sublimated** <note>Sublimation is a process where a solid is heated until it becomes a vapor and then collects again as a solid on the cooler upper parts of a vessel, used here to purify the substance.</note> in a vial, first with a moderate fire, and finally with the heat increased little by little and successively until the whole [matter] ascends to the sides of the vessel, and the matter is **exalted** <note>In alchemy, to "exalt" a substance is to raise its purity or medicinal potency.</note> into an **admirable salt**, which the philosophers call "the stone" and "the sulfur of nature." This must be **incerated** <note>original: "incerandum"; from the Latin word for wax (*cera*), this is the process of softening a dry substance by adding liquid until it flows like wax when heated.</note> with the **oil of the perfect [metals]** <note>The "perfect" metals refer to gold and silver, which alchemists believed were the most refined forms of matter.</note> until it flows very easily like wax. Then, and only then, will you have a perfect medicine: one part of which by weight, if placed over one hundred weights of **tin** <note>original: "stanni," traditionally associated with the planet **Jupiter**.</note> (if the salt came from Jupiter), or over fifty weights of **lead** <note>original: "plumbi," associated with the planet **Saturn**.</note> (if it was from Saturn), will result in a most perfect work, more perfect than anything found in nature.

For the **oil of the perfect ones** has a **fixing** <note>A "fixing" agent is a substance that prevents volatile materials from evaporating, making them stable under heat.</note> power over all things, when such things as we have mentioned are drawn from the imperfect metals. Finally, take one ounce of the **perfect [metals]** in the form of filings or leaves, and **calcine** <note>To reduce a metal to a powder by intense heat.</note> them as you know how, according to what we spoke of plainly above. From these, you shall extract their own humidity—that is, their **mercury** <note>original: "argentum vivum"; literally "living silver." In this context, it refers to the "spirit" or liquid essence of the metal.</note>—using the **key** <term>clavis</term> <note>A "key" in alchemy is a specific chemical solvent used to "open" or dissolve a substance.</note> by way of the **philosophical juice**, just as was narrated before. Once this artifice of liquefaction or evacuation is completed, the vessel in which all the liquefactions took place should be placed in a **bath** <note>original: "balneum"; a water bath or bain-marie, used for steady, gentle heating.</note>, covered with its **alembic** <note>The cap of a distillation apparatus that collects and cools vapors.</note>. From it, all the moisture should be distilled so that a viscous matter remains at the bottom of the **cucurbit** <note>The gourd-shaped base of a distillation apparatus.</note>, as thick as liquid and skimmed honey.

When the vessel has cooled, pour on enough of the **philosophical key** <term>clavis philosophicæ</term> over this liquid matter so that it stands four fingers deep above it, and place it for **digestion** <note>A slow heating process meant to mature a substance.</note> in a heat source of dung or a water bath for one whole day (a "natural day" of 24 hours). After the vessel has cooled, pour the material dissolved by this artifice of liquefaction into another vessel by tilting it gently. Afterward, place the vessel covered with its alembic back in the bath and dry the matter with a slow fire. Over this, make the water and a fresh "key" swim four fingers deep again, as before. Finally, expose it to the aforementioned digestion for a similar day, and once the digestion is done, pour out the dissolved portion. You will repeat these operations until the entire matter is converted into clear water. 

Next, you will place this water in digestion for eight days, from which you will afterward extract the qualities of the elements as follows. First, by the sweetest heat of the water bath, you should receive only as much of the water as can ascend at that temperature. When this distillation stops and the vessel cools, pour the entire distilled liquid back onto its **dregs** <note>original: "fæces"; the solid residue remaining after distillation.</note>. Place this same vessel, properly sealed, back into the digestion of the dung or water bath. Afterward, using ashes and a fire built in a **furnace governed by registers** <note>original: "furno registris"; a furnace equipped with dampers or "registers" to precisely control the airflow and heat.</note>, distill all the **oil** that can ascend at that temperature. Distill this distillate again using the heat of the water bath: that which ascends, some call **Water**; that which remains at the bottom, they call **Air**.

...as has been said. From this, another mixture can be made, namely of the "heaven" with the philosophical key, by the said artifice of generation. Afterward, let the "less-than-perfect" mentioned above be added according to the proportion of the greater work; by this path, one passes to the "greater perfect," which can multiply its own likeness in external substances by ten thousand times <note>original: "bis quinque numero millibus"; literally "twice five in number of thousands."</note>, etc.

### *Another method of practicing.* ###

Whatever of those things mentioned are put into the mixture of the "heaven"—with the "heaven" of red or white wine, or of tartar drawn through the mastery <note>original: "magisterium"; a technical term for a high-level alchemical process or the resulting potent substance.</note> of the separation of qualities from the elements—and with the "form" or "forms" placed according to the doctrine of the greater work, let it be cooked in the continuous heat of a bath <note>A *balneum* or water bath, used for gentle, even heating.</note> without interruption for several days, with the vessel sealed so that the "heaven" does not fly away. Afterward, with the vessel opened, let there be added a portion of the "air" of any of those things mentioned, as the second part of the "heaven," and let it be cooked for as many days as before. When these things are finished, the vessel being opened again, you shall add as much of the "heaven of fire" of any of those things as there was of the "heaven of wine." With the vessel sealed again, let it be cooked with continuous heat for another fifteen days. When the artifice of mixing is complete, you will see the mixed things transformed into the "less-than-perfect" by means of the colors <note>The alchemist watched for a specific sequence of colors (usually black, white, yellow, and red) to gauge the progress of the work.</note>, according to which the craftsman ought to govern the work, until he reaches the most perfect "greater work" which is able to transmute its own species in external substances and multiply it by three thousand times its own weight, etc.

...color, weight, quality, and quantity, not unlike the <term>Mercury</term> <note>Mercury, or quicksilver, was considered by alchemists to be one of the three primary principles of all matter.</note> of the common people. Thinking they had found the greatest secret, they sublimated it with corrosive substances and corrupted its very nature. As a result, they failed to achieve the goal they envisioned, because they were ignorant of the principles, the means, and the ends of this art, through which our <term>metaphysical work</term> <note>original: "opus metaphysicum"; referring to the "Great Work" of alchemy which transcends mere physical chemistry to reach a spiritual or "trans-physical" result.</note> is completed. 

But if you take <term>our Mercury</term> converted into such a form, or even common mercury, and reduce it into water without any material additive—which can be done with the "phlegm" <note>In alchemy, "phlegm" refers to a watery, tasteless distillate that lacks active properties.</note> of the medium, if you provide its "air" to it beneath the vessel—and distill it seven times, you will possess the "light of pearls." Therefore, one must be cautious in our transmutatory art regarding such an extraction of Mercury from individual substances.

In certain individual substances, <term>our Mercury</term> possesses a somewhat free action, as is seen in <term>tartar</term> <note>Tartar is the potassium bitartrate sediment found in wine casks, highly valued as a purifying salt.</note>. This is evident from the operations of goldsmiths: when there is a trace of <term>the Moon</term> (silver) within <term>Venus</term> (copper), and this is placed in white wine or its "soul" (spirit), the power of our Mercury will bring the "tincture" of the Moon to the surface. By this, the bond of its harmony with the <term>Moon</term> is revealed. Even better, when you extinguish glowing <term>Venus</term> (copper) in tartar dissolved by white wine, it will take on a whiteness; however, this color is not permanent, because it lacks a fixed spiritual subject. Another experiment is performed where <term>Mars</term> (iron) is frequently extinguished in the aforementioned solution; it then takes on the softness of the <term>Sun</term> (gold) and the <term>Moon</term> (silver).

For <term>Mars</term> (iron) is dry and very far removed from Mercury—more so than any other bodies—and all dryness has the quality of a vacuum. For this reason, <term>our Mercury</term>, which is supremely moist, is easily received into it, whereby the iron is led into the aforementioned softness.

The "form" of our heaven <note>The "heaven" (cælum) refers to the quintessence or the most highly rectified spirit of a substance.</note> is another individual substance in which two free operations are perceived. The first is that by which it truly converts everything placed upon it into the very species of the form itself. This is an evident sign of an admirable "vegetative power" <note>In this context, "vegetative" refers to the power of growth and multiplication, like a seed.</note>, by reason of which substances are transmuted into other forms. Let the craftsman therefore consider what he might be able to achieve when <term>our Mercury</term> is stripped of its own form and shaped by another. 

There is also another equally evident operation: when the bodies of "perfect metals" <note>Gold and silver.</note> are ground with that form upon a porphyry stone, both will be reduced to the form of an <term>amalgamation</term>. From this, the Mercury can be extracted through a cloth, because the Mercury existing within the <term>Sun</term> (gold) and <term>Moon</term> (silver) moves toward the Mercury contained in that "form," and vice versa. Therefore, they are gathered in an "angle of harmony" so that in our "heaven," the perfect bodies may be multiplied; their Mercury can in no way resist being reduced into the appearance of an amalgam through this natural bond. # THE ART #

...we leave aside for the sake of avoidance <note>original: "vitaris causa"; likely referring to avoiding error or long-windedness</note>, because the things already said are sufficient for understanding them. The goal of this entire mastery is this: that our Mercury be placed in the celestial sphere; otherwise, the craftsman will work in vain. It seems marvelous that our <term>Mercury</term> <note>In alchemy, "Mercury" is not just the liquid metal (quicksilver), but a spiritual principle of fluidity and transformation.</note>, situated in a super-celestial place, does not retain its color, weight, quantity, and quality, even though all these belong to its nature. But the reason for this is that it is placed under a different form than when it lay hidden within an individual substance. This is also the method for extracting Mercury in this art: namely, that the best white or red wine be put into a separator, and from it <term>burning water</term> <note>original: "ardens aqua"; an early term for distilled alcohol or brandy.</note> is distilled, as is customary. Afterward, let it be rectified to a greater subtlety four times—though three times would suffice—lest the burning spirit exhale. Therefore, those who rectify it seven times have erred. Let this be the sign of its <term>rectification</term> <note>The process of refining a liquid by repeated distillation.</note>: when sugar is added, it is burned away entirely along with the water, leaving nothing behind. This matter is the subject from which the <term>fifth essence</term> <note>original: "essentia quinta" or Quintessence; the purest, most concentrated medicinal or spiritual force in a substance.</note> is drawn through the vessel called the <term>pelican</term> <note>A specialized alchemical flask with two side-arms that cycle distillate back into the main body, allowing for continuous "circulation."</note>. By this operation, it will happen that the upper part, or the fifth essence, is separated from the lower part—that is, from the turbid dregs—along a diametrical line.

Mercury can also be extracted from <term>tartar</term> <note>Potassium bitartrate, a salty crust found in wine barrels.</note> by calcining it in a glassmaker’s furnace for three natural days; but a large quantity of it should be used, for it is greatly diminished. Grind this burnt material upon a marble stone and leave it in a very cold and damp place until it dissolves into water. This must be distilled through a filter-sleeve and received in a glass vessel. You will be able to extract Mercury from it in two ways: the first as we described above regarding wine; the second through the art of separating the qualities from the elements, etc.

->*Concerning certain annotations on those things which have been said previously.*<-

### CHAPTER XIV.

The spirits of imperfect bodies are evacuated, or their <term>exuberated</term> <note>original: "exuberatum"; meaning mercury that has been brought to its full potential or "overflowing" state.</note> quicksilver is the primary matter born fit for receiving any form. But there is a difference between these spirits and others evacuated from perfect bodies: for the latter exist formally, while the former exist materially. Likewise, imperfect bodies can be converted into oil just as the perfect ones can; this is how the preparation of form and matter occurs. Indeed, the <term>sulfur of nature</term> <note>In alchemy, Sulfur represents the principle of combustibility, heat, and "soul," which acts upon the Mercury.</note> of the perfect bodies must necessarily be converted into oil, but not that of others, because they ought to be informed by the oil of the perfect bodies—unless, however, you wish to reduce everything to oil so that the work might be made more luminous. A similar oil is made through the separation of the qualities of the four elements, etc.

<term>Saturn</term> and <term>Jupiter</term> <note>The alchemical names for lead and tin, respectively.</note> are of one and the same nature when they are reduced into spirit. Therefore, into spirit, the exuberated quicksilver...

...spirit, the **sulphur of nature**, the **tincture**, the **oil**, and the **stone** have been reduced to a similar state, with these principles existing within each of those substances in infinite number. Likewise, while these and all other things retain their ancient being, they possess one nature that is individualized, and another nature in their simple virtue which is multiplied by way of generation and procession into spirit, the sulphur of nature, the tincture, and the oil. This can be said more properly of the **stone** than of the others, because the substance is multiplied from their unities, which indeed possess a single virtue derived from all of them. Since it possesses an ultimate unity in any of the metals which it did not have before it was converted into the stone, this unity is extended by the multiplication of external principles, so that in the said substances there occurs an increase of their form and a multiplication of their virtues. Thus ends the doctrine of the <term>lesser work</term> <note>original: "operis minoris"; the initial stages of alchemy focused on purification or the creation of the "White Stone" for silver, as opposed to the "Great Work" for gold.</note>.

**Calcination** <note>Heating a substance to high temperatures to reduce it to powder.</note>, **dissolution**, **evacuation**, **multiplication**, **spirit**, the **alembic** <note>A vessel used for distillation.</note>, exuberant <term>quicksilver</term> <note>original: "argentum vivum"; mercury.</note>, the **sulphur of nature**, **tincture**, **oil**, **inceration** <note>The process of softening a substance to a wax-like consistency.</note>, **sublimation**, and the **stone** have one condition in **Saturn** <note>Lead</note>, another in **Mars** <note>Iron</note>, and another in **Venus** <note>Copper</note>, and so with the rest. Likewise, Saturn has one condition in each of these, another with **Jupiter** <note>Tin</note>, another with Mars, another with the **Sun** <note>Gold</note>, another with Venus, and another with the **Moon** <note>Silver</note>. Similarly, Jupiter has a uniquely different condition when mixed with each of the aforementioned. A different condition also arises by mixing Saturn and Jupiter with Mars and Venus; or by mixing Jupiter or Saturn with either one of those; or Venus and Jupiter with Saturn, or with Mars itself. By this reasoning, the conditions of the metals can be multiplied by mixing one or more with another. In as many ways as the mixture is made, the condition of the **Stone** will be varied accordingly.

Furthermore, **Calcination** is equal to **Solution**, and **Dissolution** to **Evacuation**; this is equal to **Multiplication**, which relates to **Spirit**, and so forth, for the constitution of the subject, which is the stone. Likewise, the **Alembic** communicates itself equally to all according to its function.

The **sulphur of nature** is greater than the **exuberant quicksilver**, and that is greater than the **spirit**. The **lesser work** can by no means be accomplished without the sulphur of nature drawn from imperfect things, because the medium that <note>original: "sapiens"; literally "tasting of" or "knowing."</note> shares their nature would be lacking; in its absence, the "perfect" things (gold and silver) could not transmute the "imperfect" ones into their own species. For this is what the definition of a "medium" requires: namely, that the stone be composed of the sulphur of nature and the quicksilver exuberant from the imperfect things, together with the oil of the perfect things. Thus, the stone is a medium participating in both natures. By reason of the harmony it has with the said imperfect things, these give way to it through all their parts, so that in their smallest part there is the smallest part of the stone; it penetrates all these parts existing within them by reason of its subtlety. And because the matter of the stone, which is drawn from...

->### THE ARTIFICE ###<-

...[of] imperfect [things], it is formed through all its parts and bound to a certain external form by an indissoluble bond and a <term>vegetable property</term> <note>In alchemy, "vegetable" often refers to the power of growth, life, or transition, rather than literal plants.</note>, which it receives from the **philosophical key**. It is so shaped by that form that in its smallest part there truly and verily exists a tiny portion of that same form. In this way, they cast off their old, imperfect forms which were actively within them, so that they may receive the forms of perfect things which are in them potentially, and be transmuted into perfect metallic bodies. The method of working has been stated before, using the **sulfur of nature** extracted from <term>Saturn</term> <note>Lead</note> or <term>Jupiter</term> <note>Tin</note> alone; but now we say a mixture can be made with two, three, four, or all of them, according to the will of the operator, as the craftsman desires the condition of the stone to be. There is also established a method of eliciting **oil** from perfect things, which is one and the same as all the others: through **calcination** <note>Reducing a metal to powder through heat.</note>, **dissolution**, **evacuation**, **multiplication**, **spirit**, the **alembic**, **exuberant quicksilver**, the **sulfur of nature**, **tincture**, **oil**, **inceration**, **sublimation**, and through fire. When you wish to join two, place them into calcination with our **philosophical key** mediating; afterwards into dissolution, and into the rest of the aforementioned steps, up to and including sublimation. If they have become perfect and turned into the **sulfur of nature**, place them into multiplication, and if it remains too hard, pour on a portion of <term>menstrual blood</term> <note>A common alchemical metaphor for a solvent, often a red-tinted mercurial liquid, not literal blood.</note> so that it may be converted into oil.

Note that the elements of metals drawn from them by **vegetable Mercury** are called their **first matter** <note>original: "materia prima"; the primal, undifferentiated substance from which all things are made.</note>, approaching nearest to its most general genus; it is also called the **quintessence** <note>The "fifth element" or purest essence.</note>, or even their **heaven**. This matter truly must be converted (if it is of perfect things) into the nature of forms, and into that other nature of imperfect things; this is called a **compound ferment**, which is made from the **first matter**, the nature of metals, and **oil**, dripped in drop by drop. Afterwards, by our natural **Mercury** through <term>inceration</term> <note>The process of softening a substance to a wax-like consistency.</note>, which is the medium joining **Mercury** with the said **first matter**, a **philosophical gum** is made in this way. A **simple ferment** is that to which nothing is added, such as elements or evacuated metals existing by themselves or taken simply. It is **compound** when many are mixed together. He who cannot specifically convert the bodies of perfect and imperfect things into their **first matter** will also be unable to have simple or compound ferment (without which the stone will be empty and void). The **earth** indeed raised from metallic bodies into the **sulfur of nature** is called the **salt of the philosophers** or **vegetable Mercury**, and the medium joining all extremes to one end—that is, the **heaven of form**, or the **philosophical key** for perfect bodies: and this earth is also called **mercurial elements**. The less perfect is the **philosophical stone** not fermented in virtue nor in quantity: it is composed of fire and air, or of earth and fire.

-># SUPERNATURAL #<-

**Fermentation** <note>original: "Fermentatio"</note> is an operation denoting a double multiplication: namely, of quantity and of power <note>original: "virtutis"</note>. When multiplication occurs in quantity, the power is diminished, and vice versa. There is also another multiplication of power and quantity together: the first occurs with common Mercury; the second with the Mercury of metals; and the third with the <term>vegetable Mercury</term> <note>In alchemy, "vegetable" refers to the life-force or power of growth within a substance.</note> or the <term>menstruum</term> <note>A solvent used to dissolve solids.</note> of the philosophers, etc. Fermentation is performed to shorten the long duration of time through form, heaven, and Mercury as it is commonly understood.

**Evacuation** is the name for the separation of the pure from the impure.

**Multiplication** is the reduction of the evacuated thing back upon its own earth, so that the purity of the spirit may arise.

The **spirit of bodies** is the substance which is evacuated from bodies through solution by means of the **philosophical key**.

**Exuberant quicksilver** <note>original: "Argentum vivum exuberatum"</note> is the spirit of bodies ascending together with the key and passing through the <term>alembic</term> <note>A glass or copper vessel used for distillation.</note>.

**Sulfur of nature** is the sublimated earth of bodies, converted into <term>foliated earth</term> <note>original: "terram foliatam"; a purified state of matter that appears flaky or leaf-like.</note>, which is called the first and nearest matter of metals.

**Tincture** is derived from air and fire, or from earth and fire. **Oil** is the fixed element that facilitates liquefaction and fixation.

The **Stone** is a germ or sprout [grown] from the foliated earth and the fixed oil already sown into it.

The **fire of the stone** consists of the essential fire of the body and the co-essential fire of the vegetable menstruum; from these a single fire is composed which transmutates all metals in an instant—the aforementioned fire assisting, of course, by its own vegetative power. The elements of the bodies must be distilled with the menstruum itself as many times as necessary for the Great Stone, until they are fixed and no menstruum actually appears with them. From the condition and property of these things, a fire arises like a flash of lightning, suddenly burning away any imperfect metals and inducing in them another, perfect form, etc.

## *On the shortening of the philosopher's stone.*

### CHAPTER XV.

The entire life of minerals consists in two waters: the first makes the stone volatile without labor and without danger; the second fixes it, and is fixed with it—though with danger. This is because this second water is drawn from a certain **stinking solvent** <note>original: "menstruali foetente"</note>, massed together from four things. No stronger water is found in the world; it is mortal, etc. The greater danger is that the spirits might flee during the washing. It is produced in a shorter time than other stones.

The **Animal [Stone]** is that which has almost no end, due to the governance of the elements, and in it consists a greater science than in any other stone. The **Vegetable Stone**, although it is very long and tedious [to produce] and is of the highest condition, must nevertheless follow the animal stone as far as...

**Fermentation** is an operation signifying a twofold multiplication: namely, of quantity and of virtue <note>In this context, "virtue" refers to the inherent power, potency, or medicinal effectiveness of the substance.</note>. When multiplication occurs in quantity, the virtue is diminished, and vice versa. There is also another type that multiplies both virtue and quantity simultaneously: the first is done with common Mercury; the second with the Mercury of metals; and the third indeed with the vegetable Mercury or the <term>menstruum of the philosophers</term> <note>original: "menstruo philosophorum"; an alchemical solvent believed to dissolve solids into their primary matter without destroying their "seed."</note>, etc. Fermentation is performed to shorten the long duration [of the work] by means of the form, the heavens, and Mercury as it is commonly understood.

**Evacuation** is the name given to the separation of the pure from the impure.

**Multiplication** is the reduction of the evacuated thing back onto its "earth," so that the purity of the spirit may arise.

The elements of the bodies must be distilled with the menstruum itself so many times toward the "Great Stone" until they are fixed, and no trace of the menstruum appears with them in actuality. Thus, from the condition and property of these things, a fire may arise like a bolt of lightning, suddenly burning away any imperfect metals and inducing in them another, perfect form.

*On the shortening of the philosophical stone.*

->CAP. XV.<-

The entire life of minerals consists in two waters: the first makes the stone volatile without labor and without danger; the latter fixes it, and is itself fixed with it, though with danger. This is because this [second] water is drawn from a certain "stinking menstrual" <note>original: "menstruali foetente"; likely referring to a corrosive acid or a sulfurous compound.</note> massed together from four things. No stronger water than this is found in the world; it is mortal, etc. The greatest danger is that the spirits might escape during the washing. It is produced in a shorter time than other stones.

The **Animal Stone** is that which has almost no end <note>meaning it is inexhaustible or has infinite power</note> because of the governance of the elements; it requires greater knowledge than any other stone. The **Vegetable Stone**, although it is quite long-lasting, and even of the highest condition, must nevertheless follow the Animal Stone.

<page-num>314</page-num>
<header>THE CRAFT</header>
<meta>practice</meta>

regarding the ratification and rectification of the elements: and thus prepared, it is more effective than the animal quintessence.

The **Quintessence** <note>original: "Essentia quinta"; the "fifth essence" or purest spiritual form of a substance, beyond the four elements of earth, air, fire, and water</note> is the spirit in the mineral stone that has the power both to kill and to bring to life.

In the **Animal** kingdom, it sometimes exists as the highest medicine for human bodies, particularly if it has been extracted from blood.

In the **Vegetable** stone, however, the spirit of the quintessence possesses the power to restore youth and to preserve the human body from all corruption.

### THE SHORTENED METHOD

Take 2 pounds of rectified <term>burning water</term> <note>original: "aquæ ardentis"; likely high-proof distilled alcohol or aqua vitae</note> and 1 ounce of ferment. Place them in a <term>pelican</term> <note>A specialized alchemical flask with two side-arms that loop back into the body, allowing distilled vapors to condense and flow back down for continuous circulation.</note>, and set it to digest for twenty or twenty-two days. The spirit of the quintessence will be thickened by the ferment and will be converted into a stone. After this "congealing," dissolve it in a <term>dung-bed</term> <note>original: "fimo"; a heap of decomposing manure used by alchemists as a source of gentle, steady heat</note> or a water bath for one night, and congeal it again. Let this be done three times or more, until it no longer wishes to solidify, but remains instead like oil.

With a white ferment, it does not dissolve so quickly, but it congeals faster. This medicine transmutates <note>Turns base metals into precious ones</note> only according to the nature of its ferment, and no higher. If you ferment it with its own earth, it will be a universal medicine, though not as effective as when used with one of the other ferments. If, in the aforementioned water—after the tenth distillation has been completed—you dissolve gold, and afterwards allow the water to evaporate with a gentle heat or fire, and then place this in a humid spot, it will dissolve by itself over four days into <term>potable gold</term> <note>original: "aurum potabile"; a legendary medicinal liquid gold believed to cure all ailments and grant longevity</note> for the preservation of human health. 

And if you take <term>Mercury</term> <note>original: "Mercurium"; quicksilver</note> that has been <term>sublimated</term> seven times with <term>vitriol</term> <note>Sulphate minerals used as strong acidic agents</note>, so that there is one part gold and seven parts of this Mercury, and afterwards you sublimate it as many times as needed until the Mercury is "fixed" <note>rendered solid and resistant to heat</note>, you will have a medicine that is both "tinging" <note>capable of coloring or transforming metals</note> and penetrating.

If one part of this gold, thus dissolved, is placed in a gentle fire by itself for eight days with a hundred parts of Mercury, this entire mixture will be congealed into gold. This occurs because of the spirit of the water which, during the solution of the gold, is fixed to it inseparably.

By this path, you can mix mineral substances with vegetable ones and create a medicine from them in the following manner: Once the vegetable stone has been distilled to the point where it is deprived of all "phlegm" <note>the watery, inactive part of a distillate</note>—which usually happens by the fifth distillation—take good, transparent vitriol with an equal weight of the best <term>cinnabar</term> <note>mercury sulfide</note> and grind them together. Let them dry in the sun, and afterwards over coals, until all wateriness appears to be consumed. Finally, pour on the water, and distill it first with a slow fire and then gradually increasing the heat, as is done with the sharp <term>water of the philosophers</term>. The spirit of the quintessence of the vitriol, and of the cinnabar or <term>antimony</term>, which primarily constitute the mineral stone, is then mixed with the spirit of the quintessence of our blessed burning water...

The spirit <note>original: "ritus"; likely a transcription error for "spiritus" (spirit)</note> is the soul of the **vegetable stone**: and with this continued ten times (suppose after the fifth distillation), that is, with this mixture, new materials should always be added and very well dried before they are cast into the water. After the tenth distillation, add **gold** by the weight mentioned above to the vegetable stone by itself, and you shall place it in a **philosophical furnace** <term>furno philosophico</term> <note>A specialized furnace designed to provide a constant, regulated heat over many days or months.</note>: in ten days the entire **fixation** <note>The process by which a volatile substance is rendered stable and resistant to fire.</note> will be completed, which in the vegetable [stone] by itself would scarcely be completed in twenty-five: because one spirit thickens the other. This is an most excellent work for **transmutatory Alchemy**, not for medicine. Once the fixation is done, proceed to the **solution** <note>The process of dissolving a solid back into a liquid state.</note> in a [water] bath by itself, as was said regarding the vegetable stone by itself. It should be noted that this stone made from mixtures is not dissolved as quickly as the vegetable stone by itself: but it is faster than the **mineral stone** by itself. It therefore holds a middle ground for solution, because it is finished in nine days.

It is necessary to repeat these solutions and **congealings** <note>The process of a liquid returning to a solid state.</note> often, so that the medicine may better penetrate. From the **lead of the philosophers** <note>original: "plumbe philosophorum"; not common lead, but a specific starting material in the alchemical process, often associated with antimony or a purified metallic ore.</note> is extracted an **oil of golden color**, with which if you dissolve the mineral, mixed, or animal stone after the first fixation, in three or four days, or turns, you shall be excused from the labor of the [repeated] solutions and congealings of the stone.

If you know well how to separate this from the "wateriness," and have worked according to the method of mixing set down before, you will be able to complete the stone in thirty days. This oil, however, is not necessary in the vegetable stone by itself, because solutions happen quickly in it: yet if a **sublimation** <note>The process of heating a substance until it turns to vapor and then collects as a solid again.</note> were performed there, I believe the stone could be increased.

### *On the manufacture of precious stones through the metaphysical art.*

#### CHAPTER XVI.

Extract the **mercurial water**, that is, resolve our **Mercury** <note>original: "Mercurium nostrum"; "Our Mercury" refers to the secret, purified substance of the alchemists rather than common quicksilver.</note> into the vegetable **quintessence**. Once this is done, make yourself empty wax molds, like small vessels or boats, which can be filled with liquid and float upon the water. Some make these in the shape in which precious stones are usually cut, in this manner: they take a piece of iron, cut and polished at one end just as they wish the stone to be; they dip this into oil, then into melted wax, and finally into cold water. When it is wrapped in wax, they cut the wax all around so that the form is freed from the iron. In this way, they prepare stones for themselves like gem-cutters. But I hardly believe it can be done exactly [this way]. Therefore, I would advise making them in a round or semi-round shape by whatever means, and afterward they can be cut like natural gems.

Finally, dig up the phials from the earth and bring down the others from the air. Then, fill the lower part of your spherical vessel with the "earthy" mercurial water, filling it halfway, and make the molds float upon it. Afterward, if you desire a stone of Mercury, the Sun, the Moon, Jupiter, Saturn, Venus, or Mars, fill your wax molds slightly less than full with the "heaven" of whichever said planet—that is, with its own "airy" water. However, do not fill them to the very top, lest the waters perhaps overflow. Finally, cover the spherical vessel with its upper part, and let it remain closed for several hours until you see the waters in the molds have thickened somewhat. Once this is noticed, open the vessel and turn the molds over so that the paste touches the **fixing water** <note>The liquid that stabilizes the substance, preventing it from evaporating or changing further.</note>. Leave it thus in the shade until it hardens into a stone.

But this process seems to pertain more to the **transmutatory art** <term>artem transmutatoriam</term> than to medicine, because of the simultaneous infusion of the "earth" with the "heaven." For this reason, stones made in this way are darker than those manufactured by other methods.

It is just as if a limb in the human body were injured in a wife; the corresponding limb in the body of her husband—even if it is not actually injured—nevertheless perceives the pain through potential and a certain natural compassion, born of natural love and the **divine marriage** <note>A metaphor for the deep spiritual and physical bond between husband and wife, reflecting the bond between Heaven and Earth.</note>. How much more must this very thing happen in nature itself, which consists of a divine marriage between the higher world and the lower? These were so ordained by God that one of them contains nothing that does not have a corresponding part in the other.

Since, therefore, the **lesser world** <term>minor mundus</term> <note>The "Microcosm," or man, viewed as a miniature map of the entire universe.</note>—namely man, with his body and **vital spirit** <term>spiritus vitalis</term> <note>The animating force or "breath" believed to sustain life and connect the soul to the body.</note>—was created in the likeness of the great world, and his rational part in the image of God, it is certain that whatever exists in the greater world will also be in the lesser. And just as the movements in the upper heavens never cease, so too the vital spirit of man does not cease to exercise its movements even while the body is resting or sleeping; indeed, it works more then than when he is awake. Likewise, if any limb in the body of a man is touched, the sensation of that touch soon reaches the spirit, just as was said above regarding the heavens.

We see, therefore, that there is a similar marriage between the spirit and the body of man as we have described between heaven and earth. Furthermore, whatever movement occurs in heaven flows into man, or into the elements for his use. Therefore, it is not surprising if stones not unlike precious gems can be made by **art**, by which the diseases of men can be cured, provided they were manufactured under favorable **aspects** <note>original: "aspectibus"; the relative positions of planets that determine astrological influence.</note> (as they say). How much more powerful will the remedies be when they have been dissolved into their **liquors** <note>Alchemical solutions or liquid essences.</note> and administered inside the body.

Soon after, a key is necessary, without which no entry to **natural philosophy** <term>naturalis philosophia</term> <note>The study of the physical world and its laws, a precursor to modern science.</note> is open at all.

Once we have entered, three chests appear to us. One—a vast treasure far more fortunate than the others—serves for the medicine of the human body and is contained under the waters of the air and the heavens. In the other two, waters of the air and the earth are contained together, serving both for the pursuit of immense wealth, such as the **transmutation of metals**, and for the curing of diseases. In the third, similar waters are contained, but these are for the fabrication of precious stones. From these three fountains flow waves that bring happiness to the world, through which wonders are performed in the nature of things.

When celestial waters, impregnated with mineral virtues, have been exposed to the air for a full **revolution of the circle** <note>Likely referring to a complete seasonal or zodiacal year.</note>, they become more broadly impregnated with celestial powers, through which they become fit for the resolution of all things, even the most solid of bodies. However, lower waters—also celestial, but exposed to the "belly of the earth"—receive those same virtues at the same time, but through a different medium: an earthly one. Through this, they acquire the power to **coagulate** all things, including their own **mercury** <term>argentum vivum</term> <note>literally "living silver"; the alchemical principle of fluidity and transformation.</note>. Among all various sulfurs, this one is most excellent, just as the philosophical mercury we have established is the most outstanding. Although other "philosophical" versions are found, they are not sublimated to such great subtlety and purity. Therefore, these are the greatest among the waters of the philosophers: namely, one is **formal**, celestial, and superior; the other is **material** and inferior. Yet both are born from the same root and do not differ except through the industry and application of the craft. This is to confirm what was proclaimed to us by our father **Hermes** <note>Referring to Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of alchemy.</note>, namely:

->That which is above is like that which is below, to accomplish the miracles of the one thing.<-

Here we see the first restorer of this most excellent art placing two things under a similarity of unity, through which wondrous works are made from natural things by a supernatural mastery. The first he calls "superior," that is, celestial, by which we can understand the **celestial waters**. The other he names "inferior," and this we can refer to the **earthly waters**. He says these are one and the same water; for they are from one and the same substance and do not differ in nature, but only in **accident** <note>In Aristotelian philosophy, an "accident" is a property that can change (like temperature or state) without changing the essential nature of the substance itself.</note>, which is to say, in their preparation. For through the medium of the air, the superior waters acquire a dissolving power, while through the medium of the earth, the inferior waters acquire a coagulating power. These actions are indeed accidents, not substances. See how **Johannes Trithemius** <note>A famous German abbot, polymath, and occultist (1462–1516).</note>, the most excellent of natural philosophers, explains this saying of Hermes:

->"The One" (he says) "is not a number, and from it every number arises."<-

For before the celestial water we mentioned was divided into two parts, it was one, and not divided into two vessels by separation; rather, it became two through the introduction of different accidents, as you have heard. For this reason alone, the **One** <note>original: "unarius"</note> became the **Two** <note>original: "binarius"</note>, the first of all numbers, as the same Trithemius says. It is a number, and it is numbered, because its nature is simple, and...

is, and is composed of accident. Therefore it cannot be numbered, because before it there is no number. Let this be understood concerning the unity <term>unitatis</term> <note>The Monad, or the concept of "The One."</note>, which **Hermes** explains in another way through a likeness, saying: *It is just as that*, etc. <note>original: "Est sicut id," a reference to the Emerald Tablet's "That which is below is like that which is above."</note> The **binary** <term>binarius</term> <note>The number two, representing duality or opposition.</note>, however, is denoted by Hermes through the "above" and the "below." Let the binary be cast aside (says **Johannes Trithemius**), and the **ternary** <term>ternarius</term> <note>The number three, often representing the reconciliation of opposites.</note> shall be convertible to unity. The same Hermes says, but in other words, namely: *To penetrate the miracles of the one thing.* <note>original: "Ad penetrandam miracula rei unius."</note>

It must be noted especially in this place that unity is understood by both men in two ways. Every natural thing, in its species, is numbered; however, in any particular individual, it is not numbered—unless it is considered as being composed from the elements by nature; then it is numbered. In no other way does Hermes number unity through the "above" and the "below," and Trithemius himself through the constitution of every number from the **unary** <term>unario</term> <note>The "one" as the building block of all numbers.</note>. Afterward, each measures unity by a far different method: one by the reduction of the "above" and the "below" to the likeness set for the miracle; the other by the casting away of the binary and the conversion of the same into unity through the ternary. 

Indeed, by a marvelous reasoning, they both agree in the same opinion. Therefore, **natural unity** is divisible into the binary—or rather, it is numerable—and this is reducible through the ternary to the other, **supernatural unity**, which is truly called the "attained unity," beyond which it is permitted to progress in no way. Trithemius describes it thus:

> And so, every operation of wonders consisting within the limits of nature descends from unity through the binary into the ternary: yet not before it rises from the **quaternary** <term>quaternario</term> <note>The number four.</note> through the order of steps into simplicity. For if you wish to count four, you know it must be started in no other way than from one, and you say: one, two, three, four; which, taken together, make **ten**. <note>The author uses the Pythagorean logic where 1+2+3+4=10, known as the Tetractys, symbolizing the universe.</note>
> 
> This is the perfect completion of every number, because then a return to one occurs, and beyond the **denary** <term>denarium</term> <note>The number ten.</note> there is no simple number. Those ignorant of the depths of this connection wonder at the principles we use in the operation of wonders, falsely thinking that we rely either on the help of demons or on some superstition against our Christian faith. We, however, do not wonder at those judging these things about us, because of their ignorance of those things we have mentioned before.

> Since, just as the most holy Scripture testifies concerning the internal knowledge of God—which no one understands except he who receives it—so no one can be steeped in or use these things unless he has received by divine gift a singular light of understanding from nature into nature. And there must be in him, along with the light, fire; with fire, wind; with wind, power; with power, knowledge; and with knowledge, the integrity of a sound mind. Thus far he [Trithemius] says.

From these things it appears that "attained perfection" exists in the decade—or the "second unity"—by the progress from natural unity to supernatural unity: with the binary, however, being reduced to the ternary through the quaternary, as was said above, acting as a medium. -># ARTIFICIUM<-
->[THE ARTIFICE]<-

-><page-num>322</page-num><-

If anyone wishes to obtain that wonderful thing and perform miracles, he must reduce himself from the **binary** to the **ternary** through the steps of the **quaternary** <term>quaternarius</term> <note>The number four, representing the four elements and the stages of completion.</note>, before he presumes to do this in other natural things. Indeed, man is naturally one and is not numbered, but supernaturally he is numbered as two: namely, into spirit and body, which constitute the **binary** in him. But because of the first corruption <note>original: "corruptionem primam," referring to the Fall of Man, which supposedly disrupted the harmony between body and soul.</note>, the latter overcomes the former, which means the spirit is unable to produce anything wonderful.

If he is to do so in this life, the **binary** must be overcome by the **ternary**; that is, the body must be conformed to the nature of the spirit, and the spirit must be so joined to the body that it finds peace within it. Once this is done, the **ternary** arises and rejoices in a second, perfect unity; for from the two aforementioned parts, through their conjunction, a third thing is made. However, this conjunction must be performed through the steps of the **quaternary**—that is, through the transmutation of the elements from which the body consists into a single and most pure element, in this manner:

**First**, let **water** be made from the **earth** of your body: that is, from your stony and sluggish heart, let it become soft and vigilant toward the knowledge of God and yourself, so that the images of the spirit may be imprinted upon it, no differently than characters are pressed into wax by a seal.

**Afterward**, let **air** be made from this **water**: that is, lift up your heart, now humbled, into heaven toward Him who created you; like air, always striving toward the highest things, and knocking in prayer so that your intellect might be opened to understand the things of God.

**Finally**, let **fire** be made from this **air**: that is, let all the desire of your heart be converted into love (to which fire is compared because of its heat) for God and your neighbor here on earth, so that this flame may never be extinguished.

Thus it will happen that, through this likeness, your **binary**—that is, spirit and body—will be perfectly joined into one **ternary**, through the **quaternary** and its steps, as you have heard. You now have, most excellent reader, the manifestation of the *Key of Speculative Philosophy*, published for you and all students of hidden things with a generous spirit—that key which is kept so hidden in the riddles of the ancients. It is necessary for you to fashion the key of chemical philosophy <term>philosophiae chemisticae</term> after this likeness. 

Now, what will prevent you from being able to understand these enigmatic writings in the Art? Do not falsely judge, as others do, that the professors of this art are **necromancers**—even if they perform wonders—but rather that they are **magi** and truly wise men. And so that you may see in how few words I have now explained to you what the magi, both ancient and modern, have veiled in so many and various coverings, I will not be reluctant to add some things which **Trithemius** <note>Johannes Trithemius (1462–1516), a German abbot and polymath famous for his works on cryptography and hidden knowledge.</note>—the most sagacious of all modern writers on this subject—has written. You will see that in this art, there is absolutely nothing of ghosts or superstition (which the ignorant falsely claim), nor anything that is against the true religion of God.

But I remember that previously, in the title or inscription of this little book, I made mention of the ten steps of *Speculative or Adept Philosophy*, of which we have explained seven. It is therefore right...

->## SUPERNATURAL<-

It is fitting at this point, near the end, to add a decade <note>A sequence of ten steps representing a progression toward spiritual perfection.</note> of these principles in the following manner, as follows:

**Study** generates **knowledge**. **Knowledge** gives birth to **love**. **Love** [produces] **likeness**. **Likeness** [leads to] **frequency**, or **communion**, or **familiarity**. **Communion** [gives] **confidence**. **Confidence** [yields] **virtue**. **Virtue** [attains] **dignity**. **Dignity** [results in] **power**, and **power** effects a **Miracle**.

The three degrees <note>Likely referring to the final three steps: Dignity, Power, and Miracle.</note> which are numbered here as more than the preceding ones depend on others, and are easily perceived by any initiated philosopher. For this reason, I would now make an end to our attained philosophy, were I not first reminded by the words of Trithemius <note>Johannes Trithemius (1462–1516), a German Benedictine abbot and polymath famous for his works on cryptography and the occult; he was a teacher to Agrippa and Paracelsus.</note> brought forth concerning this art, which it seemed right to place here. 

"Attained natural philosophy," he says, "which once, relying on the principles of nature, stood in its pure simplicity, has been confused by so many lies and impurities and so many deceptions, that no one—unless he is most learned in both [the true and the false]—can discern one from the other or understand them. How many wandering men have I known in this art alone, otherwise most learned, none of whom, though spending time and substance on alchemy <note>original: "alchemiæ"</note>, did not lose them: some lose their lives along with their possessions; others, wishing to draw medicine from it, achieve nothing after long labors; others, investigating the secrets of wonderful effects, could reach no practical experience; others, eager to predict the future, speak falsehoods for truths. These men, while they force in the windy opinions of their own heads, ignorantly produce bad and false things from the good and true writings of experienced men which they do not understand. 

Note three principles hidden in that natural magic, without the perfect knowledge of which, no effect follows the worker. The **first principle** consists in the **one**, not *from* which, but *through* which every virtue of natural wonders is produced into effect, of which we have spoken, because the pure proceeding from the one is not composed, nor changed. Toward it, from the **ternary** <term>ternarius</term> <note>The number three, often representing the union of body, soul, and spirit.</note> and the **quaternary** <term>quaternarius</term> <note>The number four, representing the material elements of the world.</note>, a progress is made to the **monad** <term>monas</term> <note>The "Unit" or "One," representing the Divine source or the starting point of all creation.</note>, so that the **denarius** <term>denarius</term> <note>The number ten, representing the return to unity and the completion of a cycle.</note> may be completed. For through it, there is a return of the number to the one, and at the same time a descent into the four, and an ascent into the monad. It is impossible to complete the ten except through it: the monad is joyfully converted in the triad <note>A group of three.</note>. 

All those who ignore this principle after the principle of the monad achieve nothing in the ternary, nor do they reach the sacred quaternary. For even if they possess all the books of the wise, and perfectly know the courses of the stars, the virtues, powers, operations, and properties, and fully understand their images, rings, seals, and every most secret thing: yet they can follow no effect of wonders in their operations without the knowledge of this principle, from the beginning, in the beginning. Hence, all those I have seen working in attained natural Philosophy have either achieved nothing, or have fallen into despair after long and useless operations, [succumbing] to vain, frivolous, and superstitious things. Truly, the **second principle** [is] in order, not in worth...

-># ARTIFICE<-

...indeed, separated from the first, which—existing as one—makes a **trinity** <note>original: "ternarium"; a grouping of three, often representing the spiritual or the divine in alchemical numerology.</note>, it is that which works wonders through the **duality** <note>original: "binarium"; the number two, often representing the polarization of matter or the division between the spiritual and physical.</note>. For in the one there is indeed one, and yet it is not one; it is simple, yet in the **quaternary** <note>original: "quaternario"; the number four, representing the four elements (earth, air, fire, water) or the physical foundation of the world.</note> it is composed. When this has been purified by fire in the sun, pure water comes forth, and once it has returned to its own simplicity, it will show the practitioner the completion of hidden things. 

This is the center of attained natural philosophy, whose circumference, united to itself, represents a circle—an immense order reaching into infinity. Its power is purified and simple above all things, yet smaller than all things when composed upon the degree of the quaternary. Furthermore, the **Pythagorean quaternary** <note>The number four was sacred to the followers of Pythagoras, represented by the Tetractys, symbolizing the organization of the universe.</note> number, supported by the trinity, if it observes its order and degree, being purified and pure in the one, can work the wonders and secrets of nature through the duality within the trinity. 

This is the quaternary in whose measure the trinity, joined to the duality in the one, does all things which it performs so wonderfully. For the trinity, reduced to unity through contemplation, contains all things in itself and can do whatever it wills. The **third principle** <note>In alchemy, this often refers to Sulfur, Mercury, or Salt, or specifically the "Salt" that bridges the other two.</note> is not a principle by itself, but between it and the duality lies the end of all science and the **mystical art** <note>original: "artis mysticæ"</note>, and the infallible center of the middle. In no other place is it easier to err than in this, since very few men live on earth who understand its depths. It is a varied composite, rising and remaining fixed through the **septenary** <note>original: "septenarium"; the number seven, corresponding to the seven classical planets and the seven metals.</note> multiplied eight times into the trinity. 

In this is the consummation of number, of degrees, and of order. Through this, all philosophers—true seekers of nature's secrets—have achieved wonderful effects. Through it, when reduced to the simple element in the trinity, miraculous cures for infirmities and all natural sicknesses are suddenly performed. The work of one practicing in attained natural and preternatural philosophy achieves its effect according to the arrangement of the quaternary. The prediction of future events is verified through it, and the suggestion of hidden things is perceived from nature by no other means than through this. By this unique means, the secret of nature is opened to <term>Alchemists</term> <note>Practitioners of alchemy, the ancient art of transforming matter and the self.</note>, without which neither the understanding of the art is acquired, nor the effect of the operation found. 

They err, believe me, they all err, who trust they can perform anything in the hidden sciences of nature without these three principles. However, the greater cause of error is that the wise men of old, imbued with the secrets of nature, either remained completely silent about these things or shrouded them in excessive obscurity, so that they cannot be truly understood except by those like themselves. 

The philosophy of this institution is secret and celestial; if anyone truly desires to know and understand anything within it, he must flee the tumult of men, desert the world, and contemplate heaven not only with his eyes, but with his mind. The Spirit of God breathes where it wills; it illuminates whom it wills; and whom it has overshadowed with its divine power, it leads into all knowledge of truth. He who has received this should give thanks to God, and strive to correspond to the fruits of good works according to the strength he has received, recognizing that he has received it—and thus he will find no reason to be proud. ...if it has not been granted, let him understand his own sluggishness, because he did not labor to know; or let him praise the mercy of the Creator, who willed that there be obstacles for his own benefit so that he would not know; or if he has not acquired it, let him confess that God was not his debtor for such a great gift, and let him not murmur. You are a friend; listen to a friend advising you, and you will understand what has been done. As a conqueror of your neighbors, trample the fire of envy, not the air of mortals; levity threatens danger with the hatred of the immortal God. Flee the assembly of men caring for worldly things, but associate yourself with those meditating on heavenly things. Your safety is in the swallows' little nest; danger lies in the dung of hens <note>The author uses bird metaphors: the swallow represents the "volatile" or spiritual heights, while common poultry represents the "fixed" or base, worldly concerns.</note>. Because the art of divine love is long, but time is short <note>A variation of the Hippocratic aphorism *Ars longa, vita brevis*.</note>, and it is better to always love the Creator in truth rather than the creature. However, these principles are too difficult for the intellect of men, and accessible only to a man disposed by a special condition of the stars, art, talent, and nature; without the perfect knowledge of these, those working in the "attained philosophy" achieve nothing. This natural philosophy not only produces visible effects, but also wonderfully illuminates the intellect of the man skilled in it toward the knowledge of divinity, and provides invisible fruits for the soul.

But we see its name today is hated and odious to men, so that they condemn all who study it with a single sentence, and judge its every use to be utterly adverse and contrary to the Christian religion. Yet if it were reduced to its original purity, it would once again become lovable to all and especially useful to Princes. But who is so fit, who so learned and powerful, that he can undertake this work? It is not the business of a single day, nor the work of a poor man, nor of an unlearned one; where both the deepest knowledge in almost every science is required, and wealth, so that the volumes of many can be brought together. # TREATISE
## ON THE PHYSICAL LIGHT OF NATURE TAKEN FROM GENESIS, ACCORDING TO THE WISDOM OF THEOPHRASTUS PARACELSUS
### Argument of the entire work.

<image-desc>A decorative woodcut initial 'S' depicting scrolling foliage and flowers.</image-desc>

*It is a wonder that the ancient physicists did not consider the highest and foremost secret <note>original: "arcanum"</note> of all natural philosophy, which is founded in the single center of eternal immensity. Perhaps it was because, being intent on more obvious things, they passed over those which are deeply hidden; or rather, it was not granted to them to know God more clearly through His works. Indeed, Jesus Christ willed to reveal this to His own in these latter times. Concerning this, the first of all (as far as I know), Paracelsus <note>Philippus Aureolus Theophrastus Bombastus von Hohenheim (1493–1541), a Swiss physician and influential alchemist who sought to reconcile nature with scripture.</note>, writing in his book *To the Athenians* or to their disciples, teaches under a veil <note>original: "sub involucro"; a term for cryptic or allegorical writing used to protect sacred knowledge.</note> that the **great mystery** <note>original: "mysterium magnum"; in Paracelsian thought, this refers to the primordial "mother" or womb of all creation, often equated with the chaos of Genesis.</note> is uncreated and is the mother and first matter of all natural creatures. And because it deigned to unite itself at some point with the things that will eventually pass away, it also exists in a single created center in the universe. All things (he says) are to return to their first essence, yet not into their first matter, nor into the great mystery; but into that alone which existed before it—namely, good or evil—that is, into the likeness of the **Unity** <note>original: "Unarii"; the Monad or the state of being one with God.</note> or the **Duality** <note>original: "Binarii"; the Dyad or the state of division and opposition.</note>. Nor is this mystery ever to return to that state in which it was at the time of creation. This first principle is divided into the three first natural principles <note>The "Tria Prima" of Paracelsus: Sulfur (the soul/flammability), Mercury (the spirit/volatility), and Salt (the body/solidity).</note>, the third of which is again divided into four <note>Referring to the four Aristotelian elements: Fire, Air, Water, and Earth.</note>, while the other two nevertheless remain under the sacred triad. For one was divided by one into the firmament and the element; yet they remain under the marriage of union by the power of the light that vivifies their soul and body. Truly, in these matters he [Paracelsus] wished to be obscure on purpose...*

->OF THE ENTIRE WORK.<-

<margin>X 4</margin>

Paracelsus wrote this way, admittedly not for everyone, but for those whom he judged to be unworthy of such secrets <note>original: "arcanis"</note>, and especially for those who are accustomed to despise such things: fearing perhaps that if they ever understood these things, they might abuse them. He did not notice, meanwhile, that those wandering along the broad way <note>A biblical reference to the path of destruction (Matthew 7:13); the author suggests even the "lost" should be guided toward the truth.</note> ought to be led back to the true path according to God’s command. I, on the contrary, because I saw that God is the key who unlocks His secrets to the worthy while likewise closing them to the unworthy, did not hesitate any longer; for those things which can benefit the good should be made public as far as is permitted, and not suppressed because of the wicked. For He Himself, to whom these things belong, knows how to protect them from all who strive to profane them, and to take them away whenever it seems fit to Him. He said furthermore: **To the one who has, more will be given, and from the one who has not, even what he has will be taken away.** 

Accordingly, it seemed opportune to explain in quite clear words those things which were handed down under a riddle <note>original: "sub aenigmate"</note>, not only by Paracelsus, but also by the most ancient authors and <term>spagyric</term> <note>The alchemical art of separating, purifying, and recombining materials to reveal their inner essence.</note> physicists. This was done so that, if it could ever be achieved, the mutual stains of hatred and the seeds of envy arising from obscure traditions might cease. Nor did we judge it right to use other authorities to prove our foundations of Physics <note>original: "Physices"; here meaning Natural Philosophy or the study of the physical laws of creation.</note>, except for the authority of Him who established nature itself, and taught us through Moses that the **Genesis** of all things was founded "in the beginning." Wherefore, we have undertaken to treat this subject only *physically* (as our calling requires), and not *theologically*: lest perhaps anyone should think us to be wandering outside our profession. 

Therefore, we leave to theologians and pious men their interpretations intact; indeed, we wish them in no way to be harmed in this part, but rather we embrace them theologically in a physical manner. Finally, so that it may be seen that many others—both the most ancient and also the more recent <term>spagyric</term> <note>The OCR uses "spargicos" and "spargirice," early variations of "spagyric."</note> professors of the "attained philosophy"—were of the same opinion, I bring forward as witnesses **Hermes Trismegistus** <note>The legendary Hellenistic figure to whom the foundation of alchemy (Hermeticism) is attributed.</note> and **Johannes Trithemius** <note>Johannes Trithemius (1462–1516), a German Benedictine abbot, polymath, and occultist.</note>, whose writings are taken entirely from Genesis. ## The Author’s Outcry to God.

<image-desc>An ornamental drop-cap 'S' within a square frame decorated with foliage.</image-desc>Highest goodness, immeasurable wisdom, eternal God, it is in no way possible for the human intellect, without the greatest bewilderment of mind, to consider even the smallest point of your inexhaustible wisdom—to say nothing of expressing it with a stumbling tongue or writing it with a trembling pen—unless it happens by the command of your most holy spirit, which impresses these things upon the hearts of men. It does not cease to silently warn and daily exhort them toward the confession of truth in all things. Since if this is to be attempted or achieved by anyone living on earth, it is first necessary that they be illuminated by the light of your divine splendor, so that they may recognize the darkness of their own ignorance and frankly confess that they can be freed from it by no other means than your power. And if perhaps, by the persuasion of the slanderer <note>original: "calumniatoris"; a common epithet for the Devil or the serpent who misleads humanity.</note>, he seeks help from himself, he will find himself plunged into a deeper pit of captivity; for by himself he will never find any other means of liberation than the snare in which he entangled himself from the beginning, when he turned away from the obedience he owed to you alone, his Creator. Most evident examples of this disobedience are still placed before our eyes daily through the writings that the unfaithful have produced until now out of human wisdom, especially concerning the treatment of all faculties, arts, and sciences, in which they seek and teach nothing but paths straying from the target of truth. This itself arises from no other source than their own principles and foundations, which they did not draw, as they should have, from the true fountain of truth—the center of all sciences—but from the opposite and false center of lies, namely, <term>Duality</term> <note>original: "Dualitate"; a philosophical concept where the "Two" represents separation from the "One" (God), signifying the root of all division, error, and physical decay.</note>. And what is worst, they have studied to most stubbornly defend and fortify these errors of theirs against any pious and good men who try to call those who have strayed back to the center of truth from God. To resist these men more fiercely, they have built up ramparts and bulwarks, the better to hide and protect the falsehood of their poorly-founded principles. As is evident...

...[of all] the first and most powerful: *Against one who denies principles* <note>original: "Contra negantem principia"; a traditional scholastic axiom stating that argument is impossible if the parties do not agree on basic foundations.</note> (they say) *there is no disputing.* What wonder is it? For these principles are crafted in such a way that, once they are granted, it becomes necessary for the one who agreed to them to fall into error and confusion. In this way, the children of darkness are accustomed to ensnare unwary men and deceive them with fallacies—those children who have always been wiser in their own generation than the children of light. <note>An allusion to Luke 16:8, suggesting that those focused on worldly or deceptive wisdom are often more cunning than the virtuous.</note>

Indeed, they learned what wisdom they possess from their father, namely the serpent.
