# PHILOSOPHY

...they communicate a union. Who but one who has lost his mind would deny that such virtues exist in all other natural bodies, according to a greater or lesser degree? He cannot be a philosopher who denies that bread or grain, and any other things, possess a <term>spirit</term> <note>In this context, "spirit" refers to the volatile, active essence or "life force" of a substance, such as the alcohol distilled from wine.</note> no less effective than the spirit of wine (though it may not be as abundant), provided the quantity and strength are equal. If, therefore, such a spirit can be artificially separated from bread, wine, and other things, how much more naturally and by a far more subtle division does this occur within a human being? Only through these principles can philosophical <term>transmutations</term> <note>The transformation of one substance into another.</note> be understood. Do we not know that the purer substance of bread and wine is transmuted by nature into the flesh and blood of man, and that from an invisible vegetable form, a visible animal form is created? It is not the species of things that are changed, but their forms. Who will still doubt that philosophical transmutations can be performed through art and nature within man far better than nature alone achieves with bread, wine, and the rest, when unaided by the service of the Art? For there are many other bodies in the nature of things which possess a greater natural virtue and celestial influence; from these, spirits can be separated no differently than from wine and bread, and be transmuted into the substance, flesh, and blood of man—and more excellently by art than by nature, though nature still cooperates. But why should I repeat so often those things which are clearer than light to philosophers? If anyone refuses to believe, let him experiment; if he remains stubborn, let him go his way. No one should be forced for his own benefit, but only warned: if he chooses to despise the warning, he does so at his own loss, not the counselor's.

Furthermore, let us apply what has been said to the <term>spagyric art</term> <note>The alchemical practice of separating and then recombining the constituent parts of a substance to create a more potent medicine.</note> through the attraction of virtues. In every elemental body, **our Mercury** <note>original: *Mercurius noster*; referring not to common quicksilver, but to the "Mercury of the Philosophers," a refined spiritual essence.</note> is contained. In some, however, it is so remote that a man’s life would fail before it could be removed from them; in others, it is so near that its extraction is very easy. Some, not ignorant of this secret—namely, that Mercury exists in everything—have attempted to extract it from stones, rye straw, flowers, and woods, but in vain. Some have extracted Mercury from more "proximate" sources, such as **celandine** <note>original: *chelidonia*</note>, **rosemary flowers**, **mercury herb**, and **white lily**, and from their juices, through the mastery of the water-bath and the dung-pit <note>original: *balnei fimique magisterium*; horse dung was used as a consistent, gentle heat source for alchemical digestion.</note>. This Mercury was not unlike common mercury in color, weight, quality, and quantity. Therefore, thinking they had found the greatest secret, they sublimated it with corrosives and corrupted its nature. But whoever takes the Mercury of the philosophers converted into such a species, or takes common mercury and reduces it to water without any material additive (which can be done with the "phlegm of the medium," if he gives it its "air" within the vessel and distills it seven times), he shall possess the **light of pearls**; for this is their...

...heterogeneous part, which lacks the condition of the **philosophical stone**. Therefore, the extraction of such a Mercury is not necessary for the transmutatory art. In certain specific substances, our Mercury possesses a somewhat free action, such as in **tartar** <note>original: "tartaro"; a potassium salt that crusts in wine barrels, used as a flux or solvent in alchemy.</note>: for it is evident from the operations of goldsmiths that when there is something of **silver** <note>original: "lunæ"</note> within **copper** <note>original: "Venere"</note>, and it is placed in white wine or in its "soul" <note>The "anima" or essence of the wine.</note>, the power of the **philosophical Mercury** will bring the silver tincture to the surface. By this, the bond of its harmony with silver is revealed. It works better when you have quenched glowing copper in tartar dissolved by white wine; it will take on a whiteness, but it is not a permanent color because it lacks a fixed spiritual subject. 

Another experiment of it is made where **iron** <note>original: "Mars"</note> has been frequently quenched in the aforementioned solution; it will take on the softness of **gold** <note>original: "solis"</note> and **silver** <note>original: "lunæ"</note>. For iron is dry, and far removed from Mercury more than any other bodies, and all dryness has the character of a void; therefore, the philosophical Mercury is easily received into it, by which it is also brought to that softness.

The form of the **philosophical sky** <note>original: "Cæli vero philosophici"; likely referring to a specific refined state of matter or a specialized vessel.</note>, however, is another substance in which two free operations are seen: the first is that by which it truly converts everything placed upon it into the species under which it itself exists. This is an evident sign of an admirable **vegetable power** <note>In alchemy, "vegetable" refers to the power of life and growth—the ability of a substance to "sprout" or multiply like a plant.</note>, by reason of which substances are transmuted into other forms. Let the craftsman therefore consider what this Mercury can accomplish when stripped of its own form and shaped by another. 

There is also another equally evident operation, such as when the bodies of the **perfect metals** <note>Gold and silver.</note> are ground upon a porphyry stone with that form; both of these will be reduced to the form of an **amalgam**, from which Mercury will be extracted over the course of a year. This is because the Mercury existing here in the gold and silver is moved toward the Mercury contained in that form, and vice versa. Hence, in the "angle of harmony," they are gathered together so that in the philosophical sky the perfect bodies may be multiplied, and their Mercury can in no way resist being reduced into the form of an amalgam by another natural bond. In other specific substances, these operations of the philosophical sky could also be observed, which we leave aside for the sake of brevity, and because they can be understood from what has already been said. 

The end of this entire **mastery** <note>The "Magisterium" or the successful completion of the alchemical process.</note> is that the Philosophical Mercury be placed in the celestial sphere; otherwise, the craftsman will work wrongly and in vain. It seems marvelous that this Mercury, situated in a "super-celestial" place, does not retain its color, weight, quality, and quantity, even though all these belong to its nature. The reason for this is that it is placed under another form than when it lay hidden within a specific substance. 

There is also this method of extracting Mercury in this craft: namely, that the best white or red wine be put into separation, and from it **burning water** <note>original: "ardens aqua"; a historical term for distilled alcohol or ethanol.</note> be distilled as is customary. Afterward, let it be **rectified** <note>Distilled repeatedly to increase purity and concentration.</note> four times for greater subtlety, though three times alone will be enough, lest the burning spirit evaporate; therefore, those who rectify it seven times have erred. # PHILOSOPHY #
### 442 ###

...the sign of the purification <note>original: "cationis," likely completing "purificationis" from the previous page</note> shall be this: when sugar placed upon it together with water is entirely consumed, leaving nothing behind. This material is the subject from which the **quintessence** <note>original: "essentia quinta"; the "fifth essence" or purest spiritual component of a material, beyond the four elements.</note> is drawn through a **pelican vessel** <note>original: "vas pellicanicum"; a specialized alchemical flask used for continuous distillation and circulation, named for its resemblance to a pelican pecking its breast.</note>. By this operation, it will happen that along a diagonal line, the upper part—or the quintessence—will be separated from the lower part, namely from the murky dregs.

**Mercury** <note>original: "Mercurius"; here referring to the metallic element or its alchemical "spirit."</note> can also be extracted by calcining it in a glassmaker’s furnace for three days, though in a large quantity, because it is greatly diminished in the process. Once burnt, let it be ground upon a **marble stone**, and while contained upon it in a cold and damp place, it will dissolve into water. Afterward, it must be distilled through a **filter sleeve** <note>original: "manicam filtream"; a conical cloth filter used to clarify liquids.</note> and received in a glass vessel. Mercury can be extracted from this in a twofold way: the first, just as we have said concerning wine; the second, truly through the artifice of separating the qualities from the elements, and so on. From Mercury treated in this manner, the **best work** can be made, as described below.

The **sky** <note>original: "cælum"; in alchemy, this refers to the most refined, volatile, and "heavenly" part of a substance.</note> of any individual substance, together with the sky of red or white wine, or a mass of **tartar**, is placed with either form according to the teaching of the **Great Work** <note>original: "majoris operis"; the process of creating the Philosopher's Stone.</note> by the mastery of separating qualities from the elements. Once the vessel is blocked up so that the "sky" does not flee, let it be cooked by the steady heat of a **bath** <note>original: "balnei"; likely a "balneum Mariae" or water bath, used for gentle heating.</note> without intermission for several days. Afterward, when the vessel is opened, let a portion of the "air" of any of the aforementioned things be added for the second part of the "sky," and let it be cooked for as many days as before. When these days are finished, the vessel is opened again, and a portion of the "sky of fire" of any of them is added—as much as there was of the sky of wine. With the vessel blocked again, let them be cooked by steady heat for another fifteen days. When the artifice of mixing is complete, you will see the mixture <unclear>for</unclear> change into a less perfect state through intermediate colors. By these colors, the craftsman must direct this work until he arrives at the most perfect **Great Work**, which—by the virtue acquired through the **spagyric** <note>original: "spagiricum"; the alchemical process of separating and then recombining the constituents of a substance to create a more potent medicine or material.</note> work—is able to transmute and transform its own appearance into external substances three thousand times its own weight.

The individual things suitable for mixing are: **rosemary flowers**, **new honey**, **mercury herb** <note>original: "mercurialis"; refers to the plant *Mercurialis annua*, not the metal.</note>, **celandine**, **red lily**, **human blood**, etc. Furthermore, because dignity is acquired through virtue, before the initiate is received into power, we judge it right to add in this place those things which can render one worthy who wishes to work toward greater things.

Hence, we shall bring forth into the light the **spagyric offspring** from a threefold genus of individual substances, derived from the "abbreviated work."

The entire way of minerals, therefore, consists in **two waters**: the first makes the **stone** volatile without labor and without danger; the latter fixes it, and is fixed with it, but with danger. This is because this water is drawn from a certain foul-smelling **menstruum** <note>original: "menstruali"; a solvent used in alchemy to dissolve solids.</note> made into a mass from four things. No water more powerful than this is found in the world; it is mortal, etc. It is produced in a shorter time than other stones.

The **animal work**, however, hardly has an end because of the governance of the elements, and there is greater science in it than in any other stone.

### CHEMICA. ###
#### 443 ####

The **Vegetable Stone** <term>Vegetable Stone: An alchemical substance derived from plant matter, believed to hold the "soul" of the plant and provide extraordinary healing properties.</term>, although it requires a quite lengthy process, is nevertheless of the highest composition. It must, however, follow the **Animal Stone** <note>original: "animalem... lapidem"</note> in terms of the balancing and purification of its elements; prepared in this way, it is more effective than the animal stone.

The **quintessence** <note>original: "Essentia quinta"; the spiritual "fifth essence" that remains when the four physical elements are removed.</note> is a spirit within the Mineral Stone that has the power to both kill and bring to life.

In the Animal Stone, the greatest medicine for human bodies sometimes exists, especially when it has been extracted from blood.

In the Vegetable Stone, however, the spirit of the quintessence serves as the restoration of youth and the most powerful preservation of the human body from all decay.

Therefore, into two pounds of rectified **water of life** <note>original: "aquæ ardentis"; literally "burning water," referring to highly distilled alcohol or a potent alchemical solvent.</note>, throw one ounce of ferment; let it digest by the artifice of the **pelican vessel** <note>original: "pellicanico... artificio"; a specialized flask used for continuous circulation of a liquid.</note> for a space of twenty or twenty-two days, and by this path, it will be converted into the stone. After coagulation in dung <note>original: "fimo"; used as a source of steady, gentle heat</note> or a water bath, let it be dissolved again, and then thickened once more. Let this be done a third time or more often until it can no longer be thickened into a solid, but remains liquid like oil. With white ferment, it does not dissolve so quickly but thickens faster. This medicine transforms things into nothing other than what its ferment was, and no higher.

If you ferment it with its own earth, it will be a **universal medicine**, though not as effective as it would be with one of the other ferments. If you dissolve gold in the aforementioned water after a tenth distillation has been performed, and afterward allow the water to evaporate with a gentle heat or fire, and keep the material in a damp place, it will dissolve by itself within four days into **potable gold** <term>Potable Gold (aurum potulentum): A legendary liquid gold elixir thought to cure all diseases and grant longevity.</term>, for the preservation of human health. Likewise, if you take **Mercury** <note>original: "Mercurium"</note> sublimated seven times with **vitriol** <note>original: "vitriolo"; a sulfate mineral</note>—so that there is one part gold to seven parts of this "silver" [mercury]—and sublimate it as many times until the Mercury is fixed <note>original: "figatur"; made resistant to heat and no longer volatile.</note>, you will have a medicine that dyes and penetrates. Again, if one part of this dissolved gold is placed by itself over a slow fire for eight days with a hundred parts of Mercury, this entire mixture will be thickened into gold. This happens because of the spirit of the water, which is fixed with the gold in an inseparable bond during its dissolution. In this way, minerals can be mixed with vegetable substances, and a medicine can be made from them in this manner.

#### 445 ####

...[virtue] is granted to us by divinity; through diligent observation of truth and virtue in both words and deeds, a constancy of virtues is infused from heaven for the sake of power. Similarly in **Spagyrics** <term>Spagyrics: The alchemical art of separating and then recombining the essential components of plants or minerals to create potent medicines.</term>, even though virtues are extracted from insensible natural bodies through this art, they will not be fit for a miraculous act unless they are led further to their extreme power. But the more they are purified and subtilized, the closer they approach that primary celestial influence which they possess, having been made more like it; and consequently, they penetrate and work more effectively, so that what they achieve in the cure of any infirmity must be regarded as a miracle. 

But now we must see what the power of natural things lacking sensation is, such as minerals and others of that kind. Thus, the spirits of imperfect bodies <note>In alchemy, "imperfect" bodies typically refers to base metals like lead or iron, which were believed to be "sick" or "immature" versions of gold.</note> are evacuated, or their **exuberant quicksilver** <term>Argentum vivum exuberatum: A highly refined, potentized form of mercury believed to be the "root" of all metals.</term> is drawn out, or the **first matter** <term>Materia prima: The formless, original substance from which all things are made; in alchemy, the goal is to reduce matter to this state so it can be "reborn."</term> is made fit to receive any form. There is, however, a difference between these spirits and others evacuated from perfect metals: for these are formal, while those are material. 

Likewise, the imperfect as well as the perfect can be converted into oil, and in this way, the preparation of form and matter takes place. Necessarily, the **sulfur of nature** <term>Sulphur naturae: The active, combustible, or "soul" principle of a substance.</term> of perfect things must be converted into oil, but not that of others, because it is to be informed by the oil of perfect things, unless perhaps someone wishes to reduce everything to oil so that the work becomes clearer. 

Oil of this kind is made through the separation of qualities in the elements. **Saturn** <note>Lead</note> and **Jupiter** <note>Tin</note> are therefore of one and the same nature when they are reduced to spirit, exuberant quicksilver, sulfur of nature, tincture, oil, or the stone—these things existing in both of them beyond number. Likewise, while they and all others retain their ancient being, they have one individuated nature, and another in their simple virtue multiplied by way of generation and procession into spirit, sulfur of nature, tincture, oil, and the stone. And this can be said more properly of the stone than of others, because the substance is multiplied from their unities, which indeed have one virtue from all these. Since any of the metals has an ultimate unity which it did not have before it was converted into the stone. This unity is extended by the multiplication of the extreme principles, just as in the said substances, an argument for their form and a multiplication of virtues may be made. In this manner, the doctrine of the **minor work** <term>Minor Work: Also known as the "Little Work" (Lesser Work), this refers to the alchemical process of creating the White Stone, which can transmute metals into silver, as a precursor to the Great Work (Gold).</term> concludes and ends.

**Calcination** <note>Reducing a metal to powder through heat.</note>, **dissolution** <note>Dissolving a solid into a liquid.</note>, evacuation, **multiplication** <note>Increasing the power or quantity of the alchemical medicine.</note>, spirit, the **alembic** <note>A glass or copper vessel used for distillation.</note>, exuberant quicksilver, sulfur of nature, tincture, oil, **inceration** <term>Inceration: A process of adding liquid to a dry substance until it reaches a waxy, soft consistency.</term>, **sublimation** <note>Heating a substance until it turns to vapor and then solidifies again in the upper part of the vessel.</note>, and the stone have one condition in **Saturn** [lead], another in **Mars** <note>Iron</note>, another in **Venus** <note>Copper</note>, and so on for the rest. Saturn also has one condition in any of these: one with Jupiter, another with Mars, another with the **Sun** <note>Gold</note>, and another with Venus.

...with one of these, Jupiter and Saturn, or Venus and Jupiter with Saturn, or with Mars himself <note>In alchemical shorthand, these planets represent the metals tin (Jupiter), lead (Saturn), copper (Venus), and iron (Mars).</note>. In this way, the qualities of metals can be multiplied by mixing one or more with another. However many ways the mixture is made, the condition of the stone will vary accordingly.

Calcination, in turn, is equal to solution, and dissolution to evacuation, this to multiplication, and that to spirit, and so on, for the constitution of the subject, which is the stone. Likewise, the alembic <term>Alembic: A distillation apparatus consisting of two vessels connected by a tube, used here to describe how the equipment serves every stage of the process.</term> serves all equally according to its function.

The sulfur of nature <term>Sulfur of Nature: In alchemy, sulfur represents the active, masculine, and combustible principle of a substance, often associated with its "soul."</term> is greater than the exuberant quicksilver <term>Argentum vivum exuberatum: A highly refined, potentized form of mercury believed to be the "root" or "seed" of all metals.</term>, and both of these are greater than the spirit.

The Lesser Work <note>original: "Opus minus"; the stage of alchemy focused on the creation of the White Stone, which transmutes base metals into silver.</note> cannot possibly be accomplished without the sulfur of nature extracted from imperfect bodies. This is because it would lack their specific natural "medium"; without this intermediary, the perfect bodies could not transmute the imperfect ones into their own species. This is the very definition of a medium: that the stone is composed of the sulfur of nature and quicksilver drawn from imperfect bodies, combined with the oil of perfect bodies <note>The "perfect bodies" are gold and silver.</note>. Thus, the stone acts as a medium participating in both natures. Because of the harmony it shares with imperfect metals, it can find a place throughout all their parts, so that the smallest part of the stone resides within their smallest part. It penetrates these existing parts by reason of its extreme subtility. 

And because the matter of the stone, which was drawn from the imperfect bodies, is formed through all its parts and bound to a certain external form by an unbreakable bond—and by a "vegetable" <note>Used here to mean "life-giving" or "growing" property.</note> property which it receives from the philosophical key—it is so shaped by that form that its smallest part truly contains the essence of that same form. In this way, the imperfect metals lay aside their old forms which were present in them in act, so that they may receive the forms of the perfect metals which were present in them only in potential. Thus, they are transmuted into perfect metallic bodies.

Elsewhere, the method of working with the sulfur of nature of Saturn or Jupiter <note>original: "Saturni vel Jovis"; lead or tin.</note> has been described. Now, however, we state that a mixture can be made with two, three, four, or all of them according to the will of the operator, so that the craftsman may create the condition he desires. The method for extracting the oil from perfect bodies is set out in another place; the method is the same as all the others: through calcination, dissolution, evacuation, multiplication, spirit, the alembic, exuberant quicksilver, sulfur of nature, tincture, oil, inceration <term>Inceration: A process of softening a substance, often by adding a liquid, until it reaches a wax-like consistency.</term>, sublimation, and through fire.

When you wish to join two together, place them into calcination by means of the philosophical key <note>original: "clave philosophica"; a secret solvent or specific method required to open the "locked" nature of a metal.</note>, then into dissolution, and into the rest of the aforementioned steps up to and including sublimation. If, however, they are perfect and have been made into the sulfur of nature, place them into multiplication; likewise, if the matter is too hard, pour on a portion of menstrual blood <note>original: "sanguinis menstrualis"; in this context, it is a symbolic term for a transformative solvent, likely a red mercurial liquid, rather than literal blood.</note> so that it may be converted into oil.

# CHEMISTRY #
#### 447 ####

It should also be noted that the elements of metals, when drawn from them by means of **Vegetable Mercury** <term>Vegetable Mercury: Not derived from plants, but a "living" or "animating" solvent believed to be the life-force of minerals.</term>, are called their **First Matter** <term>Materia Prima: The original, undifferentiated substance from which all things are made; in alchemy, the goal is to return a metal to this state before transforming it.</term>. This matter most closely approaches its most general nature and is also called the **Fifth Essence** <note>original: "essentia quinta"; the "Quintessence" or purest, most refined element beyond earth, air, fire, and water.</note>, or even their "heaven."

This matter must be converted (if it is from "perfect" bodies like gold or silver) into the nature of forms, and the nature of other "imperfect" bodies into it. This result is called **compound ferment**, because it is made from the First Matter, the nature of the metals, and oil dripped in drop by drop. Afterwards, by means of "natural philosophical mercury" through a process of **inceration** <note>A process of softening a substance to a wax-like consistency by adding liquid.</note>—which is the medium joining the Mercury with the said First Matter—the **philosophical gum** is produced.

**Simple ferment** is that to which nothing has been added, such as the elements or the purified metals existing by themselves, which are simply at their highest state.

**Compound ferment** occurs when several things are mixed together. He who cannot specifically convert the bodies of both perfect and imperfect metals into their First Matter will be able to possess neither simple nor compound ferment; without these, the Stone will be empty and void.

Indeed, the Earth raised from metallic bodies into the **Sulfur of Nature** is called the **Salt of the Philosophers**, or Vegetable Mercury, or the "medium joining extremes" all toward one end—that is, joining "heaven" with "form," or the "philosophical key" with perfect bodies. This Earth is also called "mercurialized elements."

That which is less perfect is a Philosophical Stone that has not been fermented in either power or quantity; it is composed of fire and air, or of earth and fire.

**Fermentation** is an operation denoting a twofold multiplication: namely, of quantity and of power. When multiplication occurs in quantity, power is diminished, and vice versa. Another kind occurs in power and quantity simultaneously: the first with common mercury; the second with the mercury of metals; and the third with Vegetable Mercury or the **Philosophers’ Solvent** <note>original: "menstruo philosophorum"; a powerful universal solvent used to break down substances.</note>, etc.

Fermentation occurs to shorten the long duration of the work, arising from form, "heaven," and mercury as it is commonly understood.

**Evacuation** is defined as the separation of the pure from the impure.

**Multiplication** is the restoration of the purified thing upon its own "earth," so that a spirit of cleanliness may arise.

The **Spirit of Bodies** is the substance that is evacuated from bodies through dissolution by means of the "Philosophers' Key."

**Exuberant Quicksilver** <note>Refined, active mercury.</note> is the spirit of bodies ascending together with the "key" and passing through the **alembic** <term>Alembic: A distillation apparatus.</term>.

The **Sulfur of Nature** is the sublimated earth of bodies, converted into **foliated earth** <note>A purified, white earth that has been layered or refined through chemical action.</note>, which is called the first and most immediate matter of metals.

It should also be noted that the elements of metals, when drawn from them by **Vegetable Mercury**, are called their <term>First Matter</term><note>original: "materia prima"; the fundamental, undifferentiated substance from which all things are made.</note>, as they most closely approach their most general category; they are also called the <term>Fifth Essence</term><note>original: "essentia quinta" or quintessence; the purest, most refined element beyond the four earthly elements.</note> or even their **heaven**.

Fermentation serves to shorten the long duration of the work, involving form, heaven, and what is commonly understood as mercury.

# 448 #

->PHILOSOPHY<-

A **Tincture** is composed of air and fire, or of earth and fire.
**Oil** is the fixed element that brings about liquefaction and fixation.
The **Stone** is "leafy earth," in which the fixed oil that has been sown serves as the sprout.
The **fire of the stone** consists of the essential fire of the body and the co-essential fire of the <term>vegetable menstruum</term><note>original: "menstrui vegetabilis"; in alchemy, a "menstruum" is a solvent used to extract essences. "Vegetable" here usually refers to a solvent derived from organic matter like wine or vinegar.</note>. From these, a single fire is composed which transmutes all metals in an instant, aided by the aforementioned fire through its "vegetative" or growing power.
The elements of bodies must be distilled with the solvent itself many times—for the sake of the great <term>philosophical and spagyric</term><note>original: "philosophicum & spagiricum"; "Spagyric" refers to the alchemical process of separating, purifying, and recombining the components of a substance.</note> offspring—until they are fixed, and none of the solvent actually remains with them. In this way, from the condition and property of these things, a fire arises like a bolt of lightning, suddenly burning away any imperfect metals and inducing a different, perfect form in them.

This concludes the discussion on the power of the sixth degree of the "meditative scale" as applied to the spagyric art; it remains for us to climb to the seventh and final step. In this degree, the **miracle** is established—which, as mentioned above, is based on the "constancy" or stability required for the most fixed stone. Therefore, the miracle of constancy is an effect produced through the power of truth. To explain this, we can only use the examples of others who attained such great happiness as to reach the aim and goal of this most expert philosophy.

First of all, this shone forth in that blessed ***Stephen the protomartyr***; while he was being overwhelmed by stones because of his most constant profession of truth, he served as an example that his soul suffered nothing, as he saw the heavens open and prayed for those who were slaughtering him. The very same thing happened to those **three youths** cast into the furnace of burning fire; while they professed the truth with a truly constant mind, the proof that they suffered no pain was that in the midst of the flames they sang a hymn and praises to God the Truth, rejoicing with a cheerful spirit.

We read that this happened not only to Christian sages, but also to pagan philosophers, such as a certain philosopher of Abdera named ***Anaxarchus***, a follower of ***Democritus***. Because of his own profession of truth, he was subjected to this martyrdom by a certain emperor and tyrant of Cyprus, ***Nicocreon***: while he was being crushed in a stone mortar with an iron pestle, he said: *Pound, tyrant, pound this little body of Anaxarchus; you do not pound the mind of Anaxarchus himself at all.* <note>original: "Tunde tyranne, tunde Anaxarchi corpusculum hoc, mentem Anaxarchum ipsum minimè tundis."</note> Since this affected the tyrant most poorly—as he wished the philosopher to no longer speak the truth, which he could not bear to hear—he ordered the executioner to cut out his tongue. But Anaxarchus bit it off with his own teeth and spat it into the tyrant's open mouth before his body was ground into a pulp. O, the admirable constancy of men, which, terrified by no martyrdoms, but rather enduring death with the greatest joy for the love of truth, conquered the tyranny of the world.

In no different a way, within the spagyric offspring, after it has reached the spagyric miracle...

...brought to the <term>spagyric</term><note>original: "spagiricum"; referring to the alchemical art of separating and recombining elements to achieve purity.</note> level, it may be seen through each of the preceding steps. It rejoices in the fire, never yielding to any flames, and overcomes every tyranny and corruption of all nature—not only within itself, but also in all other things, which it renders safe from all violence of fire. Hear now the manner of its generation: After one of the forming bodies has been mixed with common mercury and common salt and calcined, let the silver be sublimated from that composition, or let the <term>spirit of wine</term><note>original: "aqua vinum"; literally "water wine," likely referring to a distilled spirit or solvent.</note> be received, and let the salt be thoroughly washed from the body with warm water.

Afterward, let the qualities of the elements be divided. To three pounds of the <term>philosophical heaven</term><note>original: "cæli philosophici"; in alchemy, "heaven" refers to the most refined, volatile, or celestial part of a substance, often a purified spirit or solvent used as a medium.</note>, let two ounces of the "lesser form" be added. To two and a half ounces of the "greater form," however, you shall take half a pound of the "heaven." From these, make a "marriage" for mixing in a very well-closed vessel, and cherish it with steady heat until, through dissolution, it passes into alteration and another color begins to arise—namely black, though not entirely so, but in the manner of a dark pomegranate. By this sign, you shall judge that either form and the "heaven" are passing through alteration and generation; that a bond of love has been formed; and that a link has been made between the form converted into "heaven" and the "heaven" into the form.

Next, with the tempered <term>decoction</term><note>original: "decoctione"; the process of heating or "cooking" a substance in a fluid.</note> always continued, and as the form and the "heaven" begin to enter digestion and generation (operations which last until the less perfect stage), that black color is "mortified" <note>This refers to the *nigredo* stage, where the matter "dies" to be reborn.</note>, and by the persistence of the warmth, a white color arises. When everything is under this color, let it be a sign that the bones and nerves of the <term>philosophical offspring</term><note>original: "fœtus philosophici"; the developing alchemical Stone, envisioned as a growing embryo or fetus.</note> are joined with the third number; yet this operation lasts until the saffron color appears. When this appears, it will be a sign that the body of such an offspring is formed and complete with its organs, and begins to be prepared so that the <term>vegetative spirit</term><note>original: "spiritus vegetabilis"; the life-giving or "growing" spirit that animates the Stone.</note> may enter into it. This operation will last until the saffron color vanishes in the preparation and the red arises. When this has finally arisen, you shall judge that the vegetative soul is within the body of the offspring, and that the end of the termination of its body and soul is at hand.

Then, finally, it behooves the craftsman to count the intervening days between the beginning and the end of generation, which he will also be able to recognize by sight from the act of dissolution until completion. For twice that length of time, he must not cease in the least from administering the fire; once this space of time is finished, let him allow it to cool. Now the offspring will be found in the manner of an **egg**; once extracted and cleansed, let it be placed in a clean glass vessel and kept again in the furnace of decoction, which is a <term>dry bath</term><note>original: "balneum siccum"; a method of heating a vessel using sand or ash rather than water to provide a steady, dry heat.</note>, for six natural days, administering the fire successively in the same manner as before, so that the hand can scarcely be held in that heat without injury. Afterward, let it be extracted and preserved with the utmost care. One weight of this, projected upon two thousand in external substances, is able to generate a form similar to that from which it drew its origin. Namely, to one pound of the said <term>solvent</term><note>original: "menstrui"; in alchemy, a solvent capable of dissolving solids and extracting their essence.</note> let there be added two ounces, or two and a half, of the "form" or "forms," according to the aforementioned condition, and only a <term>drachm</term><note>A unit of weight, roughly 1/8th of an ounce.</note> of the lesser perfect substance. This continues until you see the body become round and red—if indeed the work was for the red—or if for the white, with a metallic whiteness. It must be noted, therefore, that the colors of these <term>offspring</term><note>original: "fœtuum"; alchemists frequently used the metaphor of human generation, calling the resulting substances "children" or "fetuses."</note> are diverse: that of the masculine and "greater perfect" is red; that of the feminine and "lesser perfect" is white. The colors appear first as green mixed with redness; second, saffron-yellow mixed with a splendid redness, which denotes the conjunction of the parts with their whole; third, a shining white, which is the sign of the completion of the offspring’s body; and fourth, a snow-white mixed with a honey-like color, and this denotes the entry of the <term>soul</term><note>original: "animæ"; the volatile or spiritual principle of a substance being reunited with its "body" or fixed base.</note> into its body.

Tinged with this color, the offspring is born from the mother’s womb; one part of its weight is able to multiply its own kind over three thousand parts of matter. By a third repetition, it is over three hundred thousand. Of this latter result, just as with the earlier "greater perfect," multiplication can also be performed. It should be further noted that in the <term>spagyric</term><note>original: "spagirico"; the art of separating and recombining elements to achieve purity.</note> work, there is no precise or certain determined time, for sometimes the offspring arises more quickly when the heat happens to be more vehement than is proper; sometimes it arises more slowly due to the slackening of the same, just as is seen in a human fetus.

Colors are the best indicators of this art, and by them it must be ruled. Thus, when the spagyric offspring is in dissolution and entirely liquefied, a black color begins to arise; from this, you shall judge that it is in the state of mixture and has passed through "alteration." And after the saffron color appears, you shall consider the body to be formed and complete in its members. But when the final color appears—namely, red—judge that the body has been joined with the soul. Once this is finished, the fire must be continued as has been said; the same must be understood regarding the qualities of the white colors. When these signs are best known and noted, with the greatest diligence and steady observation, the craftsman may approach the spagyric work with a cheerful spirit and without fear, and, God granting, bring it to perfection. Now that the "greater work" has been explained, let us come to the "lesser work."

->### PHILOSOPHIA ###<-

<meta>catchword: Peracta (Having been completed)</meta>

Once the end has been reached, the process must be repeated until it is fully accomplished. Once this is perceived, let the matter be **sublimated**<note>A process where a solid is heated until it turns into a vapor and then solidifies again on a cooler surface, used here to purify the substance.</note> through ashes in a vial, first with moderate heat, and finally with the heat increased gradually and successively until the whole substance ascends to the sides of the vessel. The exalted matter will then have become the **wonderful salt**<note>original: "sal admirabile"; a high-purity alchemical state.</note>, which the philosophers call the **stone** and the **sulfur of nature**. This must be softened with the **oil of the perfects**<note>Refers to oils extracted from "perfect" metals like gold or silver.</note> until it flows as easily as wax. You will then possess the medicine perfected in this way, one weight of which will transmigrate one hundred weights of **tin**<note>original: "stanni" or "sal Jovis" (Salt of Jupiter).</note>, or fifty weights of **lead**<note>original: "Saturno" (Saturn).</note>, transmuting them into a **perfect body**<note>Gold.</note> more excellent than any natural one. For the oil of the perfects possesses a fixative power over all salts extracted from imperfect ones.

Therefore, take one ounce of filings or leaves of perfect metals, which (as said elsewhere) have been **calcined**<note>Reduced to a powder through heat.</note>. From these, the humidity or **quicksilver**<note>original: "argentum vivum" (Mercury).</note> is to be extracted by the juice of the **philosophical key**<note>The chemical solvent or agent prepared in earlier steps.</note> through the artifice of liquefaction or evacuation. All the liquid evacuations should be distilled through an **alembic** using a water bath, until a viscous matter remains at the bottom like liquid, skimmed honey.

When the vessel has cooled, pour over this matter enough of the philosophical key so that it stands four fingers deep above it. Keep it in the **digestion**<note>A process of slow, steady heating to encourage chemical change.</note> of manure or a water bath for an entire natural day. Once the vessel is cooled, the part that has dissolved should be emptied out by a gentle tilting. Afterward, place the vessel with its **alembic** head still covered into the water bath to dry the matter with a slow fire. Over this, make the water and the same amount of fresh "key" float as before; finally, expose it to digestion for another day, and once the digestion is finished, empty out the dissolved portion.

This process must be repeated until the entire matter is converted into clear water. Next, place this water in digestion for eight days, from which you shall afterward extract the qualities of the **elements**. First, using the gentlest heat of a water bath, collect as much of the water as can ascend at that temperature. When the distillation ceases and the vessel has cooled, pour all the distilled liquor back onto its **dregs**<note>original: "fæces"; the solid sediment remaining at the bottom.</note>, and keep it in a closed vessel in a digestion of manure or a water bath for several days.

Afterward, distill the whole oil through ashes and a fire of iron filings, governed by **registers**<note>original: "registra"; sliding plates or dampers used to control the airflow and heat of a furnace.</note>, collecting whatever can ascend at that heat. Distill this distillate again using the heat of a water bath; that which ascends, they call **Water**, but that which remains at the bottom, they call **Air**. Pour the distilled water back onto the dregs again, and when they have stood in digestion for seven days, let them be distilled by an open fire or in sand with slow heat at first, until all the water has passed through the alembic. Afterward, having gradually increased the heat to the **fourth degree**<note>The highest level of heat in alchemical practice, often a glowing red heat.</note>, all the liquor should be driven upward until the matter at the bottom is thoroughly dried. When ground upon a marble slab, it should become an impalpable **alcohol**<note>original: "alcool"; here meaning a "triple-refined" or extremely fine powder, not a liquid.</note> or powder. Finally, distill the liquor in a water bath to separate the **Water** from the oil, which they call **Fire**.

### CHEMICAL MATTERS ###

...since that tree of life is named in an absolute sense, perhaps because it was never intended to cease; indeed, God speaks, lest by chance Adam "stretch out his hand and take also from the tree of life and eat, and live forever." <note>A reference to Genesis 3:22.</note> It is clear, therefore, that the life which could restore even eternal life to Adam through the tree of life is not the "long life" of which we have spoken. Rather, this is what the pious Father restored to his rebellious and lost son with these words: *Adam, where are you?* For He could have left the transgressor to be devoured by death right then and there; had that happened, there would only have remained for Adam a "short life," which was eventually prolonged into a "long life" by the coming of the Lord—that is the very life we have been discussing. It remains now for us to see in the following little treatise what "short life" is and where it took its origin, making our beginning from the third chapter of Genesis.

### The Duel of the Soul ###

...they have turned Jupiter into charity. The first companion of these men, Mars, had previously directed their pursuit and their Saturn <note>In this context, Saturn likely represents the foundational character or "cold" intellect, while Mars represents "heat" or drive.</note> toward this end: that they might seek dominion over others, but none over themselves. On the other hand, by the help of Jupiter, which they have now acquired, let them now strive to rule and curb their vain, ambitious, and proud appetites. In this way, they will transmute Mars—previously overbearing toward others—into the Sun <note>The Sun here represents the enlightened self-governance or the "reformed" life.</note> that dominates themselves and acts as the reformer of their own evil life. Venus also had persuaded these men to seek those riches for the fulfillment of all the appetites of the flesh. Now, instead, they constantly pursue the love of chastity and integrity, and thus they will change their lustful Venus into the most modest and chaste Moon.

If you do not sufficiently understand this, I will explain it more broadly. As soon as you feel the money-bags of greedy Mercury stimulating your imaginations, reflect upon the voluntary poverty of Christ. Against the vengeance and tyranny of Mars, oppose the patience of Christ. Against the lust of Venus, oppose the purity of the temple of God, which your heart ought to be. More briefly: against all these things, be mindful of death and resurrection. If, while desiring to do this, you are pulled back by the devil and drawn away from good meditations toward other vain and ruinous thoughts (as almost always happens), immediately speak against him using the word of our Lord Jesus: *Get away from me, Satan* <note>original: "Abi hinc à me Satana"</note>; and immediately return to good meditations. In this constant battle, overcome evil with good—that is, repel temptation with prayer. The most powerful weapons with which one must fight in this duel are prayer, through which we acquire strength and power against our enemy.

Again, so that this type of teaching may be better understood, I will repeat: Inasmuch as Saturn is the general leader of all pursuits <note>original: "studiorum"</note> and is the first, he rules the fetus in the mother's womb in the first month. Another leader is joined to him as a companion (otherwise one and the same pursuit would always be at work in all things, which would be absurd), who accompanies the first leader in the second place. In the third month, the first companion; in the fourth, the second; in the fifth, the third; in the sixth, the fourth; and in the seventh, the fifth companion.

For example, if someone has Jupiter as their second leader, their pursuit will be directed toward piety, charity, and holiness, provided that the first companion is a supporter of that inclination—such as the Sun, leading toward the kingdom of God. If it is the Moon, it will be a most constant profession of faith. On the other hand, if it is Mercury, it will be a mercenary one; if Mars, it will be contentious and cause disturbances in the church; if Venus, it will be stained by delights.

However, a pursuit ruled by Mars as leader, with the Sun as the first companion, seeks a kingdom through war. If Jupiter follows as leader, it leads to piety; if Venus, to lust; if Mercury, to greed and the increase of resources and riches; if the Moon, to the preservation of peace. A pursuit of the Sun with Jupiter as the first companion seeks a kingdom for the glory of God; if with Mars, it leads to cruelty and tyranny; if with Venus, to pleasures; if with Mercury, to the accumulation of wealth; if with the Moon, to the tranquility of the homeland. prevented by the woman, he decided that this long cloak was necessary, under which every part of his wickedness—from head to foot, that is, from the beginning to the end of the deceptions devised by him—might be hidden and covered. Furthermore, because he saw that this kind of animal was most ready to penetrate through any cracks or fissures, he believed that by this very means he could more effectively and gradually crawl into a healthy mind that was as yet conscious of no evil. See how astutely the father of <term>Sophists</term> <note>The author characterizes the Devil as the first "Sophist," one who twists language to mislead.</note> soon proposes a fallacy; through a deceitful question, he attempts to draw the poor woman into a lie herself, testing if by this assault he might make a small crack in her still-undivided integrity, and creep through it—which he did. Responding therefore, the incautious woman (who more wisely would have either kept silent or said, *"Go away, far from here"*) adds a doubled lie to the lie of the devil (concerning "every tree"). She said, "lest we touch it," and "lest perhaps we die." 

But God had not said, "thou shalt not eat of every tree"; on the contrary, He said: *Of every tree of paradise thou shalt eat.* But the wicked Sophist attempted to entice her into a lie with the bait of a lie. Furthermore, the Lord God had not forbidden them from *touching* the tree, nor did He leave them any occasion for doubting their death if they should eat; rather, He asserted it quite affirmatively, saying, *you shall surely die* <note>original: "morte moriemini," literally "by death you shall die," an emphasis on the certainty of the punishment.</note>—meaning you shall die, indeed you shall surely die. Having now made an entrance for himself through the lies brought forth on both sides, the wicked blasphemer repeats his lie and at the same time accuses God of lying:

> *By no means (he said) shall you die.*

It was as if he were saying: "The matter is not as God has persuaded you." The wicked one added further to confirm his false and sophisticated argument:

> *For God knows, that on whatever day you eat from it, your eyes will be opened, and you will be like Gods, knowing good and evil.*

First, he accuses God of envy, so that he might make the woman an enemy to God in this regard, as if He envied them the happiness of possessing divinity. Second, he tries to persuade the woman to look at the fruit with carnal eyes, so that she might be enticed to desire it by this sight; likewise, he speaks as if God were bewitching their eyes so they would not see the happiness within the fruit, in order to make them more and more disobedient to God. Third, he concludes that they should not obey, but rather put the outcome to the test. 

In no different way has the doctrine of faithless "wise men"—which has long been accustomed to captiously deceive the wits of men—first of all won authority for itself with a certain cloaked display, with a finery of garments stretched out into the long form of a serpent and putting forth a serpent-like "prudence," and then with an elegance of interspersed speech—now in English <note>original: "Latinis"</note>, soon in Greek, now in Hebrew, Chaldean, and Arabic (even though some of these men can scarcely speak their mother tongue...

To this Word alone, therefore, let us adhere, and let us embrace it in all our works and professions.

->DUELLUM ANIMI<-

...let us consider more broadly the craftiness of the <term>arch-sophist</term> <note>original: archisophistæ. A master of clever but deceptive reasoning.</note>, which he used in deceiving Eve. That sharp deceiver did not want to use his "first horn" first—that is, the same argument of pride by which he himself had fallen—reserving that for the end. Just as sophists sometimes perversely put the last things first so that they may more safely deceive minds through confusion, he had indeed, through ambition, transformed himself from an angel of light into an angel of darkness. 

Instead, he used the other "horn" from the opposite side of the circle: namely, calumny directed first against God, lying with deliberate effort. He knew the truth, yet he asks—not whether God had forbidden every tree—but rather he pretends to be ignorant, or rather frames the question through a lie, so that he might incite the "little woman" <note>original: mulierculam. A common, if patronizing, Latin diminutive for Eve in theological texts.</note>, once questioned, to a response that was also a lie. This is clear from the first words of Eve who replied, *We eat of the fruit of the trees, etc.*, as if she had said: "The matter is not as you ask, but in this way." Behold, as soon as she entered into conversation with the devil, she was infected by the calumny of the lie against God; wounded by that horn, she brought forth a double lie. For what else is calumny but a lie mixed with mockery, and vice versa?

Someone might say: "You said before that the <term>monarchy</term> <note>original: monarchia. Here referring to the singular, unified nature of Truth, which cannot be divided without becoming a lie.</note> was torn only on one side, because the slanderer could not force the human into calumny; why do you now bring forth something different?" I bring nothing but that very thing which I said before: that Adam was never reduced to calumny; rather, he confessed the pure and sheer truth to his Lord, saying: *I heard your voice and I was afraid because I was naked, and I hid myself; likewise, the woman whom you gave to me as a companion, she gave to me, and I ate.* Did he lie? Not at all, since it had happened exactly as he spoke. 

Therefore, on his part, the monarchy of truth was not torn, but remained coherent; but on Eve’s part, a way was opened through which the serpent crept in. For he knew that an entrance could not be opened through Adam's <term>ternary</term> <note>original: ternarium. The number three, often symbolizing the soul or a divine balance in Hermetic thought.</note> while the <term>unary</term> <note>original: unarium. The number one, symbolizing unity and God.</note> protected the ternary. Therefore, he tried to enter through Eve's <term>binary</term> <note>original: binarium. The number two, symbolizing division, duality, and the start of multiplicity/falling away from the One.</note>, so that he might carry this out through the likeness of the "first number of multitude and confusion"; for like things are attracted to like things more easily than to unlike things.

Again it will be asked: since Eve was created perfect, how could she be led astray? For it is foreign to all perfection to fall. We shall answer through another question by way of comparison; when this has been answered exactly, we shall answer even more clearly than now. How, then, did it happen that the angel of light, who was created far more perfect, even in the incorruptible heaven, should have fallen, when he had no occasion for it, and no one persuading him? Therefore, we must be most careful, O brothers, against false imaginations, lest they persuade us of those things which are outside the monarchy of truth. For this reason, certain examples of Holy Scripture were to be set before you, with which you might be armed, and become more vigilant and cautious in repelling the snares...

...of the devil, which you now perceive better than before through your imaginations and thoughts, through which he strives to sneak in like a thief and a robber into your <term>monarchy of truth and simplicity</term> <note>original: veritatis atque simplicitatis monarchiam. When, having already fled to the sacred scriptures, you catch this to be a lie of the devil once again, as before; for it is written: *In the day that you eat of it, you shall surely die,* and previously: *Eat from every tree, but from the tree of knowledge you shall not eat.* Behold, once the second lie is detected, let that persuader of lies be driven away, as before.

Just look more closely, feed your eyes, consider how delightful the sight of that apple is; carefully..."

### ->DUEL OF THE SOUL<- ###

Look very closely. With this gaze, the <term>basilisk</term> <note>original: basilisci. A mythical serpent king said to kill with its gaze; used here as a metaphor for the devil’s initial tempting look.</note> strives to pour its poison into the heart. If the poison reaches the heart, your life is in imminent danger. Therefore, fleeing to the Sanctuary, let us turn the Word of God over in our souls, so that we may turn our eyes away and not behold vanity. When the enemy cannot win in this way, he will soon return and bring something new, more virulent than the rest, such as this: *And you shall be like gods, knowing good and evil.* <note>original: Et eritis tanquam Dij scientes bonum & malum. A quote from Genesis 3:5, the serpent’s promise to Eve.</note> Now at last he uses his "first horn," which he knows and has experienced within himself to be the most effective of all temptations—the very one through which he fell into the <term>crime of treason against Divine Majesty</term> <note>original: crimen læsæ divinæ Majestatis. A legal term for high treason, applied here to the devil's rebellion against God's authority.</note>. For he was not content with that happiness with which God had graced him—namely, the sight of God, the enjoyment of His glory, and the supreme good—but instead he wished to be God himself. He had already experienced how detestable it is before God to crave that which belongs to God alone. 

Therefore, as the ultimate torment for the souls of men, he reserves **ambition**; of all vices, it is both the most persuasive and the most destructive. Having struck a lethal wound to the hearts of men with this first horn, he inflicts a second wound with the "second horn"—namely, **brutality**. By this, he now strips away all reason and mind from men, rendering them far more irrational than beasts, so that they no longer recognize God or themselves. Thus it happens that, once enslaved to the devil, they are easily carried wherever he drags them without resistance. 

At this stage, unless the mercy of God comes to the rescue, the wretched, ambitious man is in danger of being struck by the "final horn"—namely, **divorce from his Creator** (may it be far from us)—by this four-horned beast, and his salvation may be despaired of. See, I pray you, excellent reader, how dangerous it is to fall, through one’s own inclination, into the impressions of the "infernal stellar influences," and how profitable and necessary it is to have learned **Celestial Astrology**. <note>The author distinguishes between "infernal astrology" (demonic influence on the temperament) and "celestial astrology" (a spiritual understanding of divine order and the soul's inclinations).</note> Let others mock this study, for they have already experienced the wounds of the horn of brutality; but you, if you are wise, pull your foot back immediately from the "broad road" that leads to hell, lest you be unable to do so even with later effort. 

Let these things be said seriously to you and to all, even if they are despised by most as frivolous and ridiculous—as if they were uttered by "asses" (as they call them). The **donkey** has carried many sacred secrets, of which Christ—the source and origin of all secrets—did not deem the mules and she-mules worthy. We do not disdain this name: for we would rather enter the New Jerusalem riding upon a young donkey with our leader Christ, than be led upon the most decorated mules to eternal punishments. 

Therefore, friend reader, so that you may learn to beware of the <term>rejected binary</term> <note>original: reprobato binario. In Pythagorean and mystical thought, the number two (the binary) represents division, duality, and the fall away from the "One" or Unity of God.</note> and its offspring, the **quaternary**, in all things both supernatural and natural, we must now demonstrate more extensively how widely this imperfection has sown its seeds. One can see throughout the universe how this serpent has attempted to creep in. Truly, having been excluded from the **Unity** of the eternal heaven and cast out from the **Ternary** (Trinity) of the incorruptible created heaven, he fell into the **quaternary** and elementary region, which he has most miserably corrupted, and strives to corrupt more and more every day.

### ->WITH THE BODY<- ###

We have said before that the world was created with order, and that this consists of three things: namely, **number, measure, and weight** <note>original: numero, mensura, & pondere. A reference to the Wisdom of Solomon 11:20: "But thou hast arranged all things by measure and number and weight."</note>; which God, for our instruction, wished to use as instruments. Therefore, beginning from numbers, we say that all numbers are completed in the **ternary** <note>the number three</note>, and in it is the most absolute end of all numbers. For when the ternary is reflected into itself, it produces through generation the **novenary** <note>the number nine (3x3)</note>, beyond which it is not permitted to progress in numbers; rather, one must return to **unity** <note>the number one</note>, through which the "second unity" of the numbers of the second order arises. This same thing is seen to happen when the first three numbers—2, 3, and 4—are added together, for they also provide that same absolute completion <note>2 + 3 + 4 = 9</note>. From this, one can see how the ternary is the most excellent of all numbers.

By contrast, let us examine the **binary** <note>the number two</note> imperfection. The binary, through its own reproduction by generation, produces the **quaternary** <note>the number four (2x2)</note>, which is indeed a long distance from the completion of numbers. And although some might wish that completion to exist in the quaternary—since they say that by the accumulation of the first four numbers, the **denary** <note>the number ten (1+2+3+4=10)</note> is made—the contrary is quite clear. For the denary is surpassed by the quaternary <note>as a base for addition</note>, as is evident from the aggregation of the first numbers 2, 3, 4, and 5 <note>2 + 3 + 4 + 5 = 14</note>. For the **Unit** <note>original: Unarius; the number one</note> is not a number, nor is it to be counted among them; but if those committing a mathematical error do so in this manner—1, 2, 3, 4—to fashion the denary, we nevertheless deny that the denary is the completion of numbers through generation. Indeed, by this path, that offspring surpasses the denary twice over through the quaternary.

And although by progressing beyond the denary a return to unity occurs, one should not think for that reason that unity puts on multitude or composition because it is found in a series of composite things. For it is there for the reduction of composite things into simplicity and purity, just as the center exists in a circle. In the **vigenary** <note>the number twenty</note>, however, it is not so; rather, the binary is the center of the vigenary for the purpose of fabricating the **monomachia** <note>original: monomachiam; a "single combat" or duel, likely referring to the title of the work</note> placed above. Yet in the **centenary** <note>one hundred</note> and the **millenary** <note>one thousand</note>, and those similar to them, unity again presents itself as the center. These things are especially to be noted, because they are of the highest necessity for the **spagyric art** <note>original: spagiricam; the alchemical process of separating and recombining the essence of materials, often used in medicine</note>. 

The ancient prophets would have spoken better had they said that the completion of every number through the unit alone is in the ternary, rather than in the quaternary. We do not deny that the quaternary can rest in the ternary to form the **philosophical hebdomad** <note>original: hebdomadis philosophicæ; the "philosophical seven," referring to the seven planets, metals, or stages of the Great Work</note>, of which we made ample mention above. But this cannot happen before it strips away the nature of its parent, the binary, making a transition through the ternary to the simplicity of unity, and thereafter to the "adept philosophy." 

All **even numbers** are considered formal and **masculine**, whose father is the ternary; but **odd numbers** are **feminine** and material, whose mother is the binary <note>This is an unusual reversal of traditional Pythagorean numerology, where odd numbers were typically considered male and even numbers female</note>. If there lies hidden any secret in the binary—other than in its reduction, as stated above, into its quaternary through the ternary to the simplicity of unity, which might serve the promotion of the study of hidden truth—let it be brought forward and...

...and we will listen with a cheerful mind: meanwhile, however, we shall proceed to our purpose. This subject of ours, which we are now discussing, is a triple **ternary** <note>the number three</note>, categorized as natural, artificial, and supernatural. Furthermore, the natural is either simple or composite: while the artificial is decomposed, or moral, or supernatural; the latter usually follows the artificial, and sometimes precedes it. The simple does not allow for composition, because it is pure and separated from the composite. The composite ternary receives the **quaternary** <note>the number four</note>, yet it does not mix well with it except through the removal of its own **binary** <note>the number two, representing division or duality</note>; once this is overcome, it becomes the **septenary** <note>the number seven (3 + 4 = 7)</note>. The decomposed is made by the <term>spagyric</term> <note>alchemical; the art of separating and recombining elements</note> art through every kind of separation of the binary, bringing it into union with the septenary. The moral ternary is made through the scale of meditative philosophy previously established. The supernatural, however, is a gift of God, and rests in the union of the mind. The hinge of this whole mystery turns upon the rejection of the binary: only then does the ternary, joined to the quaternary, cause the latter to rest in the former through the septenary. When the ternary is restored to this, one arrives at the likeness of unity in the revolution of the **denary** <note>the number ten (completing the cycle)</note>, which lies hidden under the form of a center (as we have said), as much in natural things as in any others, and in the supernatural.

Thus far, enough has been said concerning the order of the world through numbers; now let us come to the order of measure. We said very recently that in numbers, the **unarium** <note>unity or the number one</note> is the center of the ternary and of its offspring—namely the **novenary** <note>the number nine (3x3)</note>—just as a point is in a circle. Therefore, the fountain and origin of the first measure is the center; for if a point flows from it in a straight line until it rests, it becomes a straight line. If that line is carried around by the aforementioned moving point while the center remains unmoved until it returns to its place, it becomes a circle and an image of the triad in unity, or of a monarchy. That same straight line precisely measures the circle into a perfect hexagon, which, by alternating angles, outlines the figure of a ternary, and a progressing equilateral **trigon** <note>a triangle</note> from that perfection. Furthermore, it should be noted that the center is the unity and its circle is the ternary; whatever, however, is inserted between the center and the enclosed monarchy must be considered as the binary, whether it be another circle, a triangle, or any other figure. By what way the binary, made from an angel at the beginning, became a devil, let us contemplate through the allegory of measure. I said recently that the shadowy angel had fashioned for himself a pair of compasses, of which one leg was revolving ambition, and the other was calumny. And when he tried to fix calumny, he circled for so long until he reached a semi-ternary figure; then at last ambition turned into calumny, and calumny passed into ambition, from which resulted the binary under the figure of a serpent raising four double horns. ...this instrument <note>referring to the fallen angel or adversary mentioned previously</note> vigorously resumed his work, testing if he could somehow manage this time to build a monarchy better than the previous one. Accordingly, taking his starting point from the aforementioned destruction, he approached the matter through **intersections**. He fixed both feet of a **compass** <note>a tool for drawing circles, used here as a metaphor for the geometry of creation</note>: one in **brutality**, the other in **divorce** <note>original: "divortium"; here meaning separation or discord</note>. And while he circled with the foot of brutality until he had marked a little more than a third of the circle, the foot of divorce moved from its place; by its growing slipperiness, it deceived its craftsman and yielded from the center. Thus it happened that the foot of brutality was called back by that wicked craftsman to its place, from where it had first proceeded, and it took the place of the center; meanwhile, the foot of divorce made an intersection similar to the first, following the **first intersection of Euclid’s first book** <term>Euclidean intersection</term> <note>referring to Euclid's Elements, Book 1, Prop. 1, which describes how to draw an equilateral triangle by intersecting two circles</note>. Yet this very thing happened this time with the foot of **calumny** <note>slander or false accusation</note> as happened with the foot of divorce: namely, it deceived the architect of wickedness by also slipping from its place. The result was that three points were left concluding nothing: one at the intersection, and the other two at the extremities of the **serpents** <note>likely referring to the curved lines of the failed circles</note> intersecting each other again.

And when the wicked craftsman saw that he had been deceived twice already, and had accomplished nothing more than before, he decided to try as a **lion roaring with rage** <note>a biblical reference to 1 Peter 5:8, describing the devil</note>, seeking a **ternary** <note>a group of three</note> to devour. He traveled in a circuit, repeating those heard-of intersections: the result was that through three intersections he fixed three points, and six in total; four through the intersections, the remaining two at the divided extremes, and **eight serpents**. Yet even so, that most wicked corrupter of all crafts was able to bring none of these things either to a square surface or to a solid cube. For his entire structure lacked any **center**, without which nothing perfect, solid, or stable can ever exist in the whole nature of things.

We conclude, therefore, that the devil is "by accident" <note>a philosophical term meaning a non-essential or external quality</note> without a center; that is, without the **Word of God**, *without whom nothing was made that has been made* <note>original: "sine quo factum est nihil quod factum est"; a quote from John 1:3</note>. For God alone can make something out of nothing, and the best out of the weak, and likewise all that is from that which is not—and this solely through His **Word**, which is the supernatural center of all virtue and all truth in all things. Through the corruption of his own **ternary** (under which the angel was created from the beginning), that adversary tried to tear apart and divide the monarchy of the **human ternary** <note>the triune nature of man: body, soul, and spirit</note> into a **quaternary figure** <note>the number four, often associated by these authors with the material, corruptible world</note> of this kind, with four intersections and eight serpents intersecting in pairs. This resulted in so many and such horrid parts that they were irreparable due to the lack of a center. Yet he was not able to fully accomplish this, because he was not permitted to erase the remnant of the **center of truth** in **Adam**, despite the introduction of calumny and the lie toward which he had drawn **Eve**.

Therefore, the almighty and merciful God, taking pity on the distressed misery and calamitous state of both Adam and Eve, decreed to erase the scattered mark of perdition that had been introduced—which was then clinging together by only a tiny little point—and to restore it into His own whole monarchy. He did this by restoring this tiny point into a **center**, which is the true character and the most certain mark of our salvation, situated in the Word of God.

### ->THE DUEL OF THE SOUL<- ###

Therefore, it will be necessary to establish the center of the **single combat** <note>original: *monomachia*; a duel or one-on-one contest, here used as a metaphor for the struggle for spiritual center</note> in this manner: From the individual intersections looking at each other across the diameter, always skipping two as you go around, let three diagonal lines be drawn. In the point of their intersection, you will find the true center that is sought. Now, so that I may clearly demonstrate to you the image of the reduction of the **ternary** <note>the number three</note> to the simplicity of unity by the rejection of the **binary** <note>the number two, representing division or duality</note>, and also by what logic the **quaternary** <note>the number four</note> can rest within the ternary through conjunction and become a partaker of union with it, take note:

From each intersection, draw straight lines to the next. In this way, you will have a quaternary of equilateral triangles: one of which is enclosed by the other three, yet none of them has life or a center except for the one in the middle, because in a monarchy there cannot be multiple centers, nor more than one life. Do you see now the quaternary enclosed within the ternary, yet not yet resting in the true **philosophical week** <term>philosophical hebdomad</term> <note>original: *hebdomas philosophica*; referring to the sacred number seven, often representing the completion of a stage in alchemy or creation</note> about which I recently spoke twice? 

Therefore, so that it may be reduced along with the ternary to the simplicity of unity, the ternary must be entirely cast aside in this way: From the center of the whole ternary, let a straight line be drawn to any of the three cones <note>points or vertices</note> of the great triangle. Mentally understand this line to be revolved from its furthest end, while remaining fixed at the other end in the center. Then, whatever points and lines exist, abolish and erase them through that revolution until it returns to where its motion began. Now, no binary, no ternary, and even no quaternary of the circle will appear in the monarchy; rather, the quaternary now rests and lies hidden in the ternary, and together with it, rejoices under unity—though it is not visible to external eyes, but only to the mind. 

Only the remaining line of the semi-diameter is seen, which is the **remnant of the apple** <note>original: *pomi reliquum*; a play on the fruit of the Fall and the geometric radius</note>. Because of this, we must fight manfully, and not weakly, against the daily single combat of the "counter-clever" serpent while we cling to this fleeting life, lest we fall back into the same offense as our two first parents, having forgotten them.

Behold, excellent reader, you now have the idea of the **monarchy of the triad in unity** <note>the Trinity</note>, depicted by me and placed before your eyes. By penetrating this more deeply than the letter or the picture suggests through the sharp edge of your mind, you will recognize whatever pertains to the **spagyric art** <term>spagirica</term> <note>alchemical medicine involving the separation and recombination of plant or mineral essences</note> and **adept philosophy** <term>adeptam philosophiam</term> <note>the highest form of alchemical or mystical knowledge attained by an 'adept'</note>, aided by those things I have recently revealed to you in this little work. It shall not be my fault if you do not fare well in this matter, provided you do not begrudge yourself the happiness of understanding these secrets through laziness or sluggishness. These secrets are necessary above all others in this life because, through the admiration of the **mighty works of God** <note>original: *magnalia Dei*</note>, they lead one as if by the hand to a true knowledge of Him; indeed, they draw one into His love. In this love lies the highest good of Christians, and it stands open only to those believing in God through the Word, the center of truth, His Son, in whom and through whom all things exist. To Him alone, with the Father and the Holy Spirit, be praise, honor, and glory forever.
