### THE VIRTUES OF THE OIL OF COMMON SALT

<margin>Salt excites thirst, but its oil soothes or composes it.</margin>
A single drop of this, in which gold has been dissolved or from which **potable gold** <note>original: "aurum potabile," a legendary alchemical medicine consisting of gold in a drinkable liquid state</note> has been made, overcomes all illnesses that can possibly be imagined, even those closest or bordering on death. A single drop of this oil and of **vitriol** <note>original: "vitrioli," likely sulfuric acid or a metallic sulfate</note> made through the water of dew, when administered with **water of life** <note>original: "aqua vitae," concentrated distilled spirits or ethanol</note>, has sustained and caused to rise again one who was already in the final throes of death. Furthermore, whatever things are smeared with this oil and are of a putrid nature—as happens in wounds or other pains—it erodes and consumes within a single hour. In contrast, common salt encourages every putrid thing so that it is not consumed, and it is sharp. Furthermore, salt excites thirst; however, the oil drives it away, to which fact several **dropsy** <note>original: "hydropici," referring to those suffering from edema or fluid retention</note> patients are witnesses, who after taking it were free of thirst for nine and often ten days. Finally, as far as the taste is concerned, the oil is not as acidic as salt, but greatly resembles the sweetness of honey or the juice of wild apples. Used externally, the oil of salt mixed with oil of turpentine, wax, chamomile, mullein, and similar substances, remarkably calms **gouty pains** <note>original: "dolores podagricos"</note>, disperses **tophi** <note>original: "tophos," chalky deposits of uric acid in the joints</note>, restores convulsed limbs if they are rubbed with it, heals abscesses, and cures **hernias** <note>original: "ramices"</note>. It is given by mouth drop by drop, especially that which is of a purple or lemon-yellow color, and is provided through dew-water for dissolving gold and curing infinite diseases. Taken in the amount of three drops with water of life every week, it renovates a person and consumes **subcutaneous water** <note>another reference to dropsy</note>; it disperses the **falling sickness** <note>original: "morbum comitialem," or epilepsy</note>, drives away fevers, and heals **jaundice** <note>original: "arquatum"</note>. The same is effective for ulcers which are called **malignant** <note>original: "cacoëthe," from the Greek for "bad habit" or "malice," used for stubborn, cancerous ulcers</note>, as well as **corroding ulcers** <note>original: "phagedenas"</note> of the genitals, spreading sores, and purulent ears; it removes dimness of the eyes, scars, and **white spots** <note>original: "albugines," or leukoma of the cornea</note>.

### ON THE BRINE OF COMMON SALT

The **brine** <note>original: "brodium," a decoction or salt-liquor</note> of salt is effective against dysentery; let it be given in an enema. Likewise against herpes and spreading ulcers, tumors of the breasts, sciatica, and the afterbirth. When milk curdles in the breasts, it reduces it by fomenting and protects the milk so that it does not curdle in the breasts by means of warmed linens soaked and placed on top. Whoever has worms in the belly should drink the salt brine. Whoever has a bruising of blood from blows is cured by a sponge moistened in salt brine, applied as a fomentation several times a day, either hot or lukewarm, to the **congealed area**. The same fomentation promotes health in any part. Drunk and gargled, it expels **leeches** <note>original: "sanguisugas"</note> if someone had accidentally swallowed one, but it must be drunk slowly in distinct portions and times. Likewise, when sprinkled, it kills fleas living in rooms and chambers. Likewise, when used as a fomentation, it keeps a protruding "single-eye" <note>likely referring to a prolapsed or bulging eye</note> inside so that it does not slip out further; it preserves and protects against worms and moths.

What is there (I ask) in this subject that is not worthy of wonder? Consider the conjunction of prepared salt with its incombustible agent, which does not cease from action until it is reduced into a better form. Likewise, consider the salt, meltable by itself, penetrating and converting its whole body into the **Green Lion** <note>original: "Leonem viridem," an alchemical term for a potent, acidic mineral state, often associated with vitriol or the raw "matter" of the Great Work</note> and into a permanent oil. Its spirit dissolves all bodies; I shall report more things concerning this same subject in another place. I will add this one thing: Take the bark of the Sea <note>original: "corticem Maris," likely a poetic or alchemical reference to sea salt or the crust of the mineral</note> and no other; let it be purified, and placed in glass with our vinegar for 15 days, buried in a fermenting heat <note>original: "ventre præliantis," literally "the belly of the one battling," likely referring to the heat of a digestion furnace or fermenting manure</note>. Distill the oil, and repeat for as long as it takes until it becomes the **Green Lion**. By this secret remedy, you shall radically remove **gout** <note>original: "podagram"</note>; it is applied safely both internally and externally. — B. PORTU. <note>Referring to Bernard Gilles Penot, a well-known 16th-century alchemist and physician.</note>

## ON THE BRINE OF SALT FROM OLIVES.

For anyone whose gums in the mouth have become loose, the brine of the saltiness in which olives are preserved, held often in the mouth, constricts the washed throat and gums again. Likewise, it drives away **dandruff** <note>original: "porrigines"</note> when washed frequently, as well as skin eruptions, lichens, burns, and it extinguishes **St. Anthony’s Fire** <note>original: "ignem sacrum," a skin infection now known as erysipelas</note>. Against worms in the ears, figs boiled with the brine of salt and crushed in the manner of a plaster are effective when applied. Against pustules: take the brine, mix it with wine vinegar and gargle; afterward wash the mouth with the wine itself, then with honey or **mead** <note>original: "hydromelle"</note>, and finally with water. For frostbitten limbs and soles of the feet, wash with the brine of salt; afterward cook lentils with the brine of salt, mix them together with bread crusts or crumbs and enough oil of roses to make a plaster to be applied. He who eats raw coriander should drink a fresh egg shaken well in a vial with salt brine while warm; this removes the poison. Likewise, it lessens the pains from an excess of milk in this way: let lentils be boiled very well in salt brine, with which brine you should bathe the breasts; afterward, pound and grind the lentils and apply as a plaster twice a day. Likewise, the brine of salt from olives heals pustules, and once the **gangrene** <note>original: "gangræna"</note> is removed and the mouth washed frequently with the same brine, it cures rot of the mouth. When the mouth and swollen gums are washed, it consumes the overgrowths of flesh.

## ON OXALMA OR SOUR BRINE.

Oxalma or sour brine is made thus: Take salt, water, and vinegar (or equal parts salt brine and vinegar), mix them, and it is effective against the bites of vipers, spiders, snakes, and dogs, as well as herpes and consuming wounds, when washed and bathed with the **oxalma** <note>a classical mixture of vinegar and brine</note> or sour brine. Thus it stops wounds dripping with blood. When a hernia has been removed, or for a stone of the bladder, immediately pour in oxalma; use oxalma when a "one-eye" <note>original: "monoculo," possibly referring to a specific surgical tool or a type of fistula</note> emerges. Likewise, it is used against putrefying wounds. Also, if **leeches** <note>original: "hirundines," literally "swallows," but in a medical context regarding water, it almost certainly refers to "hirudines" or leeches</note> are swallowed by accident...

## ON SALT AMMONIAC.

A broth <note>original: "brodium," a liquid extract or brine</note> of salt ammoniac <note>original: "Sal armoniacum," usually referring to ammonium chloride</note>, when swallowed, heals dysentery and abdominal cramps arising from a cold nature; it purges by warming <note>original: "fomentando"</note>. When drunk, it loosens [the bowels], yet when used with enemas, it binds them. If swallowed frequently by those with dropsy <note>edema or fluid retention</note> or those burdened with cold phlegm <note>original: "pituita," one of the four bodily humors</note>, it not only purges the phlegm and water but even consumes them. The same water, when drunk and gargled, brings out leeches and all kinds of worms from the throat and mouth, killed. The same, when used as a gargle, raises the uvula and reduces its swelling. It kills skin eruptions <term>impetigines: inflammatory, crusting skin diseases</term> and cures whitlow <term>panaritium: an infection of the fingertip or nail bed</term> through washing and rubbing. It treats ulcers and decay of the mouth through gargling; stones of the kidneys and bladder by drinking; and cures paralysis caused by cold, St. Anthony's Fire <term>Erysipelas: a bacterial skin infection</term>, gout <term>podagra</term>, and spasms. It strengthens all limbs and the nerves from which gout arises. It cleanses the womb <note>original: "Matricem"</note> and soothes pains caused by coldness, as well as swellings of the private parts arising from cold and moisture, and those of the whole body and feet; likewise, it eases headaches.

## ON NITRE AND ITS VIRTUES.

Properly prepared powder of nitre <note>original: "Nitrum," likely saltpeter or potassium nitrate</note> is very useful for all people. For adults, take one dram <note>original: "drachma," a unit of weight approximately 3.9 grams</note> with an equal amount of sugar in wine, or without sugar with mead <note>original: "mulsa"</note> in beer, or in the juice or water of parsley or strawberries with a decoction of the aforementioned herbs, as available. It can also be taken with other suitable herbs according to a person's temperament <note>original: "complexione," the balance of the four humors</note> and will, in the morning for 10 or 12 continuous days. For smaller or weaker people, take a half-dram without pain. In tiny infants of two, three, or four years, one may use a sixteenth part—that is, a quarter of a dram—without any fear. It expels stones from the kidneys and every corrupt matter and internal humor collected from viscous foods, from which sand is often generated and grows. This can be recognized thus: let the urine of the one urinating be strained through a certain linen cloth; the sand and stones will be seen lying upon that linen cloth. Those who have suffered from painful urination <term>dysuria: difficulty or pain when passing urine</term> for several days should use this same powder four times a day, beginning in the morning and then every three hours. If anyone's passage <note>original: "canaliculus," likely the urethra</note> is closed or obstructed, then a small wax candle <note>an early medical sound or bougie used for clearing blockages</note> treated with butter should be inserted into the ca- <meta>catchword: -nalicu (canal)</meta>

### PREPARATION OF BLACK SALT
### against pleurisy.

Take: Saltpeter 5 lbs, Raw Tartar 1 lb. Let them be distilled through a sixth alembic <note>a type of still used in distillation; the "sixth" likely refers to a specific size or sequence in the laboratory</note>. The dose is 1 scruple <term>℈: a unit of weight equal to 1/24th of an ounce</term> up to 1 and a half scruples. It should be administered in good spring water or the best wine in the morning, around noon, in the evening, and around midnight; for it must be administered frequently so that the urine may be purged. **Addition:** Take: 2 ounces of this, 5 scruples of Aqua Regis <term>King's Water: a highly corrosive mixture of acids, here likely diluted</term>, 5 ounces of dried spirit of wine <note>original: "Alcool vini exiccati"</note>. Let a mixture be made. The dose is from 5 drachms <term>ʒ: a unit of weight</term> to 1 drachm. **For cavernous ulcers, a preparation of the same:** Take: Nitric alum 5 lbs, spring water 2 lbs. Let them be distilled into a water. **Addition:** Take: water of plantain, celandine, and oak leaves, 5 lbs of each. For pleurisy, 1 scruple is given in warm wine.

### COMPOSITION OF THE TRAVELERS' SALT, WHICH
### strengthens the stomach, aids digestion, and 
### preserves against putrefaction.

<margin>So that no one vomits at sea.</margin>
Take: Saltpeter, fused salt, and rock salt <note>original: "salis gemmæ"</note>, 1 ounce of each. Galangal, mace, and cubebs <note>warm, aromatic spices used to settle the stomach</note>, 1 scruple of each. Let a powder be made. The dose is 4 grains on an empty stomach in the morning. Whoever uses this salt while sailing at sea will not vomit.

### PREPARATION OF THE 
### Travelers' Salt.

Take 4 ounces of this salt, 5 lbs of dried spirit of wine; let the Alkali salt be extracted. Take 2 ounces of this, and 1 ounce of distilled liquor of juniper berries; reduce it into a compound. The dose is one grain in the best wine; nothing else should be added, otherwise it loses the virtue of the salt. This is its preparation in addition, which Hermes <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary ancient sage and mythical founder of alchemy</note> held in the greatest esteem for the preservation of a long life.

### ON THE SALT OF VITRIOL AND
### its powers.

<margin>The stomach is healed by oil of vitriol and lethal diseases are cured.</margin>
Salt of Vitriol <term>vitrioli: a sulfate of certain metals, such as iron or copper, used here as a potent medicinal salt</term>, if it be rightly and well prepared, is an excellent medicine for purging all those who have a hard, heavy, or painful stomach, and for curing chronic and lethal diseases arising from an abundance of food and drink—as often happens to soldiers and others who live an inordinate life. From this also come dysentery, fevers, and quinsy <term>anginæ: severe inflammation of the throat that hinders breathing</term>; and they are even forced to die at last...

### ADDITION.

The more salts are dissolved, filtered, and purified, the more they lose their foul odor <note>original: "fœtore"</note> and the more strength they acquire.

# ON ANTIMONY AND ITS POWERS.

Many doctors of medicine believe that <term>Antimony</term> <note>A metallic element often considered poisonous in its raw state, but championed by alchemical physicians as a "master" medicine when purified</note> is a poison. If indeed it is a poison, then <term>Dioscorides</term> <note>An ancient Greek physician and author of *De Materia Medica*</note> did wrong by using it in <term>collyria</term> <note>medicated eye salves</note>; and <term>Arnald of Villanova</term> and <term>Nicolaus Myrepsus</term> did wrong when they used it in a castor-based antidote against vertigo, paralysis, and stroke. Likewise, <term>Antonius Schneberg</term>, in his catalog of simple medicines against the plague, wrongly teaches that it can be taken safely in small quantities if prepared in the chemical manner. <term>Mattioli</term> <note>Pietro Andrea Mattioli, a famous 16th-century Italian physician and botanist</note> also praises it wrongly, and the doctors of Bologna act wrongly as well, for they clearly use it in melancholic diseases. Yet it is certain that these men are prudent, learned, and experienced in the art of healing, and they do not use anything rashly.

<margin>
*Praises of the flowers of antimony.*
</margin>
<margin>
*To reveal secrets to the ignorant and unskillful: this is to increase their audacity.*
</margin>
Mattioli says that it resists the poison of the plague; likewise, it drives away <term>tertian, quartan, and daily fevers</term> <note>types of recurring fevers often associated with malaria</note>, and benefits those laboring with stomach complaints or <term>celiac distress</term> <note>referring generally to abdominal or intestinal disorders</note>, for it purges the stomach of corrupt humors. Therefore, it is a health-giving medicine by the authority of Georgius Gallus of Schneeberg, the Bolognese doctors, Dioscorides, and Myrepsus. The reason is that it expels poisons. What is more excellent than the <term>Flowers of Antimony</term> <note>A white vapor or powder produced by heating antimony, used as a powerful purge or emetic</note>? What is sweeter than its oil? What is more successful, praiseworthy, and useful than its extracted essence? The use of these is far to be preferred over those poisonous and raw medicines: <term>scammony</term>, <term>spurge</term>, <term>colocynth</term>, <term>turbith</term>, and <term>agaric</term> <note>all harsh, plant-based laxatives common in medieval pharmacy</note>. For its purging is through the bowels <note>original: "per secessum"</note>, cleansing the person and, above all other secrets, uprooting and removing any impurity from the human body, cleansing it from all ailments. <term>Paracelsus</term> <note>The famous Swiss-German physician who revolutionized medicine with chemistry</note> says that if you find this medicine—or rather, this secret—do not give it to anyone unskillful; for no one can enumerate the powers hidden within it against all ailments. But such preparations must be made chemically, which those doctors are ignorant of who, fleeing at the time of the plague, are like the <term>Levites</term> <note>A reference to the Parable of the Good Samaritan: those who saw the suffering man and passed by on the other side</note> of whom Christ speaks in the New Testament, who disparage me and other good men as they pass by. Truly, in this province and other places, I have cured many whom the doctors, after holding counsel, had despaired of: specifically those with strokes, celiac distress, those infected by the plague, epileptics, and those bent over by certain <term>contractions</term> <note>possibly referring to muscle spasms or limb deformities</note>; likewise those who for four years had knobby knees and other knotted limbs, even ulcerated legs and many other defects, as well as those wounded and pierced through; also the insane, even those who had been mad for nearly three years.

<margin>
*The administration of prepared antimony.*
</margin>
The dose of antimony is this: certainly, at the beginning of an onset of the <term>falling sickness</term> <note>epilepsy</note>, nine grains should be given; after the paroxysm <note>the peak of the seizure or fit</note>...

Likewise, it cures <term>apoplexy</term> <note>a sudden loss of consciousness, similar to a stroke</note> and other brain afflictions. It removes <term>alopecia</term> <note>hair loss</note>, greatly corrects the craving for food or appetite, assists the joints and limbs, expels <term>sand</term> <note>calculi or "gravel" in the kidneys and bladder</note>, and opposes asthma and other chest ailments born from thick and phlegmatic humors. It aids the <term>stunned disease</term> <note>original: "Morbo attonito," likely referring to catalepsy or sudden seizure</note>, repairs lost hearing, and heals the ringing, pain, and deafness of the ears. It expels both types of bile <note>Yellow and black bile, according to the four humors theory</note> from the whole body, breaks stones, purges the head and brain, and benefits those with the <term>comitial disease</term> <note>original: "comitialibus," a historical term for epilepsy</note>; likewise, with five grains of the essence of hellebore, it heals convulsions. Taken with <term>aqua vitæ</term> <note>original: "water of life," usually a strong distilled alcohol or brandy</note>, it comforts the heart, soothes toothache, drives away facial spots and "winds" from deep within the body, cures <term>migraines</term> <note>original: "hemicraniam"</note>, and dispels dropsy within a few days with 3 or 4 grains taken with a half-drachm <note>represented by ʒ ß</note> of theriac. It helps obstructions of the liver, cures jaundice, intestinal pains, and erosions, strengthens the joints, generates joy, and restores health to lepers: for it is the greatest <term>arcanum</term> <note>a secret, powerful alchemical remedy</note> for leprosy, and nothing more effective than its oil can be found; it rectifies the spleen, soothes pain of the womb, promotes menstruation, and preserves its vigor, cures <term>morphea</term> <note>a skin condition causing discolored patches</note>, softens the hardness of nerves, and opens blockages. It makes the breath smell sweet, cleanses the chest and lungs, aids those with <term>gout</term> <note>original: "podagricis"</note>, warms the kidneys, soothes pains and heals their hardness, benefits spasms, and expels cold humor; it drives away flatulent spirits from deep in the body, dissolves <term>strangury</term> <note>painful or restricted urination</note>, and finally assists the <term>consumptive</term> <note>original: "tabidis," those suffering from wasting diseases</note> who cough up pus, preserves the chest against all harm, softens hard tumors, and is effective against bodily weakness: a half-drachm of <term>Diambra</term> <note>an aromatic medicinal powder containing ambergris and spices</note> with 3 grains of essentified antimony is for arousing the native heat and refreshing those who are tormented by the cold. Likewise, used externally, it heals cancerous sores, all scars, <term>elephantiasis</term> <note>often used in this era to describe the most severe form of leprosy</note>, fistulas, <term>herpes</term> <note>here referring to spreading skin rashes generally</note>, <term>lupus</term> <note>literally "the wolf," a term for skin ulcers that "eat" the flesh</note>, all scabies, <term>phthisis</term> <note>wasting disease, here appearing as a skin affliction</note>, and wonderfully heals all skin defects; the same is the highest remedy for malignant ulcers, and it separates the flesh of malignant and putrid ulcers from the living tissue without pain. Likewise, [it soothes] the pains of wounds...

### PARACELSUS ON THE USE OF ANTIMONY.

Its <term>tincture</term> <note>an alcoholic extract of a substance</note> is prepared such that in a cask of fresh wine in the month of September or October, five <term>ounces</term> <note>represented by the symbol ℥; approximately 140 grams</note> of this tincture should be poured into about twenty measures [of wine], and allowed to digest and be purified together with the wine. Let the sick person drink of this wine for three, four, or more weeks, with all other drinks entirely omitted. Nevertheless, let any ulcers be protected by common <term>plasters</term> <note>medical bandages or dressings coated with healing substances</note>, for the tincture works sufficiently from the inside to heal the outside.

#### ADDITION.

I had decided to write a complete treatise on Antimony, but other business calls me away; nevertheless, I will briefly add some operations here.
Take <note>original: "℞", the traditional symbol for a medical prescription</note> Antimony and grind it, and place it in a large new pot on well-lit coals, and allow it to stand there until it is melted. Then take four ounces each of <term>saltpeter</term> <note>original: "salem nitri," potassium nitrate, used as a flux in alchemy</note> and crude <term>tartar</term> <note>potassium bitartrate, a sediment found in wine casks</note>, reduce them to a powder, and once well mixed and sifted, throw them over half a pound of melted and well-liquefied Antimony. Throw it in little by little and stir with a rod; and when you see it liquefied like water, pour it into a large quantity of common hot water. Let it sit there for 24 hours; afterwards, strain it through a filter and add hot water again so that all saltiness departs, and thus a most deep-red antimony will remain at the bottom. Then pour distilled vinegar over it and stir; leave it for several days in <term>putrefaction</term> <note>a stage in alchemy involving slow digestion or fermentation in a gentle heat</note>, filter it, and distill it three times in a <term>bath</term> <note>original: "balneo," a water bath used for gentle, even heating</note> by returning the vinegar over it, and at the bottom you will find an oil like sweet butter. Take that essence of Antimony and place it in four times as much distilled vinegar, and place the closed <term>vial</term> <note>original: "bociam," a glass vessel with a round body and long neck</note> in <term>dung</term> <note>original: "fimum"; decaying manure was used by alchemists as a natural, steady heat source</note> for 40 days. Take it out and distill it by way of the bath, and the dissolved Antimony will remain at the bottom in the form of an oil as the vinegar recedes. This oil cures cataracts of the eyes, leprosy, cancer, the <term>falling sickness</term> <note>original: "caducum," an old term for epilepsy</note>, and performs many wonders in chemical matters.

### FROM GLASS OF ANTIMONY IS PREPARED

#### ADDITION.

A most deep-red oil of Antimony is made with sugar candy, observing the degrees of fire; it is afterwards <term>circulated</term> <note>a process where a liquid is continuously distilled and then flows back into the same vessel, thought to "exalt" the substance</note>. By a greater circulation, it becomes a sweet and most excellent medicine to be applied both internally and externally.

I had intended to write a complete treatise on Antimony, but other business calls me away; nevertheless, I will briefly add some operations here.

## THE REGULUS OF ANTIMONY.
<note>In alchemy, a "Regulus" refers to the metallic button or purified mass of a semi-metal—in this case, antimony—that settles at the bottom of a crucible after smelting.</note>

### ADDITION.

Take <note>original: "℞", the traditional symbol for a medical prescription</note> Antimony, saltpeter <note>original: "salis nitri"</note>, and crude tartar <note>original: "tartari crudi"</note> in equal amounts <note>original: "an.", short for "ana," meaning "of each"</note> as you please; pulverize them together, and place them in a large pot among coals. Apply a slow fire around it so that the fire may be ignited within. Beware of the rush of its smoke. Stir it with a stick, and when it has been well melted, pour it into a vessel that has a pointed bottom. The dross <note>original: "fæces"</note> will remain on top, but the Regulus will be at the bottom, like a metal. From this Regulus, many and diverse things are made, both in medicine and in Alchemy. 

If you take two parts of the Regulus and one of Mercury, and cook them with two parts of our oil of vitriol <note>original: "olei vitrioli", sulfuric acid</note> until it takes on the color of a lily, they produce wonders if you extract a tincture from them with spirit of wine <note>original: "spiritu vini", distilled alcohol or ethanol</note>.

Also concerning Antimony: If crude Antimony is ground on marble with distilled vinegar, and then placed in a well-sealed glass vessel to digest for twenty days or more in horse manure <note>original: "fimo equino", frequently used as a natural source of gentle, steady heat</note>; when the time is finished, let it be taken out, filtered, and drawn out through distillation. Let what remains be circulated <note>a process of continuous distillation and condensation</note> with the best spirit of wine, and you will have a most red tincture. I do not describe its powers here, but leave them to the sons of the art <note>a traditional phrase referring to dedicated practitioners of alchemy</note>.

## QUINTESSENCE OF THE MARCASITE OF SATURN.
<note>The "Marcasite of Saturn" likely refers to a lead-bearing ore or a specific form of antimony/bismuth associated with lead (Saturn is the alchemical symbol for lead).</note>

### ADDITION.

This is the most noble and sweetest matter of all things that have existed, which surpasses all things by its nature (except for potable gold <note>original: "aurum potabile", gold dissolved in a way that it could be consumed as medicine</note>), for it is surpassed by the quintessence <note>the "fifth essence" or purest extract</note> of our stone, which we call the philosophers' stone—not undeservedly, but truly by its own name. 

Take <note>original: "℞"</note> therefore the mineral mentioned above, which is sharp, long, and reddish inside; let it be crushed and sifted until it becomes an impalpable powder. Let this be soaked in the best strong wine for thirty days, and let the vessel be very well sealed. It should be noted that for 1 pound <note>represented by the symbol ℔; approximately 327 grams</note> of the aforementioned mineral, two measures of wine should be taken. Let these be placed in the sun or in a similar heat. Afterward, let them be distilled, first with a slow fire and then with a stronger one, until the water coming forth begins to turn red. Then let another receiving vessel be put in place. Keep the water and allow it to settle for a long enough time in a well-closed vessel. 

Then, within a space of nine or ten days, something black will settle at the bottom of the glass. Take the water which was floating on top, and for every 5 ounces <note>represented by the symbol ℥</note> of it, take 1 and a half ounces <note>represented by the symbol ℥ j. ß.</note> of the root of cardopacium or chameleon <note>original: "cardopacii sive camæleontis", likely referring to the thistle-like plant *Carlina acaulis*</note> cut into small pieces; let these be distilled together again. The other water, which is also red, requires a powerful fire in the distillation so that the lid glows white-hot. Then you will see a red oil above the water, which must be separated from it. In that same way, the oil of juniper is made. Both of these should be kept separately. And thus these three waters are extracted from the Marcasite of Saturn, which

it contains within itself the fifth essence <note>original: "quintam essentiam," the purest and most concentrated extract of a substance</note>. To extract this, proceed in this manner: while these three types of waters settle for a period of 30 days, you will find something earthy at the bottom of the glass, just as happened before with the first water. Then let the waters be strained; separate the clear from the turbid, retain the pure, and discard the rest. Let the stone be crushed and dissolved in distilled vinegar, then let it be distilled again. This water which comes forth in the glass should be placed over ashes at the second degree of heat; then you will find a red stone similar to a spinel <note>original: "spineto," a red gemstone often confused with ruby</note>, and this is the fifth essence of our antimony. It has not been discovered until now how useful this is to the human race: it heals all forms of leprosy, all fistulas <note>deep, tunnel-like sores</note>, scurvy, and finally all incurable diseases of that kind. It consumes all films and "clouds" of the eyes <note>likely referring to cataracts or corneal scarring</note>. It has a sweet taste, not bitter, nor a sharp harshness or thickness; it resembles nothing other than the color of red wine. It is a singular comfort to those with dropsy <note>original: "Hydropicis," those suffering from edema or fluid swelling</note>, for it quickly consumes the dropsy if the patient takes a quantity the size of a single pea in violet water. It also heals paralysis, apoplexy <note>stroke</note>, and the "assembly sickness" <note>original: "morbumque comitialem," a historical term for epilepsy</note>, if it is taken with three drops of potable gold <note>original: "auri potabilis," a medicinal oil or liquid containing gold</note>. Lest it perish, this stone must be preserved in dry places and kept in millet seed; for if it is placed in damp places, it is ruined within the space of four months.

# BALSAM OF ANTIMONY.
## ADDITION.

Take <note>original: "℞"</note> one part of Antimony reduced to a fine powder <note>original: "Alcool pulverisati"</note>, and four parts of a turpentine solvent <note>original: "menstrui Therebinthinati"</note>. Mix them well; let them be put into a glass vessel having a long neck, and let them be digested at the second degree of fire for as long as it takes to acquire a red color, which will happen shortly. Pour it off; pour in other new solvent, and do this until the whole has been dissolved. Draw off the solvent by a gentle fire. That which remains, like a gum, is extremely useful for wounds and ulcers. But if you wish to drive it through a retort <note>a glass vessel with a long downward-pointing neck used for distillation</note>, you will have a Balsam. You shall do the same with the glass; I leave this to the experience of the Chemists. B. à PORTU <note>Likely Bernard G. Penot, a famous alchemist and physician known as Bernardus à Portu</note>.

<margin>The powers of the oil of orpiment.</margin>
It suppresses growths, removes hair, and when combined with resin, it fills in hair loss <note>original: "Alopecias"</note>, cures lice infestations <note>original: "phthiriasi"</note>, and is beneficial for ulcers of the nose and mouth. When mixed with rose oil, it aids the eruption of pustules and cleanses filthy ulcers. Likewise, it heals long-standing, weeping sores that refuse to scar, as well as fungal-like growths, and consumes "unclean flesh" <note>likely referring to necrotic tissue or proud flesh</note>. Furthermore, it helps foul-smelling nasal ulcers, fistulas <note>deep, tunnel-like sores</note>, carbuncles <note>severe boils</note>, gangrene, severed nerves, ruptures <note>original: "ramicibus," likely referring to hernias or scrotal swellings</note> caused by fluid, and cancers <note>original: "carcinomati"</note>; it also aids against discharges. It may be mixed into ointments, liniments, and oils, or the edges of the ulcers may be smeared with it three or four times. But if the ulcer itself begins to weep and becomes covered with a certain crust, it can be softened with this ointment made from May butter <note>butter made from the milk of cows grazing on spring grass, prized for its purity and medicinal value</note>, which has been poured warm over bean water and a decoction of lupins and Solomon’s Seal <note>a medicinal plant of the genus *Polygonatum*</note>. For ulcers, one may use it in this manner: mix 2 ounces each of oil of orpiment, oil of myrrh, and turpentine; this is applied to cleanse any ulcer and fill it with new flesh. ## ON CORALS AND THE POWER OF CORALS.

It also cures melancholy and insanity and resists all poisons. The preparation is as follows: ℞. Two ounces of ground corals and one pound of lovage water <note>original: "aquæ ligustici"</note>.

## ON PHILOSOPHICAL GOLD AND
<insert>its powers.</insert>

Now we shall treat philosophical gold. All the philosophers say that our gold is not the common or "vulgar" kind <note>original: "vulgis aut commune"</note>, but philosophical; for without any danger or harm, it heals the human body (God the Best and Greatest giving and helping). I speak here not of a "chemical" <note>likely meaning a counterfeit or metallic alloy</note> substance, but of true and natural gold, which is surely prepared without any corrosive or poisonous waters <note>referring to harsh acids like aqua fortis (nitric acid) often used to dissolve gold</note>. It is called <term>potable gold</term> <note>original: "aurum potabile"; gold in a drinkable liquid form</note> whenever it has been reduced into a drinkable substance along with other spirits or liquids. <margin>The active power is in every tincture.</margin>

The dose of the quintessence of gold is <term>three grains</term>, mixed at various times with good <term>aqua vitae</term> <note>original: "aquæ vitæ"; literally "water of life," referring to high-proof distilled alcohol or brandy</note> or some other very subtle water. It is taken in the morning, at noon, and in the evening as the medicine requires.

If a disease were located in any principal organ, this sulfur must be fermented into a specific form, otherwise it would have no power to act upon the limbs; for these "specifics" transmute this gold from one form into another. For the nature of the balsam is one thing in the blood, another in the brain, another in the heart, and another in the spleen. A physician must know and observe all these things.

### ADDITIO
### <note>original: "ADDITIO"; Addition</note>

A true description of **diaphoretic gold** <term>diaphoretic</term> <note>From the Greek *diaphorētikos*, meaning "promoting sweat." In alchemy and early medicine, sweating was considered a vital way to purge the body of toxins or "poisons."</note>. Create an amalgam from Gold <note>original: "Sole," the alchemical name for gold, associated with the Sun.</note> and Mercury, and mix it with powder of flowers of Sulfur, the weight of which should be triple that of the amalgam. Place all these together in a strong dish over low heat for one hour. Afterward, ignite the Sulfur so that it is entirely burned away, and you will find your gold has become very spongy. Grind this carefully upon a marble slab, and while grinding, sprinkle this powder with the best rectified **aqua vitae** <note>literally "water of life"; highly concentrated distilled alcohol.</note>. When you have mixed it well, set fire to the aqua vitae so that it burns away completely, and thus you will find the gold calcined <note>reduced to a powder through heat</note>; do this three times. Grind it again upon the marble, add a little honey and prepared common salt, then place it in an earthen dish and pour in hot water. Stir it and let it rest for a while, then filter and wash it until no trace of honey or salt remains; it will then be so fine that you could write with it. Then you shall incorporate it with a triple amount of **oil of tartar** <note>a solution of potassium carbonate, used as a chemical reagent.</note>, dry it, and place it in the fire until it glows red. Afterward, place it upon the marble, and the gold will be dissolved into a deep red liquid along with the salt. If it does not dissolve the first time, you must repeat the process with what remains. Place this oil in a matrass <note>a long-necked glass flask used in distilling</note> with the best aqua vitae and put it in a water bath for eight days, and for another eight days in hot ashes; you will find your oil is as red as a ruby. Afterward, draw off the aqua vitae through a filter so that the salt of tartar is separated. Wash it frequently with aqua vitae and ignite it; save the oil that remains for use. The virtues of this **potable gold** <note>original: "auri potabilis"; a liquid gold preparation sought by alchemists as a universal medicine.</note> are so great that I can hardly count them. First, for the stone <note>original: "calculo"; kidney or bladder stones</note>, by drinking 5 or 6 drops with white wine or some suitable water, it immediately soothes the pain; and after one hour, it dissolves the stone and casts it out. During the plague, when the heart is laboring greatly, it repels the pestilential poison. It is a most excellent remedy against all kinds of poison, it cures apoplexy <note>a stroke or sudden loss of consciousness</note>, restoring a person to their former health in a short time. It heals cancer and all ulcers, cures internal abscesses, and is effective against all desperate diseases abandoned by physicians, provided that the vital moisture <note>original: "humidum"; referring to the "radical moisture," a concept in medieval medicine representing the body's innate life force or fuel.</note> in the person is not entirely extinguished.

There are some impostors who sell the following recipe as **potable gold** <term>potable gold</term> <note>Latin: *aurum potabile*. A legendary alchemical medicine believed to be gold dissolved in a liquid form, capable of curing all diseases and granting longevity.</note>: They take gold filings, which they put into a glass vessel, and over them, they add oils of camphor, cloves, and fennel, along with half a drachm <note>The symbol ʒß represents a half-drachm, roughly 2 grams.</note> of oil of vitriol <note>Sulfuric acid.</note> drop by drop. I bought this secret in Prague for the price of 24 ducats, and I offer it to you for free: but beware that you do not administer such "potable gold" to anyone. The reason is ready at hand:

### ON RECOVERING YOUTH
<margin>Raymond.</margin> <note>Refers to Raymond Lull (c. 1232–1315), a Majorcan philosopher. Many alchemical texts were attributed to him in the centuries following his death.</note>

Take the "Heaven of the Philosophers," <note>original: "Cœlum philoſophorum"</note> that is, the **quintessence of gold**. With this noble drink, an old man can take the amount of half an ounce in the morning and evening, and within a very few days he will reach such a state of health that he will clearly and perceptibly feel that he has returned to his former youth; however, caution is needed to use wine moderately during this time. This is the rule you shall observe for the loss of old age and the recovery of youth.

### THE SAME [LULL] ON THE CARE OF THE HOPELESS.

Take celandine <note>original: "chelidonia," likely Greater Celandine, prized by alchemists for its gold-colored sap.</note>, whose flower and fruit are hot in the [highest] degree, and extract the "fourth element" through mastery, which is of the element of fire, like a liquid oil. Attach this to our quintessence <note>original: "q." or "q. e." for *quinta essentia*.</note> in the quantity of one grain of wheat, and immediately the patient will rise up in a short space of time, if he is capable of swallowing it. Then comfort him with the administration of our quintessence by itself, and know that he will be perfectly cured, unless the Lord God wills him to die entirely. The same Lull says this regarding the cure of leprosy, which comes to men from the corruption of humors <note>The four bodily fluids (blood, phlegm, yellow and black bile) believed to control health.</note> or the nature of infecting poisons; for such people, we intend to provide this remedy and perfect health, whether the disease has progressed for a long or short time. Take the **secret of the sun** <note>original: "arcanum solis," a preparation of gold.</note> and of pearls, and administer it to the patient for eight days, giving him one full nutshell's worth in the morning, and thus he will be fully cured. For this is a heavenly medicine, which cures the whole of leprosy from whichever offending humor within a short time. Also, take water made from strawberries <note>original: "fragis."</note> and attach it to our quintessence of gold and pearls and apply it; for indeed, the water of these things masks the marks of lepers if it is drunk or if the spots are smeared with it; especially, however, if one mixes it with **burning water** <term>burning water</term> <note>original: "aquam ardentem," distilled alcohol or aqua vitae.</note>, and thus...

...you will perfectly cure all leprosy with its various types. For those suffering from dropsy <note>original: *hydropicis*; a condition where fluid builds up in the body's tissues or cavities.</note>, **potable gold** is beneficial, taken with oil of hellebore and sulfur.

### PARACELSUS ON GOUT.

In the beginning, the gouty patient should be purged with a full and perfect cleansing, and then treated with the **coralline secret** <term>coralline secret</term> <note>Latin: *arcano corallino*. In Paracelsian medicine, this usually refers to a red-colored preparation, often made from mercury or gold, believed to have high medicinal potency.</note>, that is, the color separated and abstracted from the substance by spirit of wine <note>High-proof alcohol or ethanol used as a solvent.</note>. Through the intervention of this spirit, the gouty fluxes are drawn out, so that no place remains for the gout to linger. In this coralline secret, which is derived from the **essence of gold**, there is such great power and virtue that it is impossible for a physician to perceive it without first performing this purging. Let this purging be done six or seven times, depending on the age, severity, or nature of the gout. Paracelsus, by means of the **quintessence** <term>quintessence</term> <note>The "fifth essence" or purest part of a substance, believed to be the most potent medicinal element.</note> of the sun <note>In alchemy, "Sol" or the Sun always refers to Gold.</note>, as well as its oil, removes leprosy along with all other diseases; it renews and restores the body. Furthermore, it strengthens the sight and makes it clear. 

**Potable gold** may be used in electuaries <note>A medicinal paste made by mixing powders with honey or syrup.</note>, and it is also effective against the **"universal" or Spanish disease** <note>Names used in the 16th century for Syphilis.</note>. Take 8 grains <note>A small unit of weight, roughly 0.05 grams.</note> in wine, or 1 ounce <note>The symbol ℥ denotes an ounce.</note> of theriac water, on an empty stomach in the morning for 10 continuous days. For it is a diaphoretic <note>A substance that induces sweating to expel toxins.</note> medicine, purging away superfluous sweats and all harmful humors from the entire body. It is beneficial for those with consumption <note>Latin: *phthisicis*; tuberculosis.</note>, hectic fever, spleen disorders, cancerous and "eating" ulcers <note>Latin: *phagedænicis*; sores that rapidly spread and destroy tissue.</note>, lupus-like sores, and fistulas. It preserves the entire human body from putrefaction and corruption until the day ordained by God the Best. 

Furthermore, it is able to cure every "new illness" that arises from the unctions and fumigations of **"living gold"** (common Mercury), as well as precipitates, sublimates, cinnabar, and other absurd medicines used by the unskilled (who hand out lethal poison instead of a remedy). The dose for **precipitated gold** is half a denarius <note>A weight roughly equal to 1.5 grams.</note> for younger people, and a whole one by weight for adults. It cures the plague when taken with **theriac** <note>A famous ancient "universal antidote" made of many herbal and mineral ingredients.</note>, drives away dropsy <note>Latin: *aquam intercutem*; literally 'water under the skin'.</note>, elephantiasis, and other diseases difficult to cure, and opens obstructions of the internal organs. It helps those who have swallowed poison. This same remedy is taken internally for curing malignant ulcers in the "French disease" <note>Another common name for Syphilis.</note>.

**Take** <note>The symbol ℞ stands for the Latin *Recipe*.</note> 1 denarius of precipitated gold and mix it with 1 ounce of electuary of rose juice. Also take 5 scruples <note>The symbol ℈ denotes a scruple, about 1.3 grams.</note> of the **"species of gems"** <note>A medicinal powder containing crushed precious stones like emeralds or rubies.</note>; mix them together and let it be given as is customary, taken two, three, or four times. It promises that the pestilence will be soon extirpated. Then, for external use, it is successfully mixed with cleansing ointments and plasters to treat foul and cavernous sores, though not for "creeping" ones <note>Likely referring to spreading skin conditions like herpes or erysipelas.</note>.

The administration and use of the **Tincture of the Sun** <note>A liquid extract of gold.</note> according to Paracelsus is as follows: **Take** 1 ounce of the Tincture of the Sun or Gold and mix it with 1 ounce of the best Venetian Theriac. Let 1 scruple of this mixture be given to the patient on an empty stomach at dawn. Let sweat be commanded and promoted by covering the patient with blankets in bed. This process of administration is to be repeated until the ulcer ejects blood, or any other bloody humor, as usually happens, perhaps by the twelfth day...

# ON CHEMICAL MATTERS

...you will perfectly cure every kind of leprosy along with all its specific forms. **Potable gold** <term>potable gold</term> <note>Latin: *aurum potabile*; a liquid form of gold believed to be a universal restorative.</note> is beneficial for those suffering from **dropsy** <term>dropsy</term> <note>Edema, or the accumulation of excess fluid in the body's tissues.</note>, when combined with oil of hellebore and sulfur.

### PARACELSUS ON GOUT

In the beginning, let the sufferer of **gout** <term>gout</term> <note>Latin: *podagra*; specifically gout of the foot.</note> be purged with a full and perfect cleansing. Then, let him be treated with the **coralline secret** <term>coralline secret</term> <note>original: *arcanum corallinum*; a red-colored chemical preparation, usually involving mercury or gold, named for its coral-like hue.</note>—that is, the color separated and abstracted from the substance by the **spirit of wine** <term>spirit of wine</term> <note>Alcohol or ethanol used as a solvent.</note>. Through its intervention, the "fluxes" of gout are drawn out, so that no place remains for the gout to take hold. In this coralline secret, which is derived from the **essence of gold**, there resides such great force and virtue that it is impossible for a physician to grasp it unless this purging has first been performed. This purging should be done six or seven times, depending on the age, the severity, or the nature of the gout.

Paracelsus removes **leprosy** <note>In the 16th century, "leprosy" often referred to a wide variety of chronic skin diseases, not just Hansen's disease.</note> along with all other diseases by using the **quintessence of the sun** <gloss>gold</gloss> and its oil; it renews and restores the body. Furthermore, it strengthens the sight and makes it clear. Potable gold is used in **electuaries** <term>electuary</term> <note>A medicinal paste made by mixing powders with honey or syrup.</note>, and likewise against the **Catholic** or **Spanish disease** <note>Syphilis, which at the time was often named after rival nations (the "French disease" to the English/Germans, the "Spanish disease" to the Italians, etc.).</note>; eight grains should be taken in wine or one dram of **theriacal water** <term>theriacal water</term> <note>A medicinal water infused with theriac, a famous ancient herbal jam used as an antidote.</note> in the morning on an empty stomach for ten continuous days. 

For this is a **diaphoretic** <term>diaphoretic</term> <note>A medicine that induces sweating to expel toxins.</note> medicine, purging all superfluous and harmful **humors** <term>humors</term> <note>The bodily fluids—blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile—which ancient medicine sought to balance.</note> of the whole body. It is conducive to the treatment of **consumption** <gloss>phthisis</gloss>, hectic fevers, ailments of the spleen, cancerous and **phagedenic** <term>phagedenic</term> <note>Rapidly spreading or "eating" ulcers.</note> ulcers, lupus, and fistulas; it preserves the entire human body from putrefaction and corruption until the day destined by God the Almighty. 

Indeed, it is even powerful enough to cure every new illness that arises or emerges from the unctions and fumigations of **quick-gold** or **common mercury**, as well as from **precipitates**, **sublimates**, and **cinnabar**, and other absurd medicines of the unskilled (who offer or hold out lethal poison as a remedy). 

The dose of **precipitated gold** is half a **denarius** <note>A small weight measurement, roughly equivalent to a scruple or 1.2 grams.</note> for younger people, and for adults the weight of a full denarius. ### ON THE MOON AND PHILOSOPHICAL SILVER
#### and its Virtues.

**Philosophical silver** <term>philosophical silver</term> <note>original: *Argentum philosophicum*; silver that has been purified or prepared through alchemical processes to enhance its medicinal properties.</note> is a diaphoretic <note>A substance that induces sweating, believed to expel toxins.</note> for diseases arising from inflammation of the brain, convulsions of the nerves, the "stunned disease"—also known as the Cosmopolitan or **Spanish disease** <note>original: *morbo attonito Cosmopolitico seu Hispanico*; in this context, "Spanish disease" refers to syphilis, while "stunned disease" often refers to apoplexy or a stroke.</note>—mania or insanity, and delirium. It is a singular remedy for the ailments and obstructions of the liver, spleen, and menstrual cycles. Indeed, it expels the corrupt qualities of the human body through the pores without any fear, danger, weakening, or loss of strength. It strengthens the vital organs and the vital spirits, restoring the entire human body to its original health. 

Silver leaves or scraps are commonly mixed into the **Electuary of Gems** <term>electuary of gems</term> <note>original: *Electuario de gemmis*; a medicinal paste made of honey or syrup containing crushed gemstones, used to treat heart and brain conditions.</note>, Galen’s "gladdening" medicines, and the "golden" medicines of Alexandria to treat mania, melancholy, and to strengthen the brain itself. The **Spagyrists** <term>spagyrists</term> <note>Alchemists who practiced the art of separating and recombining the "essences" of minerals and plants for medicine.</note>, however, extract an oil from **Luna** <note>The alchemical name for silver, associated with the Moon.</note> itself, of which two or three drops are administered in water of wood betony, sage, or lemon balm to treat the **falling sickness** <term>falling sickness</term> <note>original: *morbum caducum*; epilepsy.</note> and all afflictions of the brain. The "white body" and "fixed Luna" remain; it is reduced into Mercury within a few days and becomes precipitated by feverish heat on its own, turning into a powder. Eight grains of this powder are administered against **dropsy** <term>dropsy</term> <note>original: *hydropem*; edema, or the accumulation of fluid in the body.</note>.

### THE TRUE PREPARATION OF LUNA.
#### AN ADDITION.

Separate the water from the tartar through a filter; the oil of silver will remain at the bottom. Wash this repeatedly until the water no longer tastes of tartar.

### ON SATURN OR PHILOSOPHICAL LEAD,
### *and its powers.*

Saturn <note>The alchemical name for Lead.</note> or philosophical lead is beneficial for all burns, whether caused by fire, water, or oil. It heals hemorrhoids, restrains the growth of ulcers, and opposes cancerous and putrid ulcers whether used by itself or mixed with other ingredients. It heals the "Holy Persian Fire" <note>original: *Ignem Persicum sacrum*; historically used to describe various skin conditions such as shingles, erysipelas, or carbuncles.</note> as they call it, is useful for skin eruptions <term>impetigo</term>, fills up any cavities in the flesh, and suppresses bleeding. Likewise, if rubbed onto convulsed or weakened limbs, it restores them in a short time. This same oil, when mixed with oil of chamomile and olive oil, disperses tumors caused by hot imbalances; furthermore, it restrains inflammations arising from any cause and any kind of burns, especially if a blue cloth soaked in it is placed over them. However, for those suffering from the "colic passion" <note>Severe abdominal pain or intestinal cramping.</note> and other pains of the intestines, 3 or 4 grains are given to drink in some liquid.

Let these things now suffice regarding the manifold powers of minerals and metals. When these are reduced into a liquid by a subtle preceding preparation, they are found to have wonderful effects. However, according to the preparation of common pharmacists and many other unskilled persons, they have almost none. This is because the natural heat of the body is not so powerful or strong that it can break down and transmute Gold <note>original: *solem*; literally "The Sun," alchemical shorthand for gold.</note>, Silver <note>original: *Lunam*; literally "The Moon," alchemical shorthand for silver.</note>, and other metals so that they, having been changed into blood, can nourish the human body, comfort the vital spirits, and perform the other tasks granted to them by nature, as long as they remain in their harder substance. This is equally known to all physicists and physicians.

### ADDITION.

Take 2 pounds of Minium <term>Minium</term> <note>Red lead, a bright red-orange pigment and chemical compound.</note> and place it into a glass vessel. Pour over it distilled vinegar until it rises six fingers' height above the powder. Place the vessel, well-sealed, over warm ashes. Stir it immediately with a rod so it does not stick to the bottom. On the following day, pour off the vinegar—which should now be sweet—into another vessel. Add new vinegar and do as you did before. Continue this until all the minium has been dissolved. Having collected all the vinegar, you must filter it through a new filter; then, let it putrefy in horse dung <note>Alchemists used the natural heat of decomposing horse manure as a steady, low-temperature incubator.</note> for 15 days. When the time is up, distill the vinegar to "thirds"—that is, so that only one part out of three remains. Place this third part in a cool place, such as a cellar, and crystals will form. Then pour off the vinegar and take the crystals and save them. Distill the vinegar again to thirds and set it in a cool place, and crystals will form again. Repeat this until you have reduced all that material into crystals. Take 2 ounces of that crystalline salt and keep it until I tell you what must be done with it. Take all the rest of that crystalline material and place it in a glass retort <term>retort</term> <note>A glass vessel with a long, downward-pointing neck used for distilling substances.</note> fortified with the best lute <term>lute</term> <note>A clay-based cement used to seal alchemical apparatus and protect glass from high heat.</note>. Attach a sufficiently large receiver vessel to it and, having sealed the joints, begin the distillation. First, a white smoke will come out, and then a red oil. Increase the fire with dry wood until the distillation is complete. Separate the water from the oil in a Maria's Bath <term>Maria's Bath</term> <note>Also known as a *Balneum Mariae* or bain-marie; a water bath used for gentle, even heating.</note>. Keep both aside. You shall rectify <note>To purify a liquid through repeated distillation.</note> the oil three times, and likewise clean the water separately in the bath. This old man <note>Likely referring to a specific alchemical authority or perhaps the personification of Lead/Saturn himself.</note> is endowed with such great prudence and wisdom that scarcely any mortal can count it. Use his "sweat and blood" <note>Metaphorical terms for the distilled water and red oil produced by the process.</note> in all diseases, both externally and internally, giving thanks to God. B. à PORTU. <note>Likely Bernardus à Portu, the Latinized name of Bernard Georges Penot, a famous 16th-century alchemist and physician.</note>

## ON HUMAN BLOOD AND
### *its powers.*

**From** human blood, oil and salt can be made, and after these, a red stone of wonderful efficacy and virtue: it restrains the flow of blood and expels many infirmities. <term>℞.</term> <note>The traditional symbol for "Recipe" or "Take."</note> Take human blood and let it decay <note>original: *putrefac*; the process of "putrefaction" was a standard alchemical stage where organic matter was broken down by gentle heat.</note> in warm dung; then distill it, and a white water like milk will come forth. Afterward, increase the fire and you will distill an oil; finally, rectify the dregs remaining in the bottom of the vessel until they are as white as snow. By pouring its oil back onto them, a clear and red stone will be formed. The salt of human blood is effective against diseases of the joints, and it also cures gout of the feet, hands, and knees. <note>The original text uses the specific Latin terms *podagra* (foot gout), *chiragra* (hand gout), and *gonagra* (knee gout).</note>

Let this now suffice regarding the more excellent and highly necessary medicines, the correct preparation of all of which has been taught by the Chemical art—though it is condemned by the unskilled common folk. For "Theophrastic" <note>Referring to Theophrastus Paracelsus (1493–1541), the Swiss physician who pioneered the use of minerals and chemicals in medicine.</note> remedies are taken or extracted not only from plants—as many foolish people think and persuade the whole world—but also from metals, gems, and precious stones. These remedies, however, are not sharp or violent, as the ignorant and unskilled shout; rather, they are most sweet and very familiar to our nature. They preserve the excellence of the spirits, vivify them, and purge them of impurities, mostly through sweat alone. In their whole substance, they are of no small benefit, as many of the learned experience daily with happy success. But it is no wonder these things seem filthy to those who are so submerged in those dregs and impurities of their own that their minds cannot emerge to higher and subtler things. Furthermore, through their own laziness, they flee the labor required in the preparation of these medicines. 

But I warn such men: either let them learn better things, or let them not envy better institutions; at the very least, let them not reproach what is unknown to them. If they do not, we will nonetheless not be delayed by their efforts, because it will come to pass that truth will obtain the palm of victory while they snarl in vain. Finally, dispersing those shadows with its brightness, truth will reveal things as they truly are.

<header>ON MEDICINES</header>

<margin>
Where I first obtained this treatise.
</margin>

The name of the author of this treatise is unknown to me. Whoever he was, he was undoubtedly most skilled in all matters and possessed a remarkable knowledge of both medicines <note>Likely referring to the "twofold medicine" of the era: traditional Galenic herbalism and the newer Paracelsian "spagyric" or chemical medicine.</note>. When I shared a treatise on saltpeter <term>saltpeter</term> <note>original: *sale nitro*; potassium nitrate, a key ingredient in gunpowder and chemical medicine.</note> with the most learned Wenceslaus Lavinius of Prague, which I had acquired, he gave me this miscellaneous treatise to be transcribed; it was so full of errors that I could barely extract the true meaning. You, kind reader, look favorably upon our nighttime labors and take them in good part. B. à PORTU. <note>Bernard Georges Penot (c. 1519–1617), a French physician and alchemist.</note>

# . T H E  P R E P A R A T I O N .
# O F  S A L T P E T E R .

<image-desc>Woodcut ornamental initial 'A' decorated with foliage and scrolls within a square frame.</image-desc>The saltpeter is exposed to the sun in a large dish or another leaden vessel until it turns white; then it is reduced to a white powder. Prepared in this way, it acquires more "subtlety" <note>In alchemy, "subtlety" refers to a state of being more refined, volatile, or chemically active.</note> and can be called purified froth of saltpeter <note>original: *aphron nitron puricatum*. *Aphron nitre* was a historical term for the light, efflorescent crust found on saltpeter.</note>.

Or, it is calcined <term>calcined</term> <note>Heated to a high temperature to remove impurities or change the substance's physical state.</note> with a strong fire until it turns white; its "gummy" <note>Referring to sticky or oily impurities in the raw mineral.</note> nature will thus be greatly diminished, and it will have greater heat and refinement in its operation.

### ADDITION.

Gradually melt the saltpeter in a strong crucible. Once melted, slowly cast in common sulfur the size of beans until it will no longer absorb any more. Pour it into a vessel full of water, filter it, coagulate it <note>Solidify by evaporating the liquid.</note>, melt it again, and cast in sulfur once more. Repeat this five times. Finally, dissolve, filter, and coagulate it, and then it is ready.

## O I L  O F  S A L T P E T E R .

### ADDITION.

Melt purified lead and throw the best saltpeter upon it as much as you like; it will then be melted into an oil. When removed from the fire, it will congeal and be separated from the lead; store it in a glass vessel. When you wish to use it, place it by the fire and it will quickly turn into an oil, which fixes <term>fixes</term> <note>To "fix" a substance means to make it stable and non-volatile so that it no longer evaporates or changes when heated.</note> most perfectly. This oil is rectified <term>rectified</term> <note>Purified through distillation.</note> by distilling through a retort, for the moisture passes over and the purified oil remains.

## T H E  F I X A T I O N  O F  S A L T P E T E R .

### ADDITION.

<term>℞.</term> <note>The traditional symbol for *Recipe*, meaning "Take."</note> Take saltpeter and iron filings in equal parts, and two parts of quicklime <term>quicklime</term> <note>Calcium oxide, a caustic substance used to strip impurities or facilitate chemical reactions.</note>. Grind them together and place them in a well-sealed pot, and put it in a blast furnace so that it burns for four hours. When it has cooled, pour clear water over it and let it stand overnight; then the saltpeter will be separated from the lime. Filter, evaporate, and congeal it; once dried, melt it, and it will flow into a fixed oil.

## *For removing all skin defects and blemishes: such as moles, skin discolorations, jaundice, the itch, pustules, swellings, ringworm, and leprosy.*

Dissolve prepared saltpeter <term>saltpeter</term> <note>original: *nitrum*; potassium nitrate. While used for gunpowder, in this context it is a "chemical" salt used as a topical cleanser and drying agent.</note> in warm water or a lye made from grapevines, roses, willows, rosemary, sage, hyssop, lavender, thyme, or laurel. Alternatively, it may be dissolved in the distilled urine of a young boy, distilled vinegar, lemon juice, or purified honey (macerated for three days), or even in goose fat, swan fat, or oil of almonds. Apply this to the skin when going to bed. In the morning, wash the affected area with rose water, bean water <note>Water in which beans were boiled, traditionally used as a cosmetic skin softener.</note>, or a decoction of barley flour, wheat bran, and mallow roots.

### For the same purpose.

Take (℞) selected tragacanth <note>A natural gum used as a binder.</note> as much as you wish; soak it in rose water or rose vinegar until it dissolves. Add very fine powder of Arum roots (also called serpentaria) that has been soaked seven times in rose water and dried in the sun, as well as Orris powder <note>powdered root of the Iris flower</note> and rice flour. Take the same amount of each of these as you did of the tragacanth. Then add as much saltpeter as the combined weight of all the previous ingredients. Place over a moderate fire, stirring constantly until the saltpeter melts, and continue until it thickens. Then add a little camphor. When it reaches a consistency where it can easily be formed into pills, remove it from the fire. At the beginning, you may also dissolve a little musk, civet, or ambergris <note>Aromatic animal substances used to scent the medicine.</note> in the rose water or rose vinegar if you wish. When going to bed, moisten one pill with rose water, rose vinegar, or lemon juice, and rub it onto yourself. In the morning, wash yourself with bean or rose water.

### Lotion for ringworm.

Take (℞) 3 drachms <term>drachm</term> <note>original: *ʒ*; a medical weight approximately equal to 3.9 grams.</note> of saltpeter, 1 drachm of common salt, 4 ounces of dock water <note>original: *aqua lapathij*; a liquid distilled from the dock plant, used for skin ailments.</note>, and 1 ounce of squill vinegar <note>vinegar infused with sea onion (squill), often used for its sharp, cleansing properties.</note>. Let them be dissolved and mixed. Dip a cloth into this warmed liquid and rub the face.

### *Ointment for removing swellings, calluses, and hardness of the skin.*

Take (℞) equal parts of saltpeter, rock salt <term>rock salt</term> <note>original: *salis gemmæ*; high-quality crystalline salt.</note>, tips of hyssop, and pennyroyal. Let them be crushed and incorporated into rose cerate <note>A wax-based ointment scented with roses.</note> over a gentle fire.

### *A proven remedy for the itch, ringworm, and itching.*

Take (℞) 1 drachm each of saltpeter, sulfur, and marjoram. Let those that need grinding be powdered, let the marjoram be crushed, and mix them with rose oil to make an ointment.

*A wash or liniment that draws out and cures smallpox, redness, and pustules of the body.*

Take (℞) saltpeter <note>original: *nitrum*</note> mixed with the juice of hyssop, marigold <term>marigold</term> <note>original: *calthae*</note>, and chamomile, with added oil of bitter almonds.

->*Against leprosy.*<-

Saltpeter tempered with vitriol <note>Metal sulfates, such as copper or iron sulfate, used for their astringent properties.</note> and verdigris <term>verdigris</term> <note>original: *aere viridi*; a green pigment and medicinal substance formed by the weathering of copper.</note> removes leprosy when applied.

->*To ripen, cleanse, and cure ulcers, carbunculos, and fistulas.*<-

Saltpeter mixed with turpentine <term>turpentine</term> <note>original: *terebinthina*; a resin harvested from pine trees, frequently used in this period to "draw out" infection from wounds.</note> applied and rubbed in.

->*A potion for the disease of jaundice.*<-

One spoonful of saltpeter swallowed with wine on an empty stomach cures jaundice <note>original: *icterum*</note>.

->*A liniment for skin spots.*<-

Let saltpeter be dissolved in white wine or distilled vinegar, or lemon juice; rub the skin with it when going to bed <note>original: *morpheam*; in this period, "morphea" referred to various types of skin discolorations, scurvy-like spots, or localized leprosy.</note>.

->*An ointment for whitening the face and making the skin clear.*<-

Take (℞) 1 ounce of psyllium seed <term>psyllium</term> <note>original: *sem. psillij*</note> and 3 ounces of oil of tartar <note>A caustic solution of potassium carbonate, used here as a chemical peel.</note>; let them soak in a lead vessel for three days. Afterward, squeeze the mucilage through a small bag and mix it with rose oil; then dissolve 1 ounce of saltpeter and 1 ounce of rock salt <term>rock salt</term> <note>original: *salis gemmae*</note> into it, and make an ointment.

->*To make the hair golden.*<-

Saltpeter tempered with crushed lupines <term>lupines</term> <note>A type of legume; the meal was often used as a detergent or cosmetic scrub.</note> and warm water makes the hair beautiful if washed often.

->*Lest the hair fall out.*<-

Let saltpeter be dissolved in Malmsey wine <term>Malmsey wine</term> <note>original: *vino malvatico*; a sweet, potent Mediterranean wine often used as a solvent for medicines.</note>, and rub the spot with it; afterward, apply crushed beet.

->*To remove lice, nits, and dandruff of the head.*<-

Let saltpeter and Samian earth <note>A medicinal clay from the island of Samos, prized since antiquity for its drying and healing properties.</note> be dissolved in radish seed oil and applied.

->*Against excessive moisture of the brain and dandruff of the head.*<-

Let saltpeter be dissolved in white vinegar, add powder of frankincense <term>frankincense</term> <note>original: *olibani*</note>, and rub the affected area with it.

->*To whiten the teeth.*<-

Prepared saltpeter cleanses the teeth if they are rubbed with it.

->*Against toothache.*<-

Saltpeter cooked with wine and pepper eases the pain of teeth if held in the mouth.

### *For headache.*

Saltpeter <note>original: *nitrum*</note> mixed with the juice of ivy leaves and berries, either inhaled through the nostrils or applied to the head with rose vinegar, soothes the pain of the head.

### *Against earache, as well as suppuration, ringing, and blockage.*

Let saltpeter mixed with the juice of ivy leaves and berries, along with the oil of bitter almonds, chamomile, violets, and roses, be poured lukewarm into the ears.

### *For all eye defects.*

Saltpeter mixed with rose honey or Malmsey wine <term>Malmsey</term> <note>original: *vino malvatico*; a sweet, potent Greek wine often used as a solvent in early modern medicine.</note>, or endive water, when applied to the eyes, dispels cloudiness, removes spots and tearing, and sharpens the vision.

### *For nosebleeds.*

Saltpeter mixed with silphium <note>A medicinal plant from antiquity, likely a species of giant fennel.</note> or asafetida <term>asafetida</term> <note>original: *assa foetida*; a pungent herbal resin used for various medicinal purposes.</note>, and applied to the nostrils, stops the blood.

### *For deformities of the nails.*

Let saltpeter be dissolved in Malmsey wine, then placed over hot ashes inside the hollowed-out rind of a pomegranate; with linen cloths soaked in this, apply it to the deformed nails.

### *For quinsy and throat defects.*

Let saltpeter be boiled with violets, to which violet honey and liquid pitch or cedar resin <note>original: *cedria*</note> are added; let it be made into a gargle.

->*Or:*<-

Let saltpeter be dissolved in a decoction of hyssop and figs, and let it be made into a gargle.

### *Against paralysis of the tongue.*

Let saltpeter be boiled with sage and posca <note>A traditional mixture of vinegar and water.</note> or water, vinegar, and salt; add this mixture to the leaven <note>yeast or sourdough starter</note> which is put into the dough from which bread is to be made. Let the patient eat this bread.

### *Against paralysis and numbness of the nerves, loss of sensation, convulsion, distortion, piercing pain, and spasms.*

Let the patient use a bath or fomentations <note>warm, moist medicinal applications</note> with saltpeter boiled in water and salt, to which is added sage, lavender, rosemary, thyme, hyssop, oregano, pennyroyal, savory, elder, mint, horehound, elecampane, and oak polypody <note>original: *polypodium quercinum*; a type of fern growing on oak trees, prized in pharmacy.</note>. Let the affected area be anointed with oil of castor <note>original: *oleo castorei*; a substance derived from beaver scent glands, then used for nervous system disorders.</note>, or oil of spike lavender, or oil of mastic.

### *A most healthy footbath.*

Take (℞) red rose petals, chamomile, betony, oregano, sage, and rue, one handful of each. Put these into a linen bag; let the bag be tied and boiled in sufficient water. Add half a pound of saltpeter and a little coarse salt, and it is prepared.

### *For sciatica and ailments of the hip.*

Take saltpeter <note>original: *nitrum*</note> with a decoction of dwarf elder <note>original: *ebuli*</note>, or the bark of elder roots, and elecampane <note>original: *enulae campanae*; a bitter herb used for respiratory and digestive health</note>; let it be made into an enema.

### *For hoarseness, cough, asthma, and other defects of the lungs and chest.*

Let saltpeter be boiled with hyssop and figs; let cabbage be mixed into the decoction, and let the patient drink from it.

->Or.<-

Let saltpeter be dissolved with *posca* <term>posca</term> <note>original: *posca*; a common Roman drink made of vinegar and water, often used as a solvent in medicine.</note> or water and vinegar in which lemon balm <note>original: *melissa*</note> has been steeped; let it boil with figs and raisins, and let the asthmatic person use that liquid.

### *Against blockage of the lungs and against frequent groaning.*

Let saltpeter be drunk in barley water <note>original: *ptisana*</note>.

### *For sluggish humors of the stomach, for flatulence, and pains of the intestines.*

One drachm <note>A unit of weight, roughly 3.9 grams.</note> of saltpeter eaten with rose honey purges the waste of the stomach and stimulates the appetite.

### *For "suffocation" of the stomach.*

Let saltpeter be drunk with sweet benzoin <note>original: *asa dulci*; likely a fragrant resin similar to laserpitium, used to treat digestive distress</note>, or *posca*, or warm water with vinegar and salt.

->Or.<-

Let almond milk be prepared with a decoction of saltpeter, chamomile flowers <note>original: *momillae*, a variation of *chamomilla*</note>, violets, borage, bugloss, lemon balm, mint, rose leaves, and sweet benzoin.

### *For stomach cramps.*

Saltpeter and lemon balm drunk in warmed wine soothes the torments <note>original: *tormina*; sharp, twisting intestinal pains</note> of the stomach.

### *For blockage of the liver.*

Let a decoction be made from chicory, endive, dandelion <note>original: *dente leonis*</note>, and red roses; let saltpeter be added. Likewise, let a plaster be made from saltpeter and oil of bitter almonds, rose oil, and rose vinegar in which glowing steel has been quenched <note>original: *chalybs ignitus extinctus fuit*; quenching hot metal in liquids was believed to transfer the "strength" of the iron to the medicine</note>; let it be applied to the region of the liver.

Likewise, let enemas <note>original: *clysteres*</note> be prepared from the same decoctions, with oil of bitter almonds, chamomile, rose honey, and saltpeter.

### *Against a hardened and swollen spleen.*

Let saltpeter, fenugreek, red roses, and capers be dissolved in oxymel <term>oxymel</term> <note>original: *oxymelle*; a medicinal syrup made of honey and vinegar.</note> and rose vinegar in which red-hot steel has been quenched; let it be drunk on an empty stomach.

### *A plaster for the same.*

Take 5 ounces of saltpeter, powdered fenugreek or lupins, omphacine rose vinegar <note>original: *aceti rosati omphacini*; vinegar made from rose petals and unripe grapes or olives</note>, oil of bitter almonds, chamomile oil, dill <note>original: *anethi*</note>, elder, and caper roots, 1 ounce of each; let it be made into a plaster.
